01-01.title: Darfur conflict (ongoing genocide and humanitarian crisis)
01-01.description: Armed conflict between government-aligned Janjaweed militias and rebel groups continued across Darfur throughout 2006, marked by attacks on civilians, mass displacement and a severe humanitarian crisis. A September 2006 study published in the journal Science estimated at least 200,000 deaths since the conflict began in 2003, with estimates up to 300,000-400,000 cited by the UN Secretary-General and other organizations, most deaths resulting from violence, disease and starvation. The Darfur Peace Agreement signed in May 2006 failed to end the fighting, and more than two million people remained displaced.

review.note: Science publication date is September 15, 2006, not an event onset. Its mortality estimate is cumulative since 2003 and would overlap earlier Darfur records; January 1,2006 is unsupported as a specific event date. Primary study and GAO discuss uncertainty; do not treat 200,000 as additional deaths during 2006.

sources.name: Hagan and Palloni, Death in Darfur

01-01.title: Iraq War (2007)
01-01.description: Iraq Body Count's current database records 26,112 civilian deaths from violence during calendar year 2007. This full-year total includes separately recorded attacks and is not a death count for January 1.

review.note: 26,112 matches current IBC annual database, not January1 deaths. January1 is an annual-index placeholder and cannot be verified as a discrete event date. Remove unsupported causal assertion linking annual deaths to surge and military-death comparison; annual total overlaps individual attacks.

sources.name: Iraq Body Count current annual database

01-01.title: Kenya post-election violence
01-01.description: Violence followed Kenya's disputed December 2007 election and continued into February 2008. The Waki commission recorded 1,133 deaths during its December 27, 2007-February 29, 2008 assessment period. The toll includes killings across multiple provinces, not one January 1 incident.

review.note: Waki commission supports1,133 deaths in the December27-February29 inquiry period. January1 is not the onset; reported first violence, declaration and inquiry dates differ. Correct toll/geographic scope, but do not replace uncertain onset with another unqualified date. Mediation was African Union-led, not simply UN-brokered.

01-01.title: Afghanistan conflict — 2012
01-01.description: UNAMA documented 2,769 civilian deaths and 4,821 injuries in Afghanistan during 2012, making it the first year of decline since UN casualty tracking began, though the toll remained among the highest of the war; several thousand Afghan security forces, international troops (about 400 coalition deaths) and insurgents were also killed. 2012 saw a record spike in insider 'green-on-blue' attacks on coalition personnel.

review.note: UNAMA retrospective confirms annual 2,769 civilian deaths/4,821 injuries. January 1 is a calendar-period anchor, not a dated incident. Coalition/insurgent fatalities, first-decline and insider-attack record claims need separate evidence; no full-record verification. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

01-01.title: Jakarta flood disaster
01-01.description: Record rainfall of nearly 400 mm on New Year's Eve overflowed the Ciliwung and Cisadane rivers, flooding large parts of Jakarta and surrounding areas in the early hours of 1 January 2020. Officials reported 66 deaths, the highest toll from flooding in the city since 2007, with about 60,000 people displaced and more than 397,000 evacuated to higher ground at the peak. Water levels reached 30 to 200 cm across many districts and up to four metres in parts of East Jakarta.

review.note: 377 mm daily rainfall and 397,171 displaced reported. Exact onset requires UTC conversion: early January 1 local is December 31 UTC. No primary final 66-death tally, 60,000 residual-displacement cutoff or full water-depth/rivers support retrieved. Retain unresolved rather than selecting an arbitrary onset time.

01-01.title: Somalia drought: estimated excess deaths in 2022
01-01.description: A study commissioned by WHO and UNICEF and released in March 2023 estimated approximately 43,000 excess deaths associated with Somalia's drought during January-December 2022, about half among children younger than five. January 1 marks the start of the study year, not the date these deaths occurred; the total is an estimate rather than a confirmed count.

review.note: 43,000 is modeled excess mortality in Somalia across all 2022, not a January 1 event or Horn-wide confirmed famine toll. Commissioned by WHO/UNICEF, with FAO support; no area-level famine declaration implied. January 1 is a study-year boundary, not an established discrete disaster date. The annual mortality estimate is supported, but the current calendar record needs a justified period representation before publication.

01-01.title: Noto Peninsula Earthquake
01-01.description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck the Noto Peninsula in Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan, on January 1, 2024, triggering tsunami warnings, building collapses, and a major fire in Wajima. The disaster killed 241 people, injured more than 1,300, and destroyed or damaged tens of thousands of homes, with Wajima and Suzu among the hardest-hit towns.

review.note: January 1 and magnitude 7.6 JMA are established, but 241 is an early 2024 snapshot, not the final toll. An indexed August 14, 2026 Kyodo report gives 750 across affected prefectures: 228 direct plus 522 related deaths; its full page failed to open. Need the current official table and explicit national/prefectural and direct/indirect scope before replacing the toll. Withhold rather than silently freeze an obsolete count.

sources.name: International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction

01-01.title: New Orleans Bourbon Street truck attack
01-01.description: On January 1, 2025, Shamsud-Din Jabbar drove a pickup truck into crowds celebrating New Year on Bourbon Street, then opened fire, killing 14 people and injuring dozens before being fatally shot by police. The FBI classified the attack as a terrorist act inspired by the Islamic State, to which Jabbar pledged allegiance in videos posted before the attack.

01-03.title: Baga massacre by Boko Haram
01-03.description: Boko Haram attacked Baga and Doron Baga in early January 2015, beginning on January 3. Satellite imagery showed widespread destruction, and witnesses described mass killings. Reported tolls ranged from an official figure around 150, including fighters, to local estimates as high as 2,000; the final number remains uncertain.

review.note: 2,000 was an upper estimate from local accounts, not a confirmed Amnesty body count; government put deaths including fighters at about 150. Satellite destruction cannot by itself resolve deaths. January 3 is campaign start, not a single-day total.

sources.name: Amnesty International, satellite and witness evidence

01-03.title: Kerman Bombings (Soleimani Memorial Attack)
01-03.description: On January 3, 2024, two explosions struck a crowd gathered in Kerman, Iran, for a ceremony commemorating the fourth anniversary of the assassination of General Qasem Soleimani. Islamic State (ISIS) claimed responsibility for the attack, which killed at least 95 people and wounded about 280, making it one of the deadliest attacks in Iran's modern history.

review.note: Date and memorial identity are established. Early 103/95 counts were corrected to 84, then 94 by January 11; a definitive subsequent 95-person count was not established. ISIS claim is supported, but final toll requires reconciliation. The Al Jazeera evidence is used only for the later figure and claim.

01-05.title: Tel Aviv Central Bus Station double suicide bombing
01-05.description: Two suicide bombers attacked near Tel Aviv's old central bus station on January 5, 2003, killing 23 people, including eight foreign nationals, and injuring more than 100. The al-Aqsa Martyrs Brigade claimed responsibility.

01-05.title: Iraq civilian deaths in 2012 (annual total)
01-05.description: Iraq Body Count recorded 4,622 civilian deaths from violence across Iraq during calendar year 2012, up from 4,162 in 2011. This is a full-year aggregate, not a toll for a single incident.

review.note: IBC supports the full-year 4,622 total, not the original rounded 4,600. Neither January 5 nor an invented December 31 substitute is a verified incident date for this annual aggregate. Retain the original identity in quarantine and withhold from the dated public event dataset pending an appropriate period representation. The supported title/toll/prose corrections do not solve the date blocker.

01-07.title: Charlie Hebdo shooting
01-07.description: Gunmen attacked Charlie Hebdo's Paris office on January 7, 2015, killing 12 people, including journalists and police officers. The Kouachi brothers were killed by police two days later. Separate linked attacks killed five more people, bringing the January 7-9 victim total to 17.
sources: Committee to Protect Journalists, attack report

01-07.title: Los Angeles wildfires (Palisades and Eaton fires)
01-07.description: The Palisades and Eaton fires began in Los Angeles County on January 7, 2025 local time and were contained on January 31. CAL FIRE records 31 civilian deaths and 16,264 destroyed structures across the two fires.

01-08.title: Tucson mass shooting targeting Rep. Gabrielle Giffords
01-08.description: A gunman attacked Representative Gabrielle Giffords's constituent event in Tucson, Arizona, on January 8, 2011, killing six people and injuring 13, including Giffords. Jared Lee Loughner pleaded guilty to federal charges and in November 2012 was sentenced to life imprisonment without release.

01-09.title: Chinagodrar military camp attack
01-09.description: Militants attacked Niger's military post at Chinagodrar near the Mali border on January 9, 2020. Reuters subsequently reported that at least 89 Nigerien soldiers were killed. French fighter jets were sent to help repel the attackers.

01-10.title: China winter storms (2008 Chinese snowstorms)
01-10.description: A series of snow, freezing-rain and severe-cold episodes affected southern and central China beginning January 10, 2008, disrupting electricity and transport. The Asian Disaster Reduction Center's subsequent summary records 129 deaths across 20 provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities.

01-12.title: Haiti Earthquake
01-12.description: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck near Port-au-Prince, Haiti, on January 12, 2010, devastating the capital and surrounding areas. PAHO and UN accounts report an estimated 220,000 deaths and about 300,000 injuries.

01-13.title: El Salvador Earthquake
01-13.description: An earthquake struck off El Salvador on 13 January 2001 at 17:33 UTC. USGS strong-motion documentation gives magnitude Mw 7.6. Official impact figures cited in a subsequent technical report were 944 deaths and 5,565 injuries, with more than 100,000 houses destroyed. Landslides caused extensive loss of life, including in Santa Tecla.

01-14.title: Sulawesi earthquake
01-14.description: A magnitude 6.2 earthquake struck near the city of Mamuju on Sulawesi island, killing at least 105 people and injuring hundreds more. The quake toppled homes, hospitals, and hotels, triggering landslides in the mountainous region. Thousands were displaced and months of aftershocks hampered rescue and recovery efforts.

review.note: UTC origin is January 14 at 18:28, not January 15. 105 appears in secondary summaries; months of aftershocks hampering rescue is not established. Propose only supported UTC correction pending full final-toll and recovery evidence.

01-15.title: DusitD2 complex attack
01-15.description: Al-Shabaab attacked the DusitD2 hotel and business complex in Nairobi on January 15, 2019. Twenty-one victims were killed. Kenyan authorities said all five attackers also died. The toll of 21 excludes the attackers.

01-15.title: Yeti Airlines Flight 691 crash
01-15.description: Yeti Airlines Flight 691, an ATR 72-500 flying from Kathmandu, crashed on approach to Pokhara on January 15, 2023, killing all 68 passengers and four crew. Nepal's final investigation identified inadvertent movement of both condition levers to the feathered position as the most probable cause, resulting in loss of thrust, an aerodynamic stall and ground impact.

01-16.title: Mustansiriya University bombing
01-16.description: Bombing attacks near Mustansiriya University in Baghdad on January 16, 2007, killed about 70 people, many of them students, according to UNAMI. Numerous others were injured.

01-17.title: Mount Nyiragongo eruption
01-17.location: Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo
01-17.description: Nyiragongo erupted on January 17, 2002, sending lava through Goma and causing mass evacuation. A Smithsonian report records conflicting mortality assessments: 147 deaths reported by the UN and about 70 estimated by a subsequent medical field investigation. Both include deaths in a petrol-station explosion on January 21.

review.note: The original 100 is not established as an enumerated toll. The Smithsonian report explicitly contrasts a UN count of 147, including 60-100 petrol-station deaths, with Peter Baxter's field assessment of about 70 total and about 20 at the petrol station. This is a substantive contradiction within the same source, not resolved by attribution alone. The proposed 147 is only a documented alternative and must not be published as settled.

01-17.title: Gul Plaza shopping mall fire
01-17.description: A fire broke out at the Gul Plaza shopping centre in Karachi on the night of 17 January 2026. Pakistan's National Disaster Management Authority subsequently reported at least 80 deaths and dozens of injuries; an earlier inquiry report counted 79 deaths. The fire spread through the multistorey commercial building.

01-18.title: Gaza War (Operation Cast Lead)
01-18.description: Israel's military offensive against Hamas in the Gaza Strip ran from December 27, 2008, to a ceasefire on January 18, 2009. Human rights organizations and UN agencies documented approximately 1,340-1,400 Palestinians killed, including around 750-770 civilians and more than 300 children, with over 5,000 wounded. Thirteen Israelis were killed, including 3 civilians. The offensive included heavy air strikes and ground operations and caused extensive destruction of homes, schools, and infrastructure across Gaza.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
Al Mezan Centre for Human Rights

review.note: Campaign dates corroborated. B'Tselem snapshots give 1,387 and 1,385 Palestinian deaths, not a final exact 1,400. The numeric field does not specify whether the 13 Israeli deaths are included. Civilian definitions differ; 5,000 wounded and infrastructure claims need their own evidence.

01-18.title: Nigeria fuel tanker explosion in Suleja
01-18.description: A fuel tanker accident and explosion at Dikko junction in Niger State on January 18, 2025 killed people gathered around spilled fuel. NEMA reported 98 deaths and 69 injuries in its January 28 update.

01-19.title: Gaza war ceasefire
01-19.description: A ceasefire between Israel and Hamas took effect on January 19, 2025, after 15 months of war in which the Gaza Health Ministry reported more than 47,000 Palestinians killed and most of the territory's population displaced. The first phase of the agreement included releases of hostages and prisoners before hostilities later resumed.

review.note: OCHA establishes that the ceasefire took effect January 19 at 11:15 local time, not its January 22 publication date, and reports hostage/prisoner releases. The 47,000 is a cumulative war toll, not deaths caused by a ceasefire; an exact matching January 19 cutoff is not established here. This overlaps the existing 2023 and 2024 Gaza death records. A later cumulative report cannot verify the number on the ceasefire date. Do not publish a deaths-bearing ceasefire row until its toll scope and duplicate treatment are resolved.

01-20.title: Kano bombings
01-20.description: Boko Haram carried out coordinated bombings and shootings in Kano on January 20, 2012. Authorities reported 185 deaths, including about 150 civilians, 29 police officers and three state-security officers. Targets included police, state-security and immigration facilities.

01-22.title: Monterey Park mass shooting
01-22.description: A gunman attacked Star Ballroom Dance Studio in Monterey Park late on January 21, 2023 local time, January 22 UTC, killing eleven people and wounding nine. The attack occurred during Lunar New Year celebrations. He subsequently entered another dance hall in Alhambra, where he was disarmed, and later died by suicide.

01-22.title: Antioch High School shooting
01-22.description: On January 22, 2025, 17-year-old Solomon Henderson shot and killed one student and wounded another in the Antioch High School cafeteria in Nashville, then died by suicide. Police reported ten shots within 17 seconds.

01-23.title: West Bandung landslide
01-23.location: West Bandung Regency, West Java, Indonesia
01-23.description: Heavy rain triggered a landslide in Pasirlangu village, West Bandung Regency, at about 02:30 local time on 24 January 2026 (23 January UTC), burying homes. By 10 February, West Java police had identified 80 victims. Identification of additional remains was continuing.

01-24.title: Domodedovo International Airport suicide bombing
01-24.description: A suicide bombing at Moscow's Domodedovo Airport on January 24, 2011, killed 37 people and injured more than 170. Insurgent leader Doku Umarov claimed responsibility. Three accomplices received life sentences in 2013.

01-25.title: Egyptian Revolution of 2011
01-25.description: Mass protests against the rule of President Hosni Mubarak began across Egypt on January 25, 2011, and continued for 18 days until Mubarak's resignation on February 11. Security forces used live ammunition, tear gas and beatings against demonstrators, primarily in Cairo's Tahrir Square and other cities. Egypt's official fact-finding commission reported that 846 people were killed and 6,467 injured during the uprising, which it determined involved unlawful police use of lethal force against protesters.

01-25.title: Brumadinho dam disaster
01-25.description: Vale's Corrego do Feijao tailings dam collapsed at Brumadinho, Brazil, on January 25, 2019, killing 270 people. Local authorities and victims' families commemorate 272 victims when two unborn children are included. Identification and recovery of victims continued for years after the collapse.

01-26.title: Gujarat (Bhuj) Earthquake
01-26.description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck Gujarat near Bhuj on 26 January 2001 at 03:16 UTC, India's Republic Day. USGS reports at least 20,000 fatalities, 166,836 injuries and nearly a million buildings damaged or destroyed.

01-27.title: Kiss nightclub fire
01-27.description: A fire at the Kiss nightclub in Santa Maria, Brazil, began early on January 27, 2013, after a band's pyrotechnics ignited ceiling foam. It killed 242 people and injured at least 636; toxic smoke and evacuation failures contributed to the disaster.

review.note: The commission records 242 deaths and at least 636 injured, with a 02:30 local start on January 27 (same UTC date). Replace unsupported stampede causation and historical ranking with documented facts. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

01-27.title: Kabul ambulance bombing
01-27.description: On January 27, 2018, a Taliban attacker detonated explosives carried in an ambulance in central Kabul. Afghanistan's interior minister reported the next day that 103 people had been killed and 235 wounded.

01-27.title: M23 capture of Goma
01-27.location: Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo
01-27.description: Between January 23 and 30, 2025, Rwandan-backed M23 rebels captured Goma, the capital of North Kivu province in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, after heavy fighting against the national army, UN and SADC peacekeepers, and allied militias; the UN estimated about 2,900 people were killed and another 2,900 wounded, with hundreds of thousands displaced.

review.note: The February 5 UN briefing, reproduced by ANSA, supports a provisional 2,900 dead: 2,000 bodies collected from streets and 900 in morgues. This is not a final January 23-30-only total. UNICEF describes January 26-28 fighting and control of most of Goma by January 28; the January 27 UN briefing describes an ongoing battle, while the later experts' annex calls January 27 full conquest. The same report also cites narrower health-facility fatality/injury counts. The exact capture-date framing and matching casualty period remain unsettled; do not silently resolve them with publication dates.

01-28.title: Rubaya coltan mine collapse
01-28.location: Rubaya, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo
01-28.description: Heavy rain caused a landslide and mine collapses at the Rubaya coltan mining complex in North Kivu on 28 January 2026. Rebel-appointed authorities reported at least 200 deaths. A civil-society representative subsequently estimated roughly 400 deaths; that higher figure remained provisional and was not limited to miners.

review.note: The roughly 400 figure is a provisional civil-society estimate, not a confirmed count of miners alone; AP reported at least 200. March 3 is supported by Reuters (published March 4), but that separate collapse has a disputed toll and should not be folded into January's deaths. Exact January onset time unavailable. The numeric field still reflects a provisional estimate; a confirmed comparable toll and January UTC onset remain unresolved.

01-29.title: Unity oilfield plane crash
01-29.description: On January 29, 2025, a Beechcraft 1900D operated by Eagle Air on behalf of Light Air Services crashed shortly after takeoff from the Unity oilfield airstrip in Unity State, South Sudan, while carrying oil workers to Juba; 20 of the 21 people on board were killed.

01-29.title: Balochistan Liberation Army attacks
01-29.description: Between 29 January and 5 February 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Army launched a coordinated series of attacks across Balochistan province, Pakistan, including raids on a police station and banks in Kharan, a security post in Panjgur and military positions in Harnai. The week-long campaign left at least 225 people dead, including 36 civilians and 2 security personnel, while Pakistani forces reported killing 216 militants in retaliatory raids.

review.note: January 29 is the military operation's beginning, not the coordinated BLA assault (January 31). The reported components are 216 militants, 36 civilians and 22 security personnel = 274, not 225; all are military-reported, not independently confirmed. The original identity key is retained for audit only. The proposed scope is a multi-day campaign, not a proven single-day BLA attack. Its start date must not be presented as the date of all 274 deaths; assault versus military-operation allocation remains unresolved.

01-30.title: Peshawar mosque bombing
01-30.description: A suicide bombing inside the Police Lines mosque in Peshawar on January 30, 2023 killed 84 people in the revised police count, mostly police personnel. A TTP commander claimed responsibility, but the group's spokesman denied involvement. Pakistani investigators later attributed the attack to Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, a TTP faction.

01-30.title: Potomac River mid-air collision (American Airlines Flight 5342)
01-30.description: At about 01:48 UTC on January 30, 2025 (the evening of January 29 locally), PSA Airlines Flight 5342 and a US Army UH-60L helicopter collided near Reagan Washington National Airport and fell into the Potomac River. All 64 people on the airliner and three helicopter crew members died.

02-01.title: Myanmar military coup and crackdown
02-01.description: On February 1, the Myanmar military seized power in a coup, detaining elected leader Aung San Suu Kyi and triggering nationwide civil disobedience and protests. Security forces responded with lethal force, and by the end of 2021 more than 1,400 civilians had been killed and over 10,000 detained, according to monitoring groups such as the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners.

review.note: Primary December 6 briefing reports 1,303 killed and 7,796 currently detained. Year-end more-than-1,400 and over-10,000 need December 31 evidence and a distinction between all arrested and still detained. These are cumulative post-coup deaths, not February 1 deaths. Only one source was established in this batch, below the two-source publication minimum.

02-02.title: Central Chile Wildfires
02-02.location: Viña del Mar, Valparaíso Region, Chile
02-02.description: Wildfires beginning on February 2, 2024 devastated communities around Vina del Mar in Chile's Valparaiso Region. Prosecutors later confirmed 138 deaths, including later fatalities, superseding lower early totals. Thousands of homes were damaged or destroyed.

02-03.title: al-Sadriya market bombing
02-03.description: A suicide truck bomb struck Baghdad's Sadriya market on February 3, 2007. Contemporary reports and an FBI retrospective give at least 135 deaths, while Iraq Body Count's current incident record gives 136-137.

review.note: Wrong market: Sadriya, not Shorja. FBI retrospective records135; current IBC136-137. Date and afternoon timing secure, but exact mortality not reconciled. Correct identity without treating conflicting final counts as settled.

02-03.title: Somalia famine — 2011-2012 crisis
02-03.description: A UN-declared famine that began in July 2011 in southern Somalia was declared over on 3 February 2012. A joint FSNAU/FEWS NET mortality study attributed about 258,000 excess deaths to the famine between October 2010 and April 2012, roughly half of them children under five, driven by drought, conflict, and obstruction of humanitarian access.

review.note: February 3 is the famine-classification ending announcement, not a separate fatal event. The same October 2010-April 2012 estimated 258,000 excess deaths are already represented by the July 20, 2011 entry. Recommend merging/removing this duplicate from mortality totals; no field-only replacement can prevent double counting.

02-03.title: Kwara State attacks
02-03.description: Armed extremists attacked Woro and Nuku in Kaiama, Kwara State, on the evening of 3 February 2026. Local officials and the Red Cross reported at least 162 deaths, while the state government initially gave a lower count. Homes were burned and residents abducted. Reports differed over the attackers' affiliation, and no group immediately claimed responsibility.

02-05.title: Novye Aldi massacre
02-05.description: Russian OMON police conducted a house-to-house purge of the Novye Aldi suburb of Grozny, summarily executing at least 62 civilians. The European Court of Human Rights later ruled Russia responsible.

02-05.title: Meinong (Kaohsiung) earthquake
02-05.description: An earthquake centred near Meinong in southern Taiwan struck at 19:57 UTC on February 5, 2016, or early February 6 locally. It caused severe building collapses in Tainan. Taiwan's Central Weather Administration records 117 deaths.
sources: Taiwan Central Weather Administration, event record
National Center for Research on Earthquake Engineering, study

02-06.title: Turkey–Syria earthquake
02-06.description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck near the Turkey–Syria border at 4:17 a.m., followed by a magnitude 7.5 aftershock hours later, collapsing thousands of buildings across southeastern Turkey and northern Syria. More than 59,000 people were confirmed dead, including about 50,700 in Turkey and over 5,900 in Syria, with an estimated 1.5 million people left homeless. It was one of the deadliest earthquakes in the region in modern history, compounded in Syria by the country's ongoing civil war.

review.note: February 6 UTC is correct, but original country subtotals do not sum to 59,000. EEFIT gives 62,013 (53,537 Turkey plus 8,476 Syria); secondary compilation also records a lower Syrian count of 5,951. A defensible harmonized cross-border confirmed total and cutoff remain unresolved. Avoid selecting one exact total without reconciling Syrian coverage; 04:17 is local, 01:17 UTC.

02-06.title: Islamabad mosque suicide bombing
02-06.description: An attacker opened fire at the gates of the Khadija Tul Kubra Shia mosque in Islamabad's Tarlai area during Friday prayers on 6 February 2026 before detonating explosives. The death toll subsequently rose to 36. More than 100 people were injured. Islamic State claimed responsibility.

02-07.title: Chamoli rock and ice avalanche
02-07.description: A massive rock and ice avalanche from Ronti Peak caused the Chamoli disaster in Uttarakhand on February 7, 2021. Debris swept down the Rishiganga and Dhauliganga valleys and damaged two hydropower projects. Roughly 200 people were killed or remained missing; this is a combined dead-and-missing estimate.

review.note: Scientific reconstruction identifies rock and glacier ice from Ronti Peak, not simply Nanda Devi glacier breaking off. About 200 is dead-and-missing, not 200 recovered/confirmed bodies. A combined killed-or-missing estimate cannot establish 200 deaths for the lives_lost field. Retain the supported avalanche mechanism but withhold until a death-only or legally presumed-dead count is supported.

sources.name: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences

02-08.title: Nakhon Ratchasima (Korat) mall shooting
02-08.description: On February 8-9, 2020, a Thai soldier killed 29 people in a rampage in Nakhon Ratchasima that included a military base and Terminal 21 shopping mall. He was killed by security forces after an overnight siege, bringing the total including the attacker to 30. It was Thailand's deadliest mass shooting at the time.

02-10.title: Tumbler Ridge school shooting
02-10.description: An 18-year-old former student killed eight people in Tumbler Ridge on 10 February 2026: her mother and 11-year-old brother at a home, and five students and a teacher at the secondary school. The perpetrator also died by suicide, bringing the total dead to nine. Twenty-seven people were reported injured.

02-13.title: Second El Salvador Earthquake
02-13.description: A magnitude 6.6 earthquake struck the San Vicente region of El Salvador on 13 February 2001 at 14:22 UTC, one month after the January disaster. It killed 315 people and caused further destructive landslides and building collapses.

02-13.title: Texas winter-weather disaster, February 2021
02-13.description: Severe winter weather and power failures left millions of Texans without essential services in February 2021. Texas health officials ultimately identified 246 storm-related deaths, including 158 from hypothermia. The total covers deaths from February 11 through June 4, including later deaths linked to the disaster, rather than deaths on February 13 alone.

review.note: 246 is the state's broad February winter-storm total, including deaths through June and multiple weather episodes; not necessarily all caused by a single storm starting February 13. 158 hypothermia deaths supported. The broader February winter-weather total is supported, but February 13 is not established as the start date of that matched scope. A specific storm-name/date cannot silently stand in for several weather episodes.

sources.name: Texas Department of State Health Services

02-14.title: Sunjiawan coal mine explosion
02-14.description: A gas explosion at the Sunjiawan coal mine's Haizhou shaft in Fuxin, Liaoning, on February 14, 2005, killed 214 people and injured 30, according to the official investigation.
sources: China Ministry of Emergency Management investigation

02-14.title: Parkland School Shooting
02-14.description: On February 14, 2018, a gunman killed 17 people and wounded 17 others at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida.

02-14.title: Pulwama attack
02-14.description: A Jaish-e-Mohammed suicide bomber attacked a convoy of Indian paramilitary police in Pulwama on February 14, 2019, killing 40 security personnel. The attack was followed by Indian airstrikes at Balakot and an aerial confrontation between India and Pakistan.

02-15.title: Libyan civil war and NATO intervention
02-15.description: Anti-government protests erupted in Benghazi on February 15, 2011, and escalated into a nationwide armed rebellion against the rule of Muammar Gaddafi. A UN-mandated NATO bombing campaign began in March, and fighting continued until the fall of Tripoli in August and Gaddafi's capture and killing on October 20, 2011. Estimates of the conflict's death toll range from about 20,000 to 30,000; a 2013 statistical study published by The New York Times estimated approximately 25,000 killed during the eight-month conflict, including thousands of civilians.

review.note: 25,000 appears as a 2011 officials' estimate, not a located 2013 NYT statistical study. Later government research gave lower, incomplete faction-specific totals. Claimed study attribution is unestablished; no defensible replacement all-conflict integer obtained. NATO takeover and initial coalition intervention should also be distinguished.

02-15.title: Petropolis floods and mudslides
02-15.description: Extreme rainfall caused catastrophic flooding and landslides in Petropolis, Brazil, on February 15, 2022. More than 250 mm fell within hours. A later disaster study recorded 233 deaths, the highest toll for a disaster in the city's history.

02-16.title: Quetta Hazara market bombing
02-16.description: A remote-controlled bomb struck a market in Hazara Town, Quetta, in February 2013, targeting the Shia Hazara community. Lashkar-e-Jhangvi claimed responsibility. Reports placed the death toll at at least 84, with later and contemporary accounts differing on the total.

review.note: Remote detonation contradicts the suicide-bomber claim. Contemporary reporting dates the attack February 16; HRW's retrospective says February 17 and at least 84 deaths, while SRW reports 89. Final toll needs reconciliation; do not silently replace it with an unattributed exact number.

sources.name: Human Rights Watch, Hazara killings report

02-17.title: Southern Leyte mudslide buries Guinsaugon village
02-17.description: A major landslide buried Guinsaugon village in Saint Bernard, Southern Leyte, on February 17, 2006, after prolonged heavy rain. Homes and an elementary school were buried. IFRC's subsequent report records 1,126 deaths.
sources: Center for Excellence in Disaster Management

02-17.title: Kandahar dog-fighting show suicide bombing
02-17.description: A suicide bombing struck a crowd watching a dog-fighting competition near Kandahar on February 17, 2008. A local police commander was among those killed. UNAMA recorded 67 civilian deaths, while provincial reporting gave a higher overall toll.

review.note: UNAMA annual report records67 civilian deaths; governor's contemporary account reports over100 overall. Armed police/guards may explain some difference but no reconciled breakdown was obtained.100 is not an exact count when source says over100. Date and gathering supported; attribution/ranking can be omitted but mortality remains core blocker.

02-18.title: Daegu subway fire
02-18.description: An arson attack aboard a train at Jungangno station in Daegu spread to a second train on February 18, 2003. The fire killed 192 people and injured more than 140. Combustible interiors, smoke and failures in the evacuation response contributed to the disaster.

02-18.title: Samjhauta Express bombing
02-18.description: Bombs and fire struck two coaches of the Samjhauta Express near Panipat shortly before midnight on February 18, 2007. Later court reporting records 68 people killed, most of them Pakistani nationals.

02-19.title: Iran Ilyushin Il-76 military plane crash
02-19.description: An Iranian Revolutionary Guards Ilyushin Il-76 flying from Zahedan to Kerman struck Mount Sirach during its approach in poor weather on February 19, 2003. All 275 occupants died. The Bureau of Aircraft Accidents Archives describes a premature descent below the minimum descent altitude in poor visibility.

02-19.title: Pasta de Conchos coal mine explosion
02-19.description: A disaster at the Pasta de Conchos coal mine in Coahuila on February 19, 2006, killed 65 miners. Only two bodies were recovered during the earlier recovery efforts, leaving families campaigning for the recovery of the remaining victims. Renewed recovery operations later located additional remains.

02-19.title: Hanau far-right shootings
02-19.description: On February 19, 2020, a racist attacker killed nine people of immigrant backgrounds at sites in Hanau, Germany. He also killed his mother and died by suicide. Ten victims were killed; the perpetrator's death is excluded from this count. Authorities treated the attack as far-right terrorism.

02-20.title: South Sudan famine declared
02-20.description: Famine was declared in South Sudan's Leer and Mayendit counties on February 20, 2017. UN agencies reported about 100,000 people facing starvation and one million more on the brink of famine. Famine conditions eased by June following increased assistance, while severe food insecurity persisted.

review.note: February 20 is the supported declaration date, not famine onset. UN sources substantiate Leer/Mayendit, roughly 100,000 facing starvation, 4.9 million severely food insecure and one million near famine; June 21 reports famine easing but worsening nationwide hunger. They do not establish an event-specific 20,000 excess-death estimate. Famine classification mortality thresholds cannot be converted into that annual toll.

sources.name: UN Secretary-General report on South Sudan

02-21.title: Kaduna religious riots
02-21.description: Christian-Muslim violence broke out in Kaduna on 21 February 2000 during a protest against proposed Sharia legislation. A state judicial commission reported at least 1,295 deaths in the February violence. Later violence in May is excluded from that count; people interviewed by Human Rights Watch believed the total across the 2000 riots was substantially higher.

02-21.title: The Station nightclub fire
02-21.location: West Warwick, Rhode Island, United States
02-21.description: Pyrotechnics ignited polyurethane foam during a concert at The Station nightclub in West Warwick late on February 20 local time, February 21 UTC. The rapidly spreading fire killed 100 people and injured more than 200.

02-21.title: Christchurch earthquake
02-21.description: An earthquake struck Christchurch and surrounding Canterbury at 12:51 p.m. local time on February 22, 2011 (23:51 UTC February 21), causing widespread building collapses and damage. New Zealand Police records 185 deaths. Thousands of people were injured.

02-22.title: Mozambique floods and Cyclone Eline
02-22.description: Cyclone Eline worsened severe flooding already affecting Mozambique in February 2000. The wider flood and cyclone emergency killed about 700 people and affected about two million; these are cumulative emergency totals, not deaths or displacement on the landfall date alone.

02-22.title: Zarand earthquake
02-22.description: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck near Zarand in Kerman Province, Iran, levelling several mud-brick mountain villages and killing 612 people. An estimated 80,000 people were affected and more than 900 were injured.

review.note: USGS supports Mw 6.4 and February 22. Summary attributes 612 deaths to PAGER-CAT but also reports an independent ISNA count of 799. Need source-level resolution of mortality scope and the 80,000 affected/900 injured figures before full verification.

02-22.title: Al-Askari shrine bombing triggers sectarian violence
02-22.description: Bombers dressed as security personnel detonated explosives inside the al-Askari shrine in Samarra on February 22, 2006, destroying the golden dome of one of Shia Islam's holiest sites. The blast itself killed no one, but it triggered waves of retaliatory sectarian killings across Iraq, with more than 1,000 people dead within days and hundreds of mosques attacked; leaked U.S. military documents later indicated the death toll exceeded 3,000, and the bombing is widely regarded as having ignited Iraq's civil war.

review.note: Shrine blast itself killed nobody. Subsequent1000/1300/3000 estimates refer to different periods/areas and cannot become a single Samarra bombing toll; they also overlap annual Iraq record. Need a bounded reprisal-event definition. Do not fabricate a positive bombing death count to satisfy schema.

02-22.title: Iraq sectarian civil war (deadliest year of the conflict)
02-22.description: Sectarian violence intensified in Iraq in 2006. Iraq Body Count's current database records 29,526 civilian deaths from violence during the full calendar year. This annual total includes numerous separately recorded attacks and is not the toll of the February 22 shrine bombing.
sources: United Nations Assistance Mission for Iraq (UNAMI)

review.note: IBC current annual table gives29,526 for all2006; February22 indexes a catalyst, not the start of that count. January-February deaths and other discrete events overlap. UNAMI uses a different methodology, not simply matching IBC. Annual/single-event schema and double counting must be resolved.

02-24.title: Bogoro massacre
02-24.location: Bogoro, Ituri, Democratic Republic of the Congo
02-24.description: FNI and FRPI fighters attacked Bogoro in Ituri on February 24, 2003, killing at least 200 civilians. The International Criminal Court convicted Germain Katanga in connection with the attack in 2014; Mathieu Ngudjolo Chui was acquitted in 2012.

02-24.title: Al Hoceima earthquake
02-24.description: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck near Al Hoceima in northern Morocco on February 24, 2004. A subsequent regional support committee report recorded 628 deaths and 926 injuries. Thousands of homes were destroyed and more than 15,000 people displaced.

review.note: USGS gives Mw 6.4, not 6.5. ADRC preserves the March official count of 628 and 926 injured; another reference gives 631, so attribute 628 to that report rather than call it an uncontested final toll. UTC earthquake date is February 24. The later 631 figure is not reconciled with the March snapshot; changing the prose's attribution alone does not establish final mortality. Withhold pending that reconciliation.

02-24.title: Russian Invasion of Ukraine — Start of Full-Scale War
02-24.description: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the largest conventional military attack in Europe since World War II. Tens of thousands of civilians and soldiers have been killed, and millions displaced.

review.note: Full-scale invasion began February 24, not March 24. Duplicates original February 24 invasion record. 100,000 lacks date, civilian/military definition and source; possible confusion of casualties with deaths. Merge/remove decision belongs to maintainer; do not apply date correction without duplicate review.

02-24.title: Russian invasion of Ukraine
02-24.description: Russia began its full-scale invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022. By early January 2023, UN human rights monitors had verified at least 6,919 civilian deaths since the invasion, while warning the actual toll was higher. This is a dated cumulative civilian count and excludes military deaths; it is not a count of deaths on February 24.

02-25.title: Severnaya coal mine explosions, Vorkuta
02-25.description: Methane explosions at the Severnaya mine in Vorkuta on February 25, 2016 killed four miners and trapped 26 others, who were subsequently presumed dead. A third explosion on February 28 killed five rescuers and another miner, bringing the toll to 36.

02-26.title: Outbreak of the Darfur conflict
02-26.description: Rebel groups attacked a government air base in North Darfur, triggering a counterinsurgency campaign by the Sudanese government and allied Janjaweed militias that killed an estimated 3,000 civilians and displaced more than 600,000 people by the end of 2003. The conflict escalated into a sustained campaign of attacks on civilian villages.

review.note: HRW supports conflict beginning in February 2003, but the airfield attack belongs to April 25, not the supplied February 26 date. No checked evidence establishes precisely 3,000 civilian deaths or 600,000 displaced by December 2003. Resolve onset convention and annual scope before publication; do not present this as one day's toll.

sources.name: Human Rights and Human Welfare paper

02-26.title: SuperFerry 14 bombing
02-26.description: A bomb aboard SuperFerry 14 caused a fire near Manila Bay at about 00:50 on February 27, 2004, local time, February 26 UTC. The attack was attributed to Abu Sayyaf. The reported death toll of 116 includes missing passengers presumed dead.

02-27.title: Godhra train burning
02-27.description: A coach of the Sabarmati Express caught fire following an attack near Godhra station on 27 February 2002, killing 59 passengers, including Hindu pilgrims and activists returning from Ayodhya. The incident was followed by widespread anti-Muslim violence in Gujarat.

02-27.title: Chile earthquake and tsunami
02-27.description: A magnitude 8.8 earthquake, one of the strongest ever recorded, struck off the coast of central Chile on February 27, 2010, generating a tsunami with waves up to 24 meters that destroyed coastal towns such as Dichato and Constitución. Authorities confirmed 525 deaths and 25 missing, about 800,000 people displaced, and roughly 370,000 homes damaged. The quake triggered over 1,000 landslides and a nationwide blackout affecting 93 percent of the population; the death toll was comparatively low due to Chile's stringent building codes adopted after the 1960 Valdivia earthquake.

review.note: Magnitude/date corroborated. USGS response report gives 521 dead/56 missing, while later AP uses 526. Existing 525/25 may be a different official snapshot; needs dated Chilean authority reconciliation. 24 m waves, landslide count, displacement and building-code causal comparison were not all established.

02-27.title: Balyun airstrikes on Turkish troops
02-27.description: On 27 February 2020, during the Idlib offensive in northwestern Syria, an airstrike attributed to the Syrian and Russian air forces hit a convoy of a Turkish mechanized infantry battalion near Balyun. Turkey reported 34 soldiers killed (33-34 depending on the official source) and more than 30 wounded, making it the deadliest attack on Turkish forces in Syria. Turkey responded by launching Operation Spring Shield, which ended in a Russia-Turkey ceasefire on 5 March 2020.

review.note: 33/34 official tallies vary, with later reports higher. Russian involvement is disputed rather than established. Must distinguish March 5 ceasefire agreement from its March 6 effective time and establish actual strike location/building versus convoy with primary/reputable reporting.

02-28.title: 2002 Gujarat riots
02-28.description: Weeks of communal rioting followed the Godhra train burning, with violence concentrated in Ahmedabad and other Gujarat cities. The official death toll was about 1,000, while independent estimates range up to 2,000, most of them Muslims.

review.note: HRW supports mass violence and higher estimates, but its retrospective says retaliatory attacks had already begun on 27 February, before the major 28 February escalation. The rounded official count needs a primary final tally and explicit exclusion/inclusion of Godhra victims to prevent overlap.

02-28.title: Hilla suicide car bombing
02-28.description: A suicide car bombing struck people waiting outside a clinic in Hilla on February 28, 2005, including applicants for government security jobs. Early reports counted at least 125 dead; Iraq Body Count's current incident table records 135-136.

review.note: 125 was early reporting. IBC's current table gives 135-136 although its heading still says 125-136; another summary gives 127. Date and clinic bombing are secure, final fatality total is not. Remove superlative and broad victim characterization.

02-28.title: Tempe passenger train collision
02-28.description: A passenger train and a freight train collided head-on near Tempe, Greece, late on February 28, 2023, killing 57 people. A 2025 safety investigation identified human error, outdated infrastructure and systemic railway failures. The crash triggered widespread protests over railway safety.

03-01.title: Ethiopia drought and food crisis
03-01.description: After years of failed rains, a severe drought gripped southeastern Ethiopia with 8 million facing severe food shortages. Malnutrition-related deaths ran into the low thousands before international relief averted a repeat of the 1984-85 famine.

review.note: FAO supports the regional drought and roughly eight million needing assistance. No reviewed source establishes 1 March as a discrete event or 2,000 as a measured death toll. Do not convert a broad crisis estimate into a daily count.

03-01.title: Kunming Railway Station Attack
03-01.description: Five knife-wielding attackers assaulted passengers at Kunming Railway Station on March 1, 2014, killing 31 people and injuring 141, according to the court account. Four attackers were killed by police. Three other members of the group had been arrested before the assault.

review.note: Court account distinguishes eight members of the group from five people who actually attacked the station; three had been arrested earlier. 21:12 local March 1 is 13:12 UTC. Keep 31 victim deaths excluding four attackers. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

03-01.title: Abiemnom massacre
03-01.description: Armed attackers raided Abiemnom in South Sudan's Ruweng Administrative Area on 1 March 2026. Local authorities reported 169 deaths, including 90 civilians. The UN mission said about 1,000 people sought shelter at its base. Accounts differed over the attackers' affiliation and the number injured.
sources: Global Centre for the Responsibility to Protect

03-02.title: Ashura bombings in Karbala and Baghdad
03-02.description: Coordinated explosions struck Shia worshippers observing Ashura in Karbala and Baghdad on March 2, 2004. Contemporary reports gave differing casualty totals, including 182 deaths; hundreds were injured.

review.note: Contemporary RTE reports 182, while Japan's retrospective diplomatic bluebook says over 170 with over 390 injured; final 182/550 is not established. Initial weapon accounts were disputed. Correct geographic scope and remove speculative tactical detail.

03-04.title: Peshawar mosque bombing
03-04.description: A suicide bomber attacked a Shia mosque in Peshawar's Qissa Khwani Bazaar area during Friday prayers on March 4, 2022. Reporting the next day put the death toll at 63 after injured victims died. Islamic State's regional affiliate claimed responsibility.

03-06.title: Karrada double bombing in Baghdad
03-06.description: Two explosions struck Baghdad's Karrada shopping district on March 6, 2008. The second occurred as people gathered to help victims of the first. Subsequent reporting put the death toll at 68.

03-07.title: Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370 Disappearance
03-07.description: Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370 lost contact with air traffic control at about 17:22 UTC on March 7, 2014, during its Kuala Lumpur-Beijing flight. It carried 227 passengers and 12 crew. Later satellite evidence led investigators to search the southern Indian Ocean; all 239 aboard are presumed dead.

03-07.title: Bahia Blanca flash floods
03-07.description: Flash flooding struck Bahia Blanca and surrounding areas on March 7, 2025, after 290 mm of rain in 12 hours. The confirmed death toll reached 18 after identification of the last missing child in May.

03-07.title: Syrian coastal massacres of Alawites
03-07.description: A Reuters investigation documented 1,479 Alawites killed at 40 sites during the March 7-9, 2025 massacres in Syria's coastal region. Its reporting linked attackers through a chain of command to figures serving alongside the country's new leadership; the count does not include all deaths in the wider fighting.

03-10.title: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 crash
03-10.description: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 flying from Addis Ababa to Nairobi, crashed near Bishoftu on March 10, 2019, about six minutes after takeoff. All 157 people aboard died.

03-10.title: Gamo Zone floods and landslides
03-10.description: On 10 March 2026, days of heavy rainfall in the Gamo Zone of South Ethiopia triggered widespread flash floods and landslides that killed at least 125 people. The disaster struck farming communities in the southern highlands, destroying homes, roads and farmland across multiple villages.

review.note: 125 deaths supported; sources date the sequence March 9-10, March 10, or early March 11. Exact UTC onset and road/farmland damage remain unresolved.

03-11.title: Barakova coal mine explosion
03-11.description: An explosion at the Barakova coal mine in the Krasnodon region on March 11, 2000 killed dozens of miners. RFE/RL subsequently reported 81 deaths, while contemporary Guardian reporting gave 82.

review.note: The original 80 was an early count. RFE/RL on March 16 reports 81, while The Guardian on March 13 reports 82. The sources do not explain that reduction or establish a reconciled final count. The source-attributed 81 is a candidate correction only; the unresolved exact toll prevents publication.

03-11.title: Madrid Train Bombings
03-11.description: Bombs exploded on Madrid commuter trains during the morning rush hour on March 11, 2004. Spanish government accounts distinguish 192 victims of the train attacks from a police officer killed in the related Leganes explosion on April 3. More than 1,800 people were injured in the train bombings.

03-11.title: Winnenden School Shooting
03-11.description: On March 11, 2009, 17-year-old former student Tim Kretschmer killed 15 people in a shooting spree beginning at his former school in Winnenden, Germany, and ending in nearby Wendlingen. He later died by suicide, bringing the total number of deaths to 16 including the attacker.

03-11.title: Tohoku earthquake, tsunami and Fukushima disaster
03-11.description: A magnitude 9.0 earthquake struck off the Pacific coast of Japan on March 11, 2011, generating a massive tsunami that inundated the northeastern coastline. Waves up to 40 metres high destroyed entire towns in Iwate, Miyagi and Fukushima prefectures, and the tsunami caused a nuclear meltdown at the Fukushima Daiichi power plant. Japan's National Police Agency final figures record 19,759 deaths and 2,553 missing, with most victims drowned by the tsunami; the majority of the deceased were over 60 years old.

review.note: NPA maintains dated updates, not a timeless final figure. The cited 19,759/2,553 pair needs reconciliation against a specific later table and separation of direct from disaster-related deaths; older police report is only an early snapshot. Wave maximum, age distribution and nuclear consequences also require separate sources.

03-11.title: Jaffar Express hijacking
03-11.description: Baloch Liberation Army militants hijacked the Jaffar Express in Balochistan on March 11, 2025. Pakistan's military reported 31 victims killed, 354 hostages rescued and 33 attackers killed when the operation ended the following day.

03-14.title: Cyclone Idai
03-14.description: Cyclone Idai made landfall near the port city of Beira in central Mozambique on the night of 14-15 March 2019, bringing torrential rains and winds of up to 175 km/h that caused the Buzi and Pungwe rivers to burst their banks. More than 1,500 people died across Mozambique, Zimbabwe, Malawi and Madagascar, with the toll later confirmed at 1,593, and more than 2,000 people were reported missing. Hundreds of thousands were left stranded in floodwater, and the United Nations called it one of the worst weather-related disasters to hit the Southern Hemisphere.

review.note: Landfall near Beira March 14-15 established. Claimed confirmed 1,593 and 2,000 missing not established. WHO gives 603 for Mozambique; an EM-DAT-based study gives 1,234 storm deaths. Need consistent multinational period and missing-versus-dead accounting before replacement.

sources.name: International Journal of Disaster Risk Science

03-15.title: Syrian uprising and government crackdown
03-15.description: Pro-democracy protests inspired by the Arab Spring began in the city of Daraa in mid-March 2011 and spread across Syria, where they were met with a violent government crackdown involving live fire, tanks, mass arrests and torture. The unrest progressively militarized into an armed insurgency as army defectors formed the Free Syrian Army in July. By December 13, 2011, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Navi Pillay reported that more than 5,000 people, including over 300 children, had been killed in the uprising.

review.note: UN figures are a dated cumulative estimate, not March 15 deaths. Pillay briefing was Monday December 12, rather than the December 13 publication date. Exact onset in Daraa and July FSA chronology need primary corroboration.

03-15.title: Christchurch Mosque Shootings
03-15.description: A gunman attacked the Al Noor Mosque and Linwood Islamic Centre in Christchurch, New Zealand, on March 15, 2019, killing 51 people.

03-16.title: Atlanta spa shootings
03-16.description: A gunman attacked three Atlanta-area massage businesses on March 16, 2021, killing eight people, including six women of Asian descent.

03-16.title: Kocani nightclub fire
03-16.description: A fire at the Pulse nightclub in Kocani on March 16, 2025 killed 63 people and injured more than 200, according to figures cited in court indictments. Investigators reported that pyrotechnics ignited flammable ceiling foam in a venue lacking adequate fire safety provisions.

03-19.title: Ulyanovskaya mine disaster
03-19.description: A methane explosion at the Ulyanovskaya coal mine near Novokuznetsk on March 19, 2007, killed 110 of the 203 people underground. Ninety-three survived, according to IFRC.

03-20.title: Chattisinghpora massacre
03-20.location: Chattisinghpora, Anantnag district, Jammu and Kashmir, India
03-20.description: Gunmen rounded up Sikh residents in Chattisinghpora in Anantnag district on March 20, 2000 and shot them, killing 35 people.

03-20.title: US-led invasion of Iraq
03-20.description: The US-led invasion of Iraq began on March 20, 2003, and Baghdad fell on April 9. Iraq Body Count's 2005 dossier recorded 7,299 civilian deaths during the invasion period through April 30. This is a documented period total, not deaths on the opening day or a comprehensive estimate of all war mortality.

03-20.title: Peru floods and mudslides
03-20.description: Coastal El Nino conditions caused severe floods and mudslides in Peru during 2016-2017. Peru's meteorological agency reports 162 deaths and nearly 1.5 million people affected. The disaster spanned several months rather than beginning on March 20.

review.note: SENAMHI supports 162 deaths and nearly 1.5 million affected for the coastal El Nino disaster, formally December 2016-May 2017. March 20 is a publication date for a much earlier 75-death report, not the event onset. RPP attributes 162 to an August INDECI report. The claimed EM-DAT 177 and homeless scope were not independently established. Date remains unresolved even after replacing the prose.

03-21.title: Red Lake High School shooting
03-21.description: On March 21, 2005, a 16-year-old killed his grandfather and his grandfather's companion before attacking Red Lake High School. He killed a security guard, a teacher and five students there, then died by suicide. Ten people died in total, including the attacker.

03-21.title: Battle of Mogadishu (2007)
03-21.description: Ethiopian and Somali government forces fought insurgents in Mogadishu during major offensives in March and April 2007. Human Rights Watch documented extensive civilian harm but said precise mortality figures could not be established.

review.note: HRW dates main first offensive March29-April2, second round endingApril26, and explicitly cannot give precise civilian deaths. Estimates400-1,000 first round plus about300 second are not an independently established1,200. March21 onset and annual6,000/superlative remain unverified.

03-21.title: China Eastern Airlines Flight MU5735 crash
03-21.description: China Eastern Airlines Flight MU5735, a Boeing 737-800 travelling from Kunming to Guangzhou, descended rapidly and crashed near Wuzhou, Guangxi, on March 21, 2022. All 132 people aboard died. The April 2022 preliminary investigation did not determine the cause; debris examination and flight-data analysis were continuing.

03-21.title: South Korea wildfire outbreak
03-21.description: Wildfires began in southeastern South Korea on March 21, 2025 and spread across several areas, including Uiseong and Sancheong. World Weather Attribution's April 30 account reported 32 deaths in the March outbreak; Copernicus also reports 32 deaths and around 5,000 buildings destroyed.

03-22.title: Oso Mudslide
03-22.description: A landslide near Oso, Washington, swept across the Stillaguamish River valley on March 22, 2014, destroying homes and killing 43 people. The final victim's remains were recovered that July.

03-22.title: Brussels airport and metro bombings
03-22.description: Suicide bombings struck Brussels Airport and Maalbeek metro station on March 22, 2016. Thirty-two victims died in the attacks. In 2023, the court recognized three later deaths as attributable to the attacks, bringing the official victim toll to 35.

03-22.title: Boulder supermarket shooting
03-22.description: A gunman killed ten people, including police officer Eric Talley, at the King Soopers supermarket in Boulder, Colorado, on March 22, 2021. Police captured the suspect alive. An arrest affidavit said he purchased a Ruger AR-556 semiautomatic pistol on March 16, six days before the attack.

03-22.title: Crocus City Hall Concert Hall Attack
03-22.description: Gunmen attacked Crocus City Hall in Krasnogorsk, outside Moscow, on March 22, 2024, shooting concertgoers and setting the venue on fire. AP's August 2025 trial reporting gives 149 deaths and more than 600 wounded. Islamic State claimed responsibility for the attack.

03-23.title: Ogossagou massacre
03-23.description: Armed men attacked the Fulani part of Ogossagou village in central Mali at about 05:00 on March 23, 2019. A UN investigation concluded that at least 157 people were killed. It identified most attackers as traditional hunters, accompanied by men in military and civilian clothing.

03-25.title: Nahrin earthquake
03-25.description: A magnitude 6.1 earthquake struck the Nahrin area of Baghlan Province on 25 March 2002. Later IFRC operational reporting estimated 800 deaths and 10,000 people left homeless. Early casualty estimates were substantially higher; this figure follows the later IFRC assessment.
sources: International Charter Space and Major Disasters

03-25.title: Capitol Hill massacre in Seattle
03-25.description: Kyle Huff killed six people and wounded two at a house party in Seattle's Capitol Hill neighborhood on March 25, 2006. He then died by suicide when confronted by police, bringing the total number of deaths to seven, including the attacker.

03-25.title: Kemerovo shopping mall fire
03-25.description: A fire at the Winter Cherry shopping and entertainment complex in Kemerovo, Russia, on March 25, 2018 killed 60 people, including children. Later investigations found serious fire-safety failures.

03-26.title: ROKS Cheonan sinking
03-26.location: Baengnyeong Island, Yellow Sea, South Korea
03-26.description: The South Korean corvette ROKS Cheonan sank near Baengnyeong Island on March 26, 2010, killing 46 of its 104 crew. A multinational investigation attributed the sinking to a North Korean torpedo. North Korea denied responsibility.
sources: United Nations, North Korean press conference

03-27.title: Park Hotel Passover massacre
03-27.description: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked the Park Hotel in Netanya during a Passover meal on 27 March 2002, killing 30 civilians and injuring more than 100. The attack was one of the triggers for Israel's Operation Defensive Shield.

03-27.title: Tal Afar truck bombings
03-27.description: Truck bombs struck markets in Tal Afar on March 27, 2007, collapsing buildings. Iraq Body Count records 152 deaths; a US Army history reports nearly 350 wounded. Subsequent reprisal killings are not included in this bombing toll.
sources: US Army Iraq War history volume2

03-27.title: Lahore Easter park bombing
03-27.description: A suicide bombing struck Lahore's Gulshan-e-Iqbal Park on Easter Sunday, March 27, 2016. Jamaat-ul-Ahrar claimed responsibility and said it targeted Christians. Published death totals differ, including reports of victims dying later from injuries.

review.note: Date, location and attack identity are supported. PIPS's annual report gives at least 74 deaths including 29 children and over 233 injuries. SATP's incident prose says 74, its table 75, and its April 21 entry reports a later victim raising the toll to 78. These inconsistencies do not establish a final 75 or a final child/injury breakdown. Christian targeting was the attackers' stated intent, not evidence that every victim was Christian.

03-28.title: Nias-Simeulue earthquake
03-28.description: A magnitude 8.6 earthquake struck off northern Sumatra on March 28, 2005, severely damaging Nias and nearby islands and generating a relatively small tsunami. Published death estimates vary; most fatalities occurred on Nias.

review.note: Magnitude 8.6 and March 28 UTC are secure. Later summaries span 915-1,314 while early relief estimates were higher; hundreds on Simeulue/Banyak are not established as final confirmed counts. Need final regional breakdown rather than combining initial estimates.

03-28.title: Myanmar earthquake (magnitude 7.7)
03-28.description: On March 28, 2025, a magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck near Sagaing and Mandalay in Myanmar along the Sagaing Fault, collapsing buildings and infrastructure and also killing 18 people in Bangkok, Thailand. Myanmar's military government reported about 3,770 dead, while independent Myanmar media estimates exceeded 5,000, and the true toll was widely considered higher.

review.note: The March 28 M7.7 earthquake is well supported, but 3,770 is not a final reconciled death count. Myanmar's government reported 3,782 as of August 20, 2025 for six affected regions/states; UNICEF's May 2 report used 3,835 from another reporting stream. Independent Myanmar-media estimates were substantially higher, and the Thai 18-death figure is an early snapshot (ADRC already reports 83 Thailand deaths in its May 7 snapshot). National, cross-border and independent counts need a consistent cutoff and scope. Do not equate the government count with the true whole-event toll or retain 18 as a final Thai total.

03-29.title: Moscow Metro suicide bombings
03-29.description: Two female suicide bombers attacked the Moscow Metro on the morning of March 29, 2010. The reported death toll rose to 40. North Caucasus insurgent leader Doku Umarov claimed responsibility.

03-31.title: Borujerd (Silakhor) earthquake
03-31.description: An earthquake of magnitude 6.1 struck the Silakhor plain region of Lorestan province in western Iran on March 31, 2006, early in the morning, centered near the village of Darb-e Astaneh. The quake killed about 70 people, injured more than 1,200 and damaged or destroyed buildings in roughly 330 villages, with the worst destruction in Borujerd and Dorud.
sources: International Institute of Earthquake Engineering and Seismology (IIEES)

review.note: Early IFRC and JICA reports give70; IFRC's April2007 retrospective instead gives63 deaths and1,418 injured. Mainshock March31 01:17UTC and Mw6.1 established, but revised mortality discrepancy is not reconciled.

04-01.title: Solomon Islands earthquake and tsunami
04-01.location: Western and Choiseul provinces, Solomon Islands
04-01.description: A magnitude 8.1 earthquake struck near Gizo at 20:39 UTC on April 1, 2007, the morning of April 2 locally, generating a destructive tsunami. The earthquake and tsunami killed 52 people in the Solomon Islands. The national disaster office's subsequent reconciliation reported no people still missing.

04-01.title: Mocoa mudslide, Colombia
04-01.description: Floodwater and debris swept through Mocoa in Colombia's Putumayo department on the night of March 31-April 1, 2017, April 1 UTC. The municipality's risk assessment records 336 deaths and more than 400 injuries.
sources: Colombia National Disaster Risk Management Unit

04-01.title: India's second COVID-19 wave
04-01.description: India was overwhelmed by a second wave of COVID-19 driven by the Delta variant from April to June 2021, when hospitals, crematoria, and oxygen supplies ran out in Delhi and other cities. India officially recorded about 400,000 COVID-19 deaths during 2021, the vast majority during this wave, while independent estimates such as the World Health Organization's excess-death analysis placed the true toll far higher.

review.note: 400,000 appears to conflate a cumulative pandemic milestone with calendar-2021 deaths and with the April-June wave. The later study estimates 2.4 million excess deaths in 2021 at 7.2 times reported COVID deaths, inconsistent with 400,000 as the annual official count. April 1 is not established as a discrete event date; do not replace reported deaths with excess mortality without changing scope.

04-02.title: Garissa University College attack
04-02.description: Al-Shabaab gunmen attacked Garissa University College at dawn on April 2, 2015, shooting students and taking hostages. Kenya's interior minister subsequently reported 148 people killed, most of them students. Security forces ended the siege that day.

04-02.title: Bucha massacre
04-02.description: After Russian forces withdrew from Bucha in early April 2022, Ukrainian authorities discovered mass graves and the bodies of hundreds of civilians killed during the month-long occupation of the town. Ukrainian officials recovered 458 bodies, most showing signs of shooting, torture, or other violent trauma. OHCHR documented at least 73 unlawful killings in Bucha itself and reported more than 1,300 killings across the wider Bucha district, describing the massacre as a grave violation of international law.

review.note: Municipal 458 includes 39 apparently natural deaths and one bag of remains; not 458 established unlawful killings. OHCHR records 422 bodies recovered by September and 73 documented civilian killings during March 4-30. April 2 is discovery/reporting period, not killing date. Wider 1,300 appears Kyiv-region rather than town-specific and attribution needs correction; retain contradictory denominators.

04-03.title: Binghamton Immigration Center Shooting
04-03.description: On April 3, 2009, a gunman attacked the American Civic Association in Binghamton, New York, killing 13 people and wounding four. The attacker then died by suicide, bringing the total deaths including him to 14.

04-04.title: First Battle of Fallujah
04-04.description: US forces began an assault on Fallujah on the night of April 4, 2004, after four American contractors were killed. Iraq Body Count cites about 800 reported Iraqi deaths across the April siege and estimates that 572-616 were civilians. These cumulative figures are estimates, not a single-day count.

04-04.title: Thane building collapse
04-04.description: A residential building under construction in Mumbra, Thane, collapsed on the evening of April 4, 2013. The final rescue-operation toll was 74 dead, including 23 women and 18 children. Dozens of people were injured.

04-04.title: Khan Sheikhoun chemical attack
04-04.description: Sarin was used as a chemical weapon at Khan Shaykhun, Syria, on April 4, 2017. The OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism attributed responsibility to the Syrian Arab Republic. The OPCW fact-finding team identified approximately 100 fatalities but could not establish an exact total.

review.note: OPCW confirms sarin use on April 4, and the JIM attributes responsibility to the Syrian Arab Republic. Do not confuse the FFM's chemical identification remit with JIM's attribution remit. FFM paragraphs 5.80 and 6.13 describe approximately 100 fatalities after potential duplicates among 107 reported names, explicitly unable to determine exact numbers; this does not verify 89 or over 500 distinct injured. The exact toll remains unresolved, independently of the supported attack attribution.

sources.name: OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism report S/2017/904
US Department of State, JIM report summary

04-04.title: Battle for Tripoli (Western Libya offensive)
04-04.description: On 4 April 2019, forces of the Libyan National Army under Khalifa Haftar launched an offensive to capture Tripoli from the UN-backed Government of National Accord, setting off nearly 14 months of fighting in the capital's southern suburbs. By the end of 2019 the United Nations reported that more than 1,000 people had been killed and about 146,000 displaced, with civilian infrastructure including hospitals and residential areas hit by airstrikes and shelling. The campaign continued into 2020, when a ceasefire and UN-brokered political talks brought a halt to the offensive.

review.note: 1,000 is an interim toll. The offensive ended through military withdrawal in June, before the later ceasefire; final death count remains unresolved.

04-05.title: Upper Big Branch Mine explosion
04-05.description: An explosion at Massey Energy's Upper Big Branch Mine near Montcoal, West Virginia, on April 5, 2010, killed 29 miners and injured two. MSHA identified systematic safety failures, including inadequate control of methane and coal dust, and concluded the disaster was preventable. It was the deadliest US coal mining disaster in 40 years.
sources: Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission

04-06.title: L'Aquila Earthquake
04-06.description: An earthquake struck Abruzzo and the city of L'Aquila at 3:32 a.m. local time on April 6, 2009. Italian Civil Protection records 309 deaths and more than 1,500 injuries. About 65,000 people were displaced.

04-07.title: Douma chemical weapons attack
04-07.description: On April 7, 2018, a chemical attack in Douma, Syria, killed 43 named people. In January 2023, the OPCW investigation team found reasonable grounds to believe that Syrian air forces dropped two cylinders containing chlorine on residential buildings, affecting dozens more people.

04-09.title: Palm Sunday church bombings, Egypt
04-09.description: Suicide bombings struck Coptic churches in Tanta and Alexandria on Palm Sunday, April 9, 2017. Islamic State claimed responsibility. The victim toll subsequently reached 47.

04-11.title: KwaZulu-Natal floods
04-11.description: Heavy rain and flooding devastated KwaZulu-Natal, including Durban, in April 2022. On May 3, the provincial government reported 435 deaths and 63 people still missing. Homes, roads, bridges and water infrastructure were extensively damaged. April 11 anchors the multi-day flooding episode.

review.note: 435 is supported as May 3 reported toll, with 63 missing, not a timeless final number. Remove unneeded historical superlative. April 11 remains an unestablished selection within the multi-day episode in the evidence reviewed; the dated May 3 mortality report does not establish that event date.

sources.name: South Africa Department of Water and Sanitation

04-11.title: Jilli market airstrike
04-11.description: A Nigerian airstrike hit Jilli market near the Borno-Yobe border on 11 April 2026. Amnesty International reported at least 100 civilians killed, citing survivors and medical contacts. Other estimates were higher. The military said it had targeted militants; accounts of the strike and the casualty total remained disputed.

review.note: April 11 event, April 12 publication. 100 is a rights-group toll, not official final count. Military defended the operation; exact UTC onset unavailable. A single verified UTC onset and reconciliation of the competing casualty accounts remain unavailable; the attributed minimum is not a confirmed final total.

04-13.title: Yushu earthquake
04-13.description: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck the Yushu area of Qinghai, China, on April 13, 2010 UTC (April 14 locally). USGS records at least 2,698 deaths, 270 people missing and 12,135 injured, with extensive building damage.

04-14.title: Nyanya Bus Station Bombing
04-14.description: A bomb exploded at Nyanya bus station outside Abuja during the morning rush on April 14, 2014. Later reporting put the toll at at least 75 dead and 141 injured. Boko Haram claimed responsibility.

review.note: Initial official 71 became at least 75 in later reporting; neither should be called an exact final tally. Morning Nigerian event retains April 14 UTC. Concise replacement removes unrelated kidnapping detail. The later reported minimum does not settle the final tally; the correction is partial and not publication-ready.

04-14.title: Kumamoto earthquakes
04-14.description: A sequence of earthquakes struck Kumamoto Prefecture, Japan, beginning on April 14, 2016. The larger shock occurred at 16:25 UTC on April 15, April 16 locally. The prefecture records 50 direct deaths and 225 disaster-related deaths; the numeric toll here counts direct deaths only.

04-15.title: Air China Flight 129 crash
04-15.description: Air China Flight 129, a Boeing 767 flying from Beijing to Busan, struck Mount Dotdae during a circling approach to Gimhae Airport on 15 April 2002. Of 166 people aboard, 129 died and 37 survived.

04-15.title: Boston Marathon Bombing
04-15.description: On April 15, 2013, two bombs exploded near the Boston Marathon finish line, killing three people and injuring hundreds. The FBI identified the attackers as Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev; a subsequent manhunt ended with one dead and the other captured.

04-15.title: Sewol Ferry Sinking
04-15.description: The ferry Sewol began capsizing near Jindo, South Korea, at about 23:48 UTC on April 15, 2014, or the morning of April 16 locally. Of 476 people aboard, 304 died or remained missing and presumed dead, while 172 survived.

04-15.title: Sudan civil war begins
04-15.description: War between the Sudanese Armed Forces and Rapid Support Forces began on April 15, 2023. In its update covering events through November 24, ACLED recorded more than 12,190 reported political-violence deaths since the outbreak. This is a dated, incomplete reported-death count excluding indirect mortality, not a final toll of the war.

04-16.title: Virginia Tech shooting
04-16.description: On April 16, 2007, a student gunman killed 32 people and wounded 17 by gunfire in two attacks at Virginia Tech in Blacksburg, Virginia. Other people suffered injuries while escaping. The attacker died by suicide and is excluded from the 32 victims.
sources: Virginia Tech Review Panel via US DOJ

04-16.title: Ecuador earthquake (M7.8)
04-16.description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck coastal Ecuador at 23:58 UTC on April 16, 2016, severely affecting the Pedernales area of Manabi Province. Ecuador's later national planning account reports 676 deaths and more than 16,600 injuries from the disaster.
sources: Ecuador national planning authority, Zone 4 agenda

04-17.title: Nigeria post-election violence
