04-17.description: Violence erupted in northern Nigeria on April 17, 2011, as presidential-election results indicated Goodluck Jonathan had defeated Muhammadu Buhari. Human Rights Watch reported more than 800 deaths and over 65,000 displaced people in three days of election-related and communal attacks across 12 northern states, including unlawful killings by security forces.

04-18.title: al-Sadriya market bombing
04-18.description: A car bomb exploded at Baghdad's Sadriya food market on the afternoon of April 18, 2007. Iraq Body Count records 140 deaths in this attack, excluding other bombings across Baghdad that day.

04-20.title: Lushan earthquake
04-20.description: An earthquake struck Lushan County in Ya'an, Sichuan, at 00:02 UTC on April 20, 2013. Chinese authorities measured it at magnitude 7.0. Xinhua's later retrospective records 196 deaths.

04-21.title: Deepwater Horizon explosion and oil spill
04-21.description: The Deepwater Horizon drilling rig exploded in the Gulf of Mexico on the evening of April 20, 2010 local time (April 21 UTC), killing 11 workers. The damaged Macondo well released oil for 87 days. NOAA reports approximately 3.2 million barrels entered the Gulf, damaging marine and coastal ecosystems.

04-21.title: Sri Lanka Easter bombings
04-21.description: On Easter Sunday, 21 April 2019, a series of coordinated suicide bombings struck three churches and three luxury hotels in Colombo, Negombo and Batticaloa, with two further explosions occurring later in the day. A total of 269 people were killed, including dozens of foreign nationals, and more than 500 were injured, making it the deadliest act of violence in Sri Lanka since the end of the civil war. The Islamic State claimed responsibility, and investigations focused on the local group National Thowheeth Jama'ath and its links to international militant networks.

review.note: Date and coordinated church/hotel attack supported. 269 excluding nine bombers is in secondary summaries, while initial official counts were sharply revised. Need primary/reputable final total and confirmation of all location/injury/attribution details; do not substitute the preliminary 359 or 250-260.

04-22.title: Ryongchon train explosion
04-22.description: An ammonium-nitrate explosion at Ryongchon railway station on April 22, 2004, devastated the surrounding town. IFRC reported 161 deaths and about 1,300 injuries. The French government's accident archive records 76 children among those killed.

04-22.title: Kabul voter registration center bombing
04-22.description: A suicide bomber attacked a voter registration center in the Dasht-e-Barchi district of western Kabul, a predominantly Shia Hazara area, during Afghanistan's parliamentary election registration process. The blast killed at least 57 people and wounded more than 100, mostly civilians queued to obtain voter cards. The Islamic State Khorasan Province claimed responsibility for the attack, one of a series targeting the 2018 election process.

review.note: 57 was an initial toll. Later reporting gives more than 60, with secondary summaries giving 69; UNAMA records 198 total civilian casualties without a fatality breakdown in the retrieved page. Exact final death count and breakdown remain unresolved; date, registration-site identity and IS attribution are supported.

04-24.title: Rana Plaza factory collapse
04-24.description: The eight-storey Rana Plaza building in Savar, Bangladesh, collapsed on the morning of April 24, 2013. The ILO's retrospective records 1,134 deaths; more than 2,500 people were injured. Cracks had appeared before the collapse, which intensified international efforts to improve garment-industry safety.
sources: ILO Vision Zero Fund, Rana Plaza

04-25.title: Amagasaki train derailment
04-25.description: A JR West commuter train derailed and struck an apartment building in Amagasaki on April 25, 2005. It entered a 70 km/h curve at about 116 km/h. The crash killed 107 people, including the driver, and injured 562.

04-25.title: Nepal earthquake (Gorkha)
04-25.description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck central Nepal on April 25, 2015, causing catastrophic building damage, landslides and avalanches. USGS's 2015 summary attributes 8,964 deaths to the disaster, citing OCHA. The toll's treatment of later aftershocks needs reconciliation with separately listed events.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)

review.note: USGS attributes 8,964 deaths to the April event citing OCHA, and discusses a sequence including later aftershocks. Country decomposition in original is not confirmed, and separate May 12 row risks double counting. April 25 11:56 local is 06:11 UTC.

04-26.title: Kenya Floods and Landslides
04-26.description: Heavy seasonal rains caused floods and landslides across Kenya in 2024. UNICEF's June 24 snapshot recorded 315 deaths, 38 missing people, 188 injuries and 293,205 displaced people nationwide. These are cumulative seasonal figures, not the toll of one day in Nairobi.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

review.note: June 24 national snapshot supports 315 dead, 38 missing, 188 injured and 293,205 displaced, not 291 deaths or hundreds missing. April 26 is not established as onset of this March-June seasonal event. No supported exact replacement day; withhold pending date resolution. National-disaster declaration and dam-breach claims omitted.

04-27.title: 2011 Super Outbreak tornadoes
04-27.description: Between April 25 and 28, 2011, a record outbreak of 360 tornadoes struck 21 US states from Texas to New York, with 216 tornadoes touching down on April 27 alone. The outbreak killed 324 people across six states, including 238 in Alabama, and injured more than 3,100; four tornadoes were rated EF5. The deadliest tornado, the Hackleburg-Phil Campbell EF5 in Alabama and Tennessee, killed 72 people. It was the deadliest US tornado outbreak since 1936, with damages exceeding US$10 billion.

review.note: NOAA page gives 362 tornadoes and estimated 321 deaths, versus 360/324 here; its EF5 count also differs from other accepted summaries. Must reconcile tornado-only versus all-storm deaths and revised ratings. April 27 is peak day while record describes April 25-28. Do not replace all numbers from one inconsistent retrospective. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

04-27.title: Afghanistan flash floods
04-27.description: In late April 2025, heavy rains triggered flash floods across northern Afghanistan, with the worst destruction in Baghlan Province, where entire villages were swept away; at least 150 people were killed across the affected provinces per BBC reporting, while the World Food Programme estimated more than 300 dead and hundreds more injured.

review.note: Searches did not establish an April 27, 2025 Baghlan flood with these fatalities. The 150 official/300-plus WFP reporting pattern instead matches the May 10, 2024 northern Afghanistan floods, confirmed by contemporaneous May 2024 UN and news reports. The assigned data already has a May 2024 Baghlan event. This suggests a misdated duplicate, not proof that no flooding occurred in 2025. Do not automatically move this row to May 2024 or count both; identity, date and casualty scope require reconciliation.

04-30.title: Idlib offensive (Syria)
04-30.description: On 30 April 2019, the Syrian government, backed by Russian air power, launched a ground offensive against opposition-held areas of Idlib Governorate, the last major rebel stronghold. Between April and August, the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights recorded at least 1,043 civilian deaths and roughly 3,000 combatant deaths, while the United Nations reported more than 500 civilians killed in the first months and hundreds of thousands of people displaced, including repeated attacks on schools, hospitals and camps for displaced people.

review.note: Search supports campaign identity and reports 1,043 civilians in secondary coverage. Need the underlying SOHR final interval and combatant total, UN source for 500 deaths, and distinction between April air campaign and subsequent ground offensive. Not verified from secondary summaries.

05-01.title: Rio Grande do Sul Floods
05-01.description: Heavy rain in late April and May 2024 caused widespread flooding in Rio Grande do Sul, including Porto Alegre. Brazil's Senate reported 183 deaths, 806 injuries and 27 missing people in its December 2024 review, with 478 municipalities affected.

review.note: 183 deaths, 806 injuries and 27 missing are supported retrospectively. May 1 is an emergency-declaration date, not established flood onset. IFRC dates intense rains from April 29; other accounts start April 27. Preserve this onset ambiguity rather than declare a placeholder verified. Proposed prose removes unneeded displacement precision.

sources.name: Rio Grande do Sul Civil Defense

05-02.title: Bojaya massacre
05-02.description: On 2 May 2002, during fighting between FARC guerrillas and paramilitaries in Bellavista, Bojaya, a cylinder bomb launched by FARC struck the church where civilians had taken shelter. Colombia's victims authority later recorded at least 79 deaths and more than 100 injuries; earlier reports had put the toll at 119.

05-02.title: Cyclone Nargis strikes Myanmar
05-02.description: Cyclone Nargis struck Myanmar on May 2-3, 2008, devastating the Ayeyarwady Delta and other areas. The joint government, ASEAN and UN assessment reported 84,537 deaths and 53,836 people missing as of June 24. The recorded toll includes reported deaths only, excluding the missing. About 2.4 million people were severely affected.

05-04.title: Mexico City metro overpass collapse
05-04.description: An elevated section of Mexico City Metro Line 12 collapsed beneath a train between Olivos and Tezonco late on May 3, 2021 local time, May 4 UTC. Twenty-six people died and 79 were injured.

05-04.title: South Kivu floods and landslides
05-04.description: Heavy rain on May 4, 2023 triggered flooding and mudslides in Kalehe territory, South Kivu, destroying parts of Bushushu and Nyamukubi. A later MONUSCO appeal reported an official toll of 438 dead and more than 5,000 missing. The missing-person estimate is separate from confirmed deaths.

05-06.title: Visakhapatnam LG Polymers gas leak
05-06.description: In the early hours of 7 May 2020, styrene gas leaked from a sealed storage tank at the LG Polymers chemical plant on the outskirts of Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, India. The National Disaster Response Force reported 13 deaths and more than 1,000 people sickened, with about 300 hospitalized, many of them villagers and workers asleep during the nationwide COVID-19 lockdown. The leak was compared to the 1984 Bhopal gas disaster and led to arrests of company officials.

review.note: 02:30-03:00 May 7 IST is May 6 UTC. Supported UTC correction; exact final death count and attribution to NDRF, hospitalization counts and sealed-tank wording require further final-source reconciliation.

sources.name: India National Centre for Disease Control

05-06.title: Allen outlet mall shooting
05-06.description: A gunman killed eight people and wounded seven at Allen Premium Outlets in Allen, Texas, on May 6, 2023. A police officer who was at the mall on another call shot and killed the attacker. The eight-victim total excludes the gunman.

05-10.title: Eleven-day Gaza conflict
05-10.description: An 11-day war between Israel and Hamas erupted after weeks of tension in Jerusalem, with Israeli airstrikes and Palestinian rocket fire striking densely populated areas. At least 256 Palestinians, including 66 children, and 13 people in Israel were killed. More than 100,000 Gazans were displaced before a ceasefire took effect on May 21.

review.note: 256 is Gaza-only, while record title/location and description include Israel. Same-cutoff Palestinian/Israeli totals must be reconciled before choosing a combined integer; original description's 256+13 is 269. Counts also revised after ceasefire. Start May 10 supported, not all deaths on that day.

05-10.title: Baghlan Flash Floods
05-10.description: On May 10, 2024, heavy seasonal rainfall caused flash floods that swept through villages in northern Afghanistan, most severely in Baghlan Province. United Nations agencies reported at least 315 people killed and more than 1,600 injured, with tens of thousands of homes destroyed or damaged and several thousand people displaced.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

review.note: 315 and over 1,600 injuries were Taliban/refugee-ministry figures, not established UN totals. UNICEF's May report gives preliminary 180 deaths/280 injuries across May 10-11 northeastern flooding; WHO gives over 180/242. Counts and geographic scopes conflict. Tens of thousands of homes is unsupported; RFE/RL cites 2,660 destroyed. Need reconciled Baghlan-specific total.

05-12.title: Riyadh compound bombings
05-12.description: Al-Qaeda suicide bombers attacked three foreign residential compounds in Riyadh with car bombs, killing 35 people including nine Americans and wounding more than 160. The attacks marked the beginning of a militant campaign inside Saudi Arabia.

review.note: Rewards for Justice explicitly reports 35 killed, including nine Americans, but another US government chronology reports 34 including nine attackers. Their fatality populations do not clearly align. Date, three compounds and al-Qaeda attribution are supported; victim-only versus attacker-inclusive scope needs resolution before accepting 35.

05-12.title: Znamenskoye truck bombing
05-12.description: A suicide truck bombing struck a government and security compound in Znamenskoye, Chechnya, on May 12, 2003. A UN chronology records 59 people killed. The attack also injured about 200 people.

review.note: UN chronology supports May 12 and 59 deaths. Checked sources do not establish the claim that Basayev claimed responsibility. Remove that assertion rather than converting allegations into fact; exact attacker inclusion is not specified in the UN total. That unresolved attacker/victim scope remains a publication blocker despite the supported shorter prose.

05-12.title: Wenchuan earthquake (Sichuan earthquake)
05-12.description: The Wenchuan earthquake struck Sichuan on May 12, 2008, at 14:28 local time, damaging towns and infrastructure across the region. Later official figures cited in engineering research were 69,227 deaths, 17,923 missing and 374,643 injured. The recorded toll includes reported deaths only, excluding the missing.
sources: Earthquake Engineering Field Investigation Team study

05-12.title: Nepal earthquake aftershock
05-12.description: A magnitude 7.3 earthquake struck east of Kathmandu on May 12, 2015, following the April 25 Gorkha earthquake. It caused additional deaths and destruction in Nepal and neighbouring countries. Its separate fatality count must be distinguished from cumulative totals for the earthquake sequence.

review.note: Magnitude/date supported; 218 combines 153 Nepal, 62 India, two Bangladesh and one China in secondary accounting, not 218 in Nepal. Primary country totals and exclusion from April cumulative toll are not established.

05-12.title: Kabul maternity hospital attack
05-12.description: Gunmen attacked the MSF-supported maternity wing of Dasht-e-Barchi hospital in Kabul on May 12, 2020. Afghan authorities reported 24 people killed and more than 20 injured. MSF subsequently confirmed that the dead included 16 mothers, one MSF midwife and two children aged seven and eight.

05-13.title: Enschede fireworks disaster
05-13.description: A fire at a fireworks depot escalated into massive explosions, killing 23 people including four firefighters. The blasts destroyed around 400 homes.

05-13.title: Jaipur bombings
05-13.description: A series of bombs exploded in Jaipur's old city on the evening of May 13, 2008. Later court reporting records 71 deaths and 185 injuries. Four men convicted in the serial-blast case were acquitted by the High Court in 2023; four men were convicted in a separate related unexploded-bomb case in 2025.

05-13.title: Soma Coal Mine Disaster
05-13.description: A fire in the Eynez coal mine at Soma, Turkey, on May 13, 2014, killed 301 miners. Toxic gases, including carbon monoxide, were central to the deaths. Later investigations examined the fire's origin and serious mine-safety failures.

05-14.title: Balkan Floods
05-14.location: Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Croatia
05-14.description: Exceptional rainfall in mid-May 2014 caused devastating floods across the Sava River basin, including Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Croatia. ICPDR reported at least 80 deaths after a week of flooding, with extensive damage to homes and infrastructure.

review.note: May 14 is a defensible period anchor for record rainfall, not an instantaneous UTC incident. ICPDR gives at least 80 regional deaths; do not attribute them only to two countries. Mass-grave and displacement details not fully established here are removed. A period anchor must not be treated as a verified UTC incident date; this date blocker remains after the description correction.

sources.name: ICPDR and ISRBC, final flood report

05-14.title: Gaza border protest killings
05-14.description: Israeli forces killed 60 Palestinians during demonstrations near the Gaza perimeter fence on May 14, 2018. A subsequent UN inquiry reported more than 1,100 people shot that day. Across demonstrations from March 30 through December 31, 2018, the inquiry recorded 189 Palestinian deaths, including 183 caused by live ammunition.

05-14.title: Buffalo supermarket shooting
05-14.description: A white supremacist gunman attacked a Tops supermarket in Buffalo, New York, on May 14, 2022, killing ten Black people and injuring three others. He later pleaded guilty to state charges and received life imprisonment without parole.

05-16.title: Casablanca bombings
05-16.description: Coordinated suicide bombings struck several sites in Casablanca on May 16, 2003, including a Spanish restaurant and Jewish-associated targets. The reported total of 45 deaths includes 33 victims and 12 bombers; about 100 people were injured.

05-18.title: Sri Lankan Civil War Final Offensive
05-18.description: Between January and May 2009, the Sri Lankan military's final offensive against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) trapped roughly 330,000 civilians in an ever-shrinking 'no fire zone' in the northeast. A UN Secretary-General-appointed panel of experts estimated in 2011 that as many as 40,000 civilians were killed, most by government shelling, with the LTTE also accused of using civilians as human shields. The government's own figures put the toll at about 7,000-9,000. The war ended on May 18, 2009, with the military declaring victory.

review.note: 40,000 is an upper estimate cited by the UN panel, not a confirmed count. AP corroborates tens of thousands and abuses by both sides. Government 7,000-9,000 attribution and the precise 330,000 trapped figure remain unestablished. The military defeat on May 18 and presidential victory declaration on May 19 must not be conflated.

05-18.title: Cubana de Aviación Flight 972 crash
05-18.description: On May 18, 2018, a Boeing 737 operating for Cubana de Aviacion crashed into a field shortly after departing Havana's Jose Marti International Airport. Of the 113 people aboard, 112 died and one survived. The aircraft was operated by Mexican charter company Global Air.

05-20.title: Cyclone Amphan
05-20.description: Cyclone Amphan, the first super cyclonic storm in the Bay of Bengal since 1999, made landfall near Bakkhali in West Bengal, India on 20 May 2020 with winds up to 260 km/h. The storm killed 133 people in total, including 103 in India (most in West Bengal) and 26 in Bangladesh, and displaced millions. Amphan severely damaged Kolkata and the Sundarbans, and its landfall during the COVID-19 pandemic complicated evacuation and relief efforts.

review.note: May 20 landfall supported. Landfall winds were 155-165 km/h, gusting 185, not 260; 260 confuses peak offshore strength with landfall. 103+26 does not sum to 133 and remaining country scope is absent. Need final reconciled toll; first Bay-of-Bengal super-cyclone-since-1999 claim also needs authoritative check.

05-20.title: Battle of Bakhmut
05-20.description: Russian forces completed their capture of the eastern Ukrainian city of Bakhmut on May 20, 2023, ending one of the bloodiest battles of the Russia–Ukraine war, which had raged for about ten months. U.S. officials estimated that roughly 20,000 Russian soldiers had been killed in the battle, with tens of thousands more wounded, and Ukrainian officials reported thousands of their own soldiers killed; the city was reduced to ruins. Independent verification of exact casualties was not possible due to the secrecy of the warring sides.
sources: Institute for the Study of War

review.note: The Post corrected its report: the U.S. estimate covered Russian losses across Ukraine, not Bakhmut alone. Battle-specific fatalities and the claimed thousands of Ukrainian deaths remain unverified. May 20 was a Russian capture claim disputed by Ukraine; do not present it as an uncontested end date. A reliable replacement battle toll is unavailable.

05-21.title: Boumerdès earthquake
05-21.description: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck offshore near Zemmouri in Boumerdes Province on May 21, 2003, causing extensive destruction in northern Algeria. Algeria's CRAAG reports 2,365 deaths, while other summaries give 2,266; the totals are not reconciled here.

review.note: Full CRAAG text confirms May 21 at 19:44 local time and Mw 6.8, but reports 2,365 deaths, not the original/reference-summary figure of 2,266. The earlier ledger note missed this contradiction. No source-level reconciliation establishes a final total. Remove the ranking, injury and homelessness precision, and withhold the row pending mortality reconciliation.

05-22.title: Air India Express Flight 812 crash
05-22.description: On May 22, 2010, Air India Express Flight 812, a Boeing 737-800 arriving from Dubai, overran the runway at Mangalore and crashed down an embankment. Of 166 people aboard, 158 died. The investigation found that the aircraft touched down far beyond the normal touchdown area after an unstabilized approach and that the captain failed to discontinue the landing.

05-22.title: Joplin tornado
05-22.description: An EF5 tornado struck Joplin, Missouri, on May 22, 2011, causing 158 direct deaths and more than 1,000 injuries, according to the National Weather Service. Its path extended about 22 miles.

05-22.title: Manchester Arena bombing
05-22.description: Salman Abedi detonated a suicide bomb at Manchester Arena as an Ariana Grande concert ended on May 22, 2017. Twenty-two victims were killed, excluding the bomber. His brother Hashem was later convicted of helping plan and prepare the attack.
sources: Greater Manchester Police, Hashem Abedi conviction

05-22.title: Qinyuan coal mine explosion
05-22.description: On 22 May 2026, an explosion at the Liushenyu coal mine in Qinyuan County, Shanxi Province, China, killed at least 82 miners, the worst coal-mining blast in China in more than a decade. The blast in one of China's major coal-producing regions prompted a state investigation into safety practices.

05-23.title: Poso sectarian riots
05-23.description: The third and deadliest phase of the Poso riots between Christian and Muslim communities. An estimated 300 people were killed.

review.note: HRW identifies May-June 2000 as the third phase and explains that aggregate fatality counts are uncertain. Exact 23 May onset and phase-specific 300 deaths were not established by the reviewed evidence.

05-24.title: Uvalde School Shooting
05-24.description: A gunman killed 19 children and two teachers at Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, on May 24, 2022. A US Justice Department review found a 77-minute gap between officers first arriving and confronting and killing the attacker. The victim count excludes the attacker.

05-25.title: China Airlines Flight 611 disaster
05-25.description: China Airlines Flight 611, a Boeing 747 traveling from Taipei to Hong Kong, broke up in mid-air about 20 minutes after takeoff and crashed into the Taiwan Strait. All 225 passengers and crew were killed.

05-25.title: Cyclone Aila
05-25.description: Cyclone Aila, a severe cyclonic storm in the Bay of Bengal, made landfall on May 25, 2009, near the Bangladesh-India border, bringing storm surges of up to 6 meters. Final official tallies recorded about 339 deaths across the region, including roughly 190 in Bangladesh and 140 in eastern India's West Bengal state, with hundreds of thousands left homeless and millions affected by flooding and breached embankments.
sources: University of Colorado Natural Hazards Center

review.note: Aila and May 25 landfall corroborated, but 339 as a final official regional count and the 190/140 split were not established. IMD-hosted assessment describes a 3 m surge in western Bangladesh; the claimed 6 m maximum needs a location-specific source. Satkhira is narrower than the regional toll.

05-25.title: Houla massacre
05-25.description: At least 108 people were killed in the Houla area of Syria on May 25, 2012. Human Rights Watch reported survivor accounts of executions following shelling and called for an independent investigation.

05-26.title: Yogyakarta earthquake
05-26.description: An earthquake struck the Yogyakarta and Central Java regions at about 05:54 on May 27, 2006, local time, May 26 UTC. Bantul and Klaten suffered severe damage. A subsequent IFRC report cites an official toll of 5,749 deaths and more than 38,000 injuries.

05-26.title: Indian heat wave
05-26.location: India, particularly Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
05-26.description: Extreme heat affected India during May and early June 2015, with particularly severe mortality in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Contemporary estimates exceeded 2,000 deaths, while surveillance totals differed in coverage. A precise onset date and reconciled death toll remain unestablished.

review.note: May 26 is a reporting-period date, not established onset. NOAA says at least 2,300; NASA cites 2,500 reporting, while national surveillance records a lower figure under different reporting coverage. Resolve onset, death definition and countrywide scope; do not preserve Andhra Pradesh as entire location.

05-28.title: Lahore Ahmadiyya mosque attacks
05-28.description: Gunmen from the Punjabi Taliban wing of Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan attacked two Ahmadiyya mosques in Lahore during Friday prayers on May 28, 2010, using automatic weapons, grenades, and suicide vests, and holding worshippers hostage for several hours. Human Rights Watch documented 94 people killed, 27 at the Baitul Nur mosque in Model Town and 67 at the Darul Zikr mosque in Garhi Shahu, with more than 100 wounded. The attacks were the deadliest assault on the Ahmadiyya religious minority in Pakistan's history.

review.note: HRW reported 94 deaths after the May 28 attacks. The community's June 12 primary clarification explicitly revised its own earlier 94 to 86, with some injured still hospitalized; the tertiary overview now gives 87. These competing and evolving totals are not reconciled as a final victim count. The original 94 cannot be certified merely by citing the earlier HRW report. Hostage duration and historical ranking also remain unsupported; the archived clarification opened successfully, while its original URL returned 404.

06-01.title: Dolphinarium Discotheque Bombing
06-01.description: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked outside the Dolphinarium discotheque in Tel Aviv on June 1, 2001, killing 21 other people, most of them teenagers, and injuring at least 120.

06-01.title: Nepalese Royal Palace Massacre
06-01.description: A shooting at Narayanhity Royal Palace in Kathmandu on 1 June 2001 ultimately left ten members of Nepal's royal family dead, including King Birendra, Queen Aishwarya and Crown Prince Dipendra. An official inquiry attributed the killings of nine relatives to Dipendra, who died on 4 June. Gyanendra succeeded him as king.

06-01.title: Southern Africa food crisis
06-01.description: Southern Africa faced a regional food and health emergency in 2002. WHO warned in August that the crisis could cause 300,000 additional deaths over the following six months; that was a projection, not a measured death toll. WFP later reported that relief helped prevent the food crisis from becoming a famine.

review.note: Critical: 300,000 was WHO's prospective warning of possible additional deaths, not observed mortality. Statements were issued in August/October, not 1 June. No defensible positive replacement toll or daily date established. Quarantine/remove from observed-death totals pending resolution; do not retain the projection as actual deaths.

06-02.title: Odisha train collision
06-02.description: On June 2, 2023, the Coromandel Express collided with a stationary freight train near Bahanaga Bazar in Odisha, and derailed coaches struck another passenger train. India's Ministry of Railways later reported 296 deaths. The disaster prompted investigations into signaling and railway safety failures.

06-03.title: Volcán de Fuego eruption
06-03.description: Guatemala's Volcán de Fuego erupted violently, sending pyroclastic flows and ash that buried the villages of San Miguel Los Lotes and El Rodeo in mud and rock. The eruption killed 425 people according to Guatemala's disaster agency (CONRED), injured hundreds, destroyed thousands of homes, and forced the evacuation of over 12,000 people, while dozens of victims were never recovered from the deposits.

review.note: June 3 eruption is established. The asserted 425 confirmed CONRED deaths is not established: reports variously combine recovered deaths and missing people, and the 2026 government-newspaper retrospective itself gives 429 dead plus 229 missing. Hundreds injured/thousands of homes destroyed also need final evidence. No numerical replacement proposed without reconciling categories.

06-03.title: Khartoum massacre
06-03.description: On 3 June 2019, Sudanese security forces, including the Rapid Support Forces, violently dispersed a civilian sit-in outside the army headquarters in Khartoum that had been demanding a transition to civilian rule. The Sudanese Doctors' Syndicate documented at least 104 deaths, with later tallies exceeding 128 including children, and hundreds of people wounded; an official inquiry reported 87 deaths. The crackdown followed the ouster of President Omar al-Bashir and preceded a power-sharing agreement that established a civilian-led transitional government later that year.

review.note: June 3 attack and RSF involvement supported. Amnesty distinguishes at least 100 in its estimate, 127 from Central Committee of Sudanese Doctors, 50 from a different doctors' syndicate, and 87 from attorney-general inquiry. Original 104/128 attribution conflates organizations and reporting intervals; exact canonical tally remains unresolved.

06-04.title: BM Container Depot fire and explosions (Sitakunda)
06-04.description: A fire broke out at the BM Container Depot near Sitakunda, Bangladesh, on 4 June 2022, igniting chemicals stored in shipping containers and triggering a series of massive explosions. At least 49 people were killed and more than 450 injured, many of them firefighters and workers who had tried to contain the initial blaze. The explosions hurled containers hundreds of metres, in one of Bangladesh's deadliest industrial accidents.

review.note: June 4 fire established. Initial 49 was explicitly corrected to 41 after a miscount; later secondary sources say at least 47. Need eventual reconciled death tally rather than reinstating erroneous initial total. More-than-450 injured and explosion-distance details also not established.

06-05.title: Solhan village massacre
06-05.description: Armed attackers struck Solhan in Burkina Faso early on June 5, 2021, killing civilians including children and forcing residents to flee. Contemporary reporting put the provisional toll at about 160; UNICEF reported more than 130 civilian deaths. The larger number is a reported estimate, not a reconciled final count.

06-07.title: Mindanao earthquake
06-07.description: On 8 June 2026, a magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck offshore Sarangani province, Mindanao, on the Cotabato Trench, killing at least 106 people (107 per final tallies) and injuring 1,320, with 7 missing. More than 121,000 homes were damaged or destroyed and damage exceeded ₱71 billion (US$1.44 billion). General Santos, Sarangani, South Cotabato and Davao Occidental were hardest hit, and coastal uplift of up to 2 metres damaged marine habitats across Sarangani Bay.

review.note: 07:37 local June 8 = 23:37 UTC June 7. Date-only correction; final 107 deaths, injuries/missing, housing totals, PHP 71bn loss and uplift claims remain unverified.

06-10.title: Osh ethnic violence in southern Kyrgyzstan
06-10.description: Four days of inter-ethnic violence between Kyrgyz and Uzbek communities erupted in Osh on June 10, 2010 and spread to Jalal-Abad, following the ouster of President Kurmanbek Bakiyev in April and a period of political instability. The Kyrgyz health ministry reported an official toll of about 312 dead and over 2,300 injured, while the International Crisis Group estimated up to 470 killed; interim leader Roza Otunbayeva said the true figure was likely around 2,000 because many victims were buried quickly per local tradition. Hundreds of thousands of ethnic Uzbeks fled across the border into Uzbekistan, and the U.N. reported whole districts of Osh burned to the ground.

review.note: 470 is associated with the Kyrgyzstan Inquiry Commission, not necessarily International Crisis Group. The CSCE page itself has a year typo in its retrospective paragraph. Exact source for 312/2,000 and cross-border versus total displacement needed; do not call these interchangeable final counts.

06-10.title: Tigray famine
06-10.description: Amid the war between Ethiopian federal forces and the Tigray People's Liberation Front, the United Nations declared a famine in parts of Tigray in June 2021 as an aid blockade prevented food from reaching millions of people. Research from Ghent University estimated that 162,000 to 191,000 people died from violence and starvation-related causes in Tigray between November 2020 and June 2022, most of them during 2021.

review.note: IPC explicitly says evidence did not support area-level Famine classification; household Catastrophe is different. 190,000 is not a measured June 2021 famine toll. Underlying Ghent estimate, cause categories, November 2020-June 2022 interval and 'most during 2021' require original study; do not label estimate a UN-declared famine's deaths.

06-12.title: Camp Speicher Massacre
06-12.description: From June 12 to at least June 14, 2014, Islamic State fighters killed about 1,700 soldiers, cadets and volunteers who had fled Tikrit Air Academy, known as Camp Speicher. UNITAD documented the mass killings in and around Tikrit's presidential palace complex.

review.note: Updated primary evidence gives about 1,700 soldiers, cadets and volunteers killed June 12 through at least June 14 near presidential palaces, not all at the base or all on June 12. Retain June 12 as start and 1,700 as approximation. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

06-12.title: Orlando Pulse nightclub shooting
06-12.description: A gunman attacked Pulse nightclub in Orlando in the early hours of June 12, 2016, killing 49 victims. The shooting became a hostage incident before police killed the attacker later that morning.

06-12.title: Air India Flight 171 crash
06-12.description: Air India Flight 171, a Boeing 787-8 bound for London Gatwick, crashed shortly after takeoff from Ahmedabad at about 08:09 UTC on June 12, 2025, striking B. J. Medical College hostel buildings. The official preliminary report records 241 deaths among 242 people aboard and 19 deaths on the ground.
sources: Ministry of Civil Aviation parliamentary answer

06-13.title: Grenfell Tower fire
06-13.description: A fire in a fourth-floor flat at Grenfell Tower in London spread through the building's combustible exterior cladding, killing 72 people. It was reported shortly before midnight UTC on June 13, 2017, June 14 locally.

06-13.title: Israel-Iran war (Twelve-Day War)
06-13.description: On June 13, 2025, Israel launched Operation Rising Lion, striking Iranian military and nuclear facilities and killing commanders and nuclear scientists; Iran responded with more than 550 ballistic missiles and over 1,000 drones fired at Israel over 12 days. Roughly 33 people were killed in Israel and about 1,060 in Iran, according to the respective authorities.

review.note: June 13-24 is supported, but 1,093 is not a reconciled total. The original roughly 1,060 in Iran is a July 7 official update; the spokesperson raised it to at least 1,062 on July 22. HRANA reported 1,190 using a separate casualty register. Reuters reports 28 killed in Israel, not the original 33; inclusion of indirect or later deaths is not established for the latter. Do not average competing counts or treat different reporting dates as final same-scope totals. The 550-plus missile claim is supported by AP, but the drone count was not established here. Withhold until the overall numeric toll and scope are resolved.

06-14.title: Pakistan floods
06-14.description: Monsoon flooding in Pakistan beginning in June 2022 affected more than 33 million people. UNICEF's retrospective reporting records 1,739 deaths and more than 2.2 million homes damaged or destroyed across the flood-affected areas.
sources: National Disaster Management Authority of Pakistan

review.note: 1,739 is a retrospective national total, not the toll on the June start date. UNICEF repeats the one-third-underwater claim, but mapped inundation summarized in the secondary source is substantially smaller; remove this disputed extent and unverified injury/climate details rather than assert them. June 14 is the flood-period anchor, not a one-day disaster. The exact June 14 onset anchor was not corroborated beyond the secondary summary; UNICEF establishes the June-to-seasonal disaster, not this precise day.

06-14.title: Hajj Extreme Heat Deaths
06-14.description: During the June 14-19, 2024 Hajj pilgrimage, extreme heat caused mass mortality among pilgrims in Saudi Arabia. WHO reported Saudi authorities' total of 1,301 deaths from heat exhaustion, with 83% among unauthorized pilgrims walking long distances. The toll covers the pilgrimage period, not a single day.
sources: Saudi Ministry of Municipalities and Housing

06-14.title: Shooting of Minnesota state legislators
06-14.location: Brooklyn Park and Champlin, Minnesota, United States
06-14.description: On June 14, 2025, Vance Boelter killed Minnesota Representative Melissa Hortman and her husband Mark at their Brooklyn Park home and wounded Senator John Hoffman and his wife Yvette in Champlin. After his arrest, he pleaded guilty to federal murder and related charges on June 11, 2026; the separate state prosecution remained pending as of September 21, 2026.

06-16.title: Uttarakhand floods and landslides
06-16.description: Heavy rain, flooding and landslides devastated Uttarakhand on June 16-17, 2013, particularly around Kedarnath. Thousands died or were reported missing and presumed dead, and large-scale rescue operations evacuated stranded residents and visitors. Official reports differ on the death and missing totals.

review.note: Government sources conflict materially: year-end MHA reports 580 dead plus over 5,526 missing, while NIDM lists 169 dead plus 4,021 presumed dead. Neither establishes 5,700 as an exact final fatality count or the surrounding-region 6,000 claim. June 16 is a period anchor, not a verified instantaneous UTC onset.

sources.name: India Ministry of Home Affairs, 2013 review

06-16.title: Mpondwe school massacre
06-16.description: An attack blamed on Allied Democratic Forces rebels at Mpondwe-Lhubiriha Secondary School in western Uganda on June 16, 2023 killed 42 people, according to a June 19 official update, including 37 students. Attackers set a dormitory on fire; victims also suffered gunshot and machete attacks.

06-18.title: Jerusalem bus 32A bombing
06-18.description: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked Egged bus 32A near Patt Junction in Jerusalem during the morning rush hour on 18 June 2002, killing 19 other people and wounding more than 70.

06-18.title: Charleston church shooting
06-18.description: Dylann Roof killed nine Black worshippers during a Bible study at Emanuel AME Church in Charleston on the evening of June 17, 2015, local time, or June 18 UTC. He was arrested the next day and later convicted on federal hate-crime charges and sentenced to death.

06-20.title: Typhoon Fengshen (Frank) and MV Princess of the Stars sinking
06-20.description: Typhoon Fengshen crossed the Philippines beginning on June 20, 2008, causing destructive flooding. During the storm, the ferry MV Princess of the Stars capsized near Sibuyan Island on June 21. Philippine disaster-agency reporting in July counted 557 deaths apart from the ferry disaster; a reconciled final combined toll is not established here.

review.note: The June 20 Philippine landfall is supported by HKO; June 25 was the later China landfall. NDCC reporting gives 557 deaths excluding the ferry (GMA, July 10), whereas ADRC's July 31 snapshot also lists 87 missing. The original 1,371, the ferry's asserted 800-850 deaths, and the Philippines/China aggregation were not reconciled with a final official passenger and casualty accounting. Do not add bodies recovered, presumed deaths and missing passengers indiscriminately. The shortened description removes the unsupported attribution of 1,371 to government/UN and the superlative; the numeric toll remains unresolved.

sources.name: Hong Kong Observatory: tropical cyclones in 2008
GMA News: NDCC damage and casualty report, July 10, 2008
Asian Disaster Reduction Center: Philippines typhoon record

06-21.title: Afghanistan Drought and Famine Crisis
06-21.description: Afghanistan's third consecutive year of severe drought brought the country to the brink of famine, with FAO and WFP reporting that about 5.5 million people faced severe food shortages by mid-2001. World Bank and UN officials warned of famine conditions and reported thousands of deaths from starvation and exposure, though the total death toll was never precisely counted.

review.note: FAO/WFP confirms a third drought year and famine risk. The 5.5 million assistance target is documented in September, not a specific 21 June incident. Neither a 5,000 death toll nor the asserted World Bank attribution is established.

06-21.title: Afghanistan earthquake (Khost and Paktika)
06-21.description: An earthquake struck Khost and Paktika in southeastern Afghanistan at 20:54 UTC on June 21, 2022, early June 22 locally. USGS lists magnitude 6.0. The UN's 2022 results report estimated 1,036 deaths, 2,924 injuries and damage to at least 4,500 homes.

06-22.title: Bou'in-Zahra earthquake
06-22.description: An earthquake struck the Avaj and Changureh area of northwestern Iran on June 22, 2002 at 02:58 UTC, severely damaging villages in Qazvin and neighboring regions. A disaster-science field report recorded about 261 deaths.
sources: Japan Society for Natural Disaster Science

06-23.title: Southern Peru Earthquake
06-23.description: A magnitude 8.4 earthquake struck off the coast of southern Peru, killing roughly 100 people and injuring more than 1,300, with most deaths in the Arequipa region. The quake triggered a tsunami that killed about two dozen people in the Camaná area and damaged or destroyed thousands of buildings, including historic structures in Arequipa.

review.note: USGS confirms 23 June, Mw 8.4, southern Peru and tsunami. EERI's initial assessment gives 77 dead, 68 missing and 2,713 wounded; the record mixes rounded and preliminary figures. Final deaths versus missing and tsunami subtotal require reconciliation before changing 100.

06-24.title: Karachi heat wave
06-24.description: A severe heatwave struck Karachi and other parts of Sindh in June 2015 during Ramadan. Karachi reached 44.8 C on June 20, and hospitals faced large numbers of heat-related patients. Death estimates changed rapidly and must distinguish the city from provincial or nationwide totals.

review.note: Heatwave predates June 24; PMD identifies June 19-23 and a Karachi maximum 44.8 C June 20. 49 C should not be attributed to Karachi. Neither final city toll 1,265 nor national 2,000 is established by these sources; original poverty and utilities attribution too categorical.

06-24.title: Surfside condominium collapse
06-24.description: The 12-storey Champlain Towers South condominium in Surfside, Florida, partially collapsed at about 01:30 local time on June 24, 2021, killing 98 people. NIST opened a technical investigation into the collapse.

06-24.title: 2026 Venezuela earthquakes
06-24.description: Two earthquakes, reported at magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5, struck north-central Venezuela on 24 June 2026, causing widespread destruction, particularly in La Guaira. Official figures cited by UNICEF recorded 6,125 deaths as of 3 August. Homes and infrastructure were damaged and many residents displaced.

06-25.title: Pacific Northwest heat dome
06-25.location: Pacific Northwest, United States and Canada
06-25.description: An exceptional heat dome pushed temperatures to records across the Pacific Northwest, with Lytton, British Columbia, reaching 49.6°C (121.3°F), Canada's hottest temperature ever recorded. The heat is estimated to have caused about 800 deaths or more across Canada and the U.S., mostly among elderly and vulnerable people in homes without air conditioning.

review.note: June 25-July 1 period, Lytton 49.6 C on June 29 and 619 heat-related BC deaths established. More than 800 investigated BC deaths is not the same as heat-attributed deaths. Need independent US/other-Canada totals and interval to substantiate combined about-800 figure and household demographics.

06-26.title: Cyclone Yemyin and Pakistan floods
06-26.description: Cyclone Yemyin made landfall on Pakistan's Makran coast on June 26, 2007, bringing torrential rain and flash floods that killed about 730 people in Balochistan, Sindh, and the North-West Frontier Province, with more than 100 killed in Afghanistan. Preceding heavy rain had already caused flooding and hundreds of deaths in Karachi.

review.note: 730 is a Pakistan-wide multistorm/flood figure in secondary summaries, not established as deaths from June26 Yemyin alone. IFRC documents storms fromJune23 and later flooding; final-report body retrieval failed. Need exact geographic/date scope and independently supported mortality before publication.

06-26.title: Sousse beach attack
06-26.description: A gunman attacked holidaymakers at the Imperial Marhaba hotel and beach at Port El Kantaoui near Sousse, Tunisia, shortly before midday on June 26, 2015. Thirty-eight victims were killed, including 30 British citizens.

review.note: Police confirms June 26 shortly before midday, 38 victims including 30 British. Remove unverified exact injury count and superlative; 38 excludes attacker. Midday Tunisia date unchanged UTC. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

sources.name: UK National Police Chiefs' Council, commemoration

06-28.title: Atatürk Airport attack
06-28.description: Three suicide attackers struck Istanbul's Ataturk Airport on June 28, 2016. Forty-five victims were killed, excluding the three attackers.

06-28.title: European heat waves
06-28.description: Record-breaking heat waves struck western Europe in late June and late July 2019, with France registering its highest-ever temperature of 45.9°C at Gallargues-le-Montueux on 28 June. France's public health agency attributed 1,435 excess deaths to the June heat wave, and a subsequent peer-reviewed study estimated roughly 2,500 deaths across Europe attributable to the summer's heat waves. Schools closed, rail services were suspended and cities opened cooling centres as authorities issued the highest heat alerts for the first time in several countries.

review.note: Confirmed national record is 46.0 C at Verargues June 28, not 45.9 C at Gallargues. The French mortality bulletin covers both June and July heatwaves. No identifiable peer-reviewed study supporting the claimed Europe-wide 2,500 total retrieved; replacement death scope must be settled before integration.

07-01.title: Uberlingen mid-air collision
07-01.description: A Bashkirian Airlines Tupolev Tu-154 carrying 69 people, including many children en route to a Spanish holiday, collided with a DHL cargo Boeing 757 over southern Germany. All 71 people on both aircraft died.
sources: German Federal Bureau of Aircraft Accident Investigation

07-01.title: Yangtze and Huaihe river floods
07-01.description: Seasonal floods along the Huaihe and Yangtze river basins in central and eastern China inundated large areas of Anhui, Jiangsu, and Henan provinces during the summer, killing about 1,551 people and affecting more than 100 million. It was the worst flooding in China since the 1998 Yangtze floods.

review.note: 1,551 is the nationwide annual flood total across 30 provincial-level areas, not an established Huaihe/Yangtze event toll. MFA reported 676 nationwide by July 20. July 1 onset and the Anhui-only location are unsupported for this aggregate. Must choose an event-specific scope and date before replacing the count.

07-01.title: Niger food crisis
07-01.description: Severe drought and a locust infestation triggered a food crisis in Niger affecting 3.6 million people, with UNICEF reporting 32,000 severely malnourished children under five facing death without treatment. A final death toll was never established; UN officials said thousands of children had already died, with overall mortality estimates ranging from several thousand to tens of thousands.

review.note: No checked source establishes 10,000 crisis-attributable deaths or a July 1 onset. UNICEF and the national mortality survey describe malnutrition, treatment and rates; children at risk are not observed fatalities. Do not infer a toll by multiplying treatment mortality or projected deaths. Numeric entry requires exclusion from aggregates pending evidence.

07-01.title: Yemen famine and cholera crisis
07-01.description: The war-ravaged country faced the world's worst humanitarian crisis in 2018: UN agencies reported 8.4 million people one step away from famine and over 22 million in need of assistance, while a massive cholera outbreak killed at least 2,315 people out of more than 1.1 million suspected cases recorded since the epidemic began in 2017. Port restrictions, collapsed health infrastructure, and food insecurity compounded the crisis, with the UN warning that parts of the country could slip into famine.

review.note: The outbreak and humanitarian crisis are established, but July 1 is not established as an event or reporting cutoff. The 2,315 total needs its exact WHO reporting interval; this is a cumulative cholera figure, not famine deaths or deaths on July 1. The outbreak began in 2016, with a major wave in April 2017.

07-01.title: India monsoon floods
07-01.description: The 2019 southwest monsoon caused severe and prolonged flooding across much of India between June and October, with more than 1,600 people killed in rain-related incidents according to reports citing official data. Bihar was among the hardest-hit states, along with Maharashtra, Kerala, Karnataka and Assam, and heavy flooding in the south coincided with torrential rain in Maharashtra's coastal districts. More than a million people were displaced, crops were destroyed and the floods followed unusually heavy August rainfall that came within weeks of drought in parts of the country.

review.note: Reuters supports more than 1,600 rain-related deaths since June by October 1, 2019, not deaths on July 1. Seasonal date anchor and displacement/geographic/detail claims remain incompletely supported. Needs a reporting cutoff rather than single-day presentation. Only one source was established in this batch, below the two-source publication minimum.

07-01.title: Majiya fuel tanker explosion
07-01.description: In early July 2019, a fuel tanker that had overturned near the village of Majiya in Jigawa State exploded, killing at least 48 people, many of whom had gathered to collect leaking fuel, and leaving dozens more hospitalised with severe burns. Local officials said most of the dead were burnt beyond recognition and the explosion also destroyed nearby properties. The incident highlighted the recurring danger of fuel collection at tanker crash sites across Nigeria, where fuel shortages have driven people to scoop up spilled petrol.

review.note: Search did not establish a July 2019 Majiya explosion killing 48. Primary investigation notice and AFP locate the major Majiya disaster on October 15, 2024 with much higher deaths. Likely conflation, but failed search alone is not proof of fabrication. Quarantine pending identity/date resolution; do not silently repurpose as 2024.

07-01.title: Irapuato rehabilitation center massacre
07-01.description: Three armed men attacked the Recuperando mi Vida rehabilitation centre in Irapuato, Guanajuato, on July 1, 2020. Later reporting put the death toll at 28. The killings occurred amid a series of attacks on rehabilitation centres in the state.

07-03.title: Karrada shopping district bombing
07-03.description: An Islamic State-claimed suicide bombing devastated Baghdad's Karrada shopping district shortly after midnight locally on July 3, 2016. Later reports attributed differing tolls of 323 and 324 to Iraqi authorities, after much lower preliminary counts.

review.note: Rudaw attributes 324 to the health minister on July 31, while same-period AFP reporting gives 323; both exceed the early 250/292 counts. The attack occurred shortly after midnight July 3 local time, meaning July 2 UTC; exact timing currently has only a tertiary source here. Later tertiary totals and a minister's reported much higher estimate also prevent treating 324 as an uncontested final toll. Proposed UTC shift requires stronger timing corroboration before publication.

07-04.title: Typhoon Utor (Feria)
07-04.description: Utor, known as Feria in the Philippines, passed northern Luzon on 4 July 2001 and caused destructive flooding and landslides. A subsequent monthly storm summary reported at least 168 deaths in the Philippines. The storm then struck southern China, where additional deaths occurred; those are not included in this Philippine toll.

07-04.title: Highland Park parade shooting
07-04.description: A gunman opened fire from a rooftop during the Independence Day parade in Highland Park, Illinois, on July 4, 2022, killing seven people and injuring dozens. Prosecutors subsequently brought 117 charges, including 21 first-degree murder counts covering the seven victims.

07-05.title: Russian heatwave and wildfires
07-05.description: A record-breaking heatwave in July and August 2010, the hottest in eastern Europe in 500 years, combined with massive wildfires and dense smog across western Russia, causing an estimated 55,000 excess deaths nationwide, according to the Center for Research on the Epidemiology of Disasters and peer-reviewed studies. In Moscow alone, an estimated 10,900 to 11,300 excess deaths occurred during the 44-day heat wave and accompanying smog episode, largely from cardiovascular and respiratory failure. The fires destroyed about one-third of Russia's grain harvest and caused roughly $15 billion in economic losses.
sources: Center for Research on the Epidemiology of Disasters (CRED)

review.note: Estimated summer excess mortality around 55,000 supported; WMO later lists 55,736. July 5 is not established as a unique onset date. Grain losses should not be attributed solely to fires rather than drought/heat. 44-day Moscow interval and $15 billion need dedicated sources.

07-05.title: 2016 China floods (Yangtze basin)
07-05.description: Torrential monsoon rains produced the worst flooding in China since 1998, hitting the Yangtze and Huai river basins across 26 provinces and affecting an estimated 32 million people, with hundreds of thousands left homeless. More than 350 people died in the floods, and a June 23 EF4 tornado in Jiangsu Province that killed at least 99 people brought the combined toll to more than 440. Rivers breached their banks in multiple provinces, including Hubei and Anhui, and damage was estimated in the tens of billions of dollars.

review.note: July 5 is a reporting date, not an established onset of the June-September flood season. The 449 total combines more than 350 flood deaths with 99 deaths in the separate June 23 Jiangsu tornado, inconsistent with the Yangtze flood title. TIME's July 5 report gives 186 dead and 45 missing as of the preceding Sunday, a preliminary count, not support for 449 flood deaths. Define flood period and geography before selecting date or final toll.

07-06.title: Krasnodar Krai flash floods
07-06.description: Heavy overnight rain caused deadly flooding in Russia's Krasnodar region on July 6-7, 2012. A flood wave reached Krymsk early on July 7 local time, or July 6 UTC. The regional death toll was 171.

07-06.title: Lac-Mégantic rail disaster
07-06.description: An unattended freight train carrying crude oil rolled downhill and derailed in Lac-Megantic, Quebec, at about 05:15 UTC on July 6, 2013. Spilled oil ignited, killing 47 people and destroying much of the town centre. Investigators found that the train had not been adequately secured.

review.note: Investigation gives July 6 about 01:15 EDT (05:15 UTC), 47 deaths, 72 loaded tank cars plus other rolling stock. Remove misleading 73-car shorthand and unsupported all-time Canadian ranking. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

sources.name: Transportation Safety Board of Canada, investigation

07-06.title: Western Japan floods and landslides
07-06.description: Heavy rainfall from late June through early July 2018 caused flooding and landslides across western Japan, especially Hiroshima, Okayama and Ehime. A published mortality analysis recorded 237 deaths, including 115 in Hiroshima Prefecture. The July 6 calendar entry falls within the multi-day disaster.

review.note: 225 is an early reported tally; published mortality analysis gives 237. JMA documents June 28-July 8 rainfall, including cumulative totals over 1,800 mm, not the asserted 180 mm/hour. July 6 is an anchor within the disaster, not all deaths on that date. The precise July 6 calendar date remains an unestablished selection within a June 28-July 8 rainfall episode; explaining it as an anchor does not verify it as the event date.

07-07.title: London bombings (7/7)
07-07.description: Four suicide bombers attacked three London Underground trains and a bus on July 7, 2005. The attacks killed 52 people, excluding the bombers, and injured more than 770.

07-07.title: Indian embassy bombing in Kabul
07-07.description: A suicide vehicle bombing struck the Indian embassy in Kabul on the morning of July 7, 2008. India's foreign ministry identified four Indian officials and one Afghan embassy employee among those killed. UNAMA subsequently recorded 55 civilian deaths; reported overall totals differ.

review.note: July 7 morning and the embassy identity are supported by MEA. Four Indian officials and one Afghan employee were killed, so four Indian staff is not the entire embassy-staff toll. MEA's 2008-09 annual report says about 60 Afghan nationals plus five embassy personnel; UNAMA's annual report counts 55 civilians, while secondary accounts give 58 overall. These differing populations and totals cannot be assumed equivalent. A previously indexed 2010 MEA PDF returned a 404 on opening and is not treated as primary verification of 58. Removed unsupported police/child subtotals, queue composition and superlative; overall toll remains unresolved.

sources.name: Ministry of External Affairs: annual report 2008-2009
Ministry of External Affairs: foreign relations 2008, July 7 statement
UNAMA: protection of civilians annual report 2008
Wikipedia: 2008 Indian embassy bombing, secondary comparison

07-08.title: Sudan Airways Flight 139 crash
07-08.description: Sudan Airways Flight 139, a Boeing 737, crashed near Port Sudan on July 8, 2003, killing 116 of its 117 occupants. After an engine failed following takeoff, the crew returned toward the airport; the aircraft struck terrain on approach in limited visibility.

07-08.title: Gaza War (Operation Protective Edge)
07-08.description: The Gaza conflict lasted from July 8 to August 26, 2014. UNRWA records 2,251 Palestinian deaths, including 1,462 believed to be civilians, among them 551 children, and 11,231 Palestinian injuries. The numeric toll here is Palestinian-only and does not include deaths on the Israeli side.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

review.note: Original children count 540 should be 551 for the cited 2,251/1,462 dataset. Israeli-side counts differ between OCHA pages (67 soldiers plus six civilians versus 66 plus five Israeli civilians); do not silently merge them. 2,251 is Palestinian-only across July 8-August 26, not all conflict deaths. Exact UTC onset unestablished.

07-08.title: Dallas police ambush
07-08.description: A gunman attacked police during a protest in Dallas on the evening of July 7, 2016, July 8 UTC. Five officers were killed and nine officers were wounded.

07-10.title: Victory declared in Mosul
07-10.description: Iraq declared victory over Islamic State in Mosul on July 10, 2017, while some fighting continued. An Associated Press investigation estimated 9,000-11,000 civilian deaths in the campaign from October 2016 to July 2017. The numeric toll is an approximate midpoint of that estimate.
sources: PBS interview with Associated Press investigator

07-11.title: Mumbai train bombings
07-11.description: Seven explosions struck suburban trains on Mumbai's Western Line during the evening rush hour on July 11, 2006. Later court reporting gives 189 deaths, differing from the 209 figure in some earlier accounts. Responsibility and the prosecution evidence have been disputed in court.

review.note: Modern court coverage gives189 deaths/824 injured rather than209. The High Court rejected the prosecution case in July2025; subsequent Supreme Court stay did not itself establish guilt. Remove asserted pressure-cooker mechanism and categorical attribution; final victim count requires reconciliation.

07-11.title: Kampala World Cup bombings
07-11.description: Three suicide bombs exploded in Kampala on July 11, 2010, while crowds watched the FIFA World Cup final, killing 74 people and injuring over 70. Two devices were detonated at the Kyadondo Rugby Club and one at the Ethiopian Village restaurant. The Somali militant group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility, stating the attacks were retaliation for Uganda's participation in the African Union peacekeeping mission in Somalia (AMISOM), marking the first major Al-Shabaab attack outside Somalia.

review.note: July 11 Kampala venues corroborated. Reports use both 74 and 76 and differ in preliminary reporting; final victim/attacker scope not resolved. Three devices must not automatically be described as three suicide bombers.

07-12.title: 2006 Lebanon War
07-12.description: The war between Israel and Hezbollah lasted from July 12 to August 14, 2006. Human Rights Watch reported at least 1,109 deaths in Lebanon, mostly civilians, and about one million displaced people. The recorded toll is for Lebanon only; Israeli deaths are not included.

07-13.title: Mumbai triple bombings
07-13.description: On July 13, 2011, three improvised explosive devices hidden on a parked motorcycle, in a tiffin box and on an electric pole exploded within 11 minutes at crowded commercial locations in Mumbai: Zaveri Bazaar, Opera House and Dadar. The blasts killed 26 people and injured more than 130 during evening rush hour. No group claimed responsibility initially; investigations linked the attack to the Indian Mujahideen network, and authorities later named co-founder Yasin Bhatkal as the alleged mastermind.

review.note: Secondary result supports date, three sites and 26/130 figures but not independently verified device placements, 11-minute chronology or alleged mastermind. Need original investigation or reputable final-toll reporting before certification. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

07-13.title: Mastung election rally bombing
07-13.description: A suicide bomber attacked a Balochistan Awami Party election rally near Mastung, Pakistan, on July 13, 2018. A subsequent official tally reported by Reuters put the deaths at 149, including candidate Siraj Raisani. Islamic State claimed responsibility.

07-14.title: Tropical Storm Bilis floods and landslides in China
07-14.description: Severe Tropical Storm Bilis made landfall on mainland China on July 14, 2006. Its prolonged rainfall caused extensive flooding and landslides across southern China. A meteorological study citing the China Meteorological Administration reports at least 843 deaths.

07-14.title: Nice Bastille Day truck attack
07-14.description: A truck was driven into crowds celebrating Bastille Day on Nice's Promenade des Anglais on July 14, 2016. Eighty-six people were killed and hundreds were injured. Police killed the driver.

07-14.title: Western European floods
07-14.description: Unprecedented rainfall caused devastating flash floods in western Germany, particularly the Ahr and Erft valleys, and eastern Belgium along the Vesdre river. Around 240 people died, roughly 189 of them in Germany, with dozens more killed in Belgium and other neighboring countries. Thousands lost homes, and scientists linked the extreme rainfall to climate change.

review.note: July event/weather mechanisms supported. Final geographic death totals vary across updates: secondary totals reach 243 including 196 Germany, not 189. Need primary final country breakdown and attribution study before replacing broad 240 estimate.

07-15.title: North Korea floods and food crisis
07-15.description: Floods struck several North Korean provinces in July 2006, damaging homes, farmland and infrastructure. Published death and missing-person counts differed widely, and independent assessment was limited.
sources: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC)

review.note: 600 conflates uncertain killed/missing reporting. Sources range from Red Cross151 dead to a pro-North Korean newspaper's549 dead/295 missing; outside claims are unverified. WFP describes assistance stocks used for2006 floods, so blanket rejection of relief is misleading. Exact episode onset and toll remain unresolved.

07-15.title: Typhoon Rammasun
07-15.description: Typhoon Rammasun crossed the Philippines in mid-July 2014, then intensified over the South China Sea before striking southern China and affecting Vietnam. It caused widespread deaths and damage; country totals changed as assessments continued.

review.note: HKO's early figures are at least 98 Philippine deaths and 18 in China; secondary later totals are higher. A consistent final three-country 190 toll is not established. Strongest Philippine typhoon in decades is false after Haiyan in 2013. July 15 is landfall anchor, but precise UTC onset not checked.

07-15.title: Attempted coup in Turkey
07-15.description: A faction of Turkey's armed forces attempted to overthrow the government on the night of July 15, 2016, with violence in Ankara and Istanbul. The attempt failed. Later official commemorations count 251 people killed opposing the coup, a narrower scope than totals including coup participants.

review.note: July 15-16 attempted coup in Ankara and Istanbul is supported. Later Turkish commemoration counts 251 people killed opposing the coup, excluding coup participants; HRW reported at least 241 citizens/security personnel earlier. Neither establishes a consistently scoped combined toll of 300 or the claimed 180 civilians. Later injury counts also vary. Keep the core toll unresolved rather than silently substitute a loyalist-only count.

07-15.title: 2022 European heatwaves
07-15.description: A Nature Medicine study estimated 61,672 heat-related deaths across 35 European countries between May 30 and September 4, 2022, with a 95% confidence interval of 37,643-86,807. A later methodological study inferred roughly 70,066 deaths for the full year, a different time scope. These are statistical estimates, not individually confirmed deaths.
sources: Barcelona Institute for Global Health (Nature Medicine)

review.note: 61,672 is a modeled summer estimate for May 30-September 4, not a July 15 toll. The first study's annual estimate was 62,862; the later paper inferred 70,066 for the whole year, not an interchangeable revised summer count. Use the defined study-period start and omit unresearched national temperature records. May 30 is the documented study-interval start, not a verified discrete heat-disaster date. The corrected estimate and interval are supported, but the single-day calendar representation needs resolution before publication.

07-17.title: Pangandaran earthquake and tsunami
07-17.description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake off Java on July 17, 2006, generated a tsunami that struck about 300 kilometres of southern coastline, including Pangandaran. A field-survey study reports 668 deaths, 65 people missing and 9,299 receiving medical treatment.

07-17.title: Malaysia Airlines Flight MH17 Shootdown
07-17.description: Malaysia Airlines Flight MH17 was shot down over eastern Ukraine on July 17, 2014, killing all 298 passengers and crew. Dutch investigations concluded that a Buk surface-to-air missile was fired from separatist-controlled territory. A Dutch court convicted three men for their roles in the downing.
sources: District Court of The Hague, judgment transcript

07-18.title: Second siege of Monrovia
07-18.description: LURD rebels besieged the Liberian capital Monrovia from June to August 2003, shelling civilian neighborhoods, churches, and schools and killing an estimated 1,000 to 1,500 civilians. The siege ended when President Charles Taylor went into exile and international peacekeepers arrived.
sources: UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights

review.note: Sources describe several June-July offensives and a July 18-August siege, not a clearly named second siege with a 1,500 final civilian toll. HRW documents hundreds killed and over 2,000 injured, while the summary gives 1,000 killed. Dates, episode naming and civilian estimate need reconciliation.

07-20.title: Horn of Africa famine in Somalia
07-20.description: The UN declared famine in parts of southern Somalia on July 20, 2011. A FAO/FSNAU and FEWS NET study published in 2013 estimated approximately 258,000 excess deaths from severe food insecurity between October 2010 and April 2012, including about 133,000 children under five. Estimated mortality peaked at about 30,000 excess deaths per month from May through August 2011.

07-20.title: Aurora theater shooting
07-20.description: A gunman attacked a midnight screening of The Dark Knight Rises at a movie theater in Aurora, Colorado, on July 20, 2012, killing 12 people and injuring 70. James Holmes was convicted and in 2015 received 12 consecutive life sentences without parole, plus additional prison terms.

07-20.title: Syrian civil war — 2012 escalation
07-20.description: The Syrian civil war escalated dramatically in 2012, from protests to full-scale urban warfare including the Battle of Aleppo from July. Monitors estimated about 50,000 people were killed during the year alone (SOHR's year-by-year count was 52,916, including 22,663 civilians), and the UN reported more than 60,000 cumulative deaths since March 2011 by early 2013; massacres such as Houla and Daraya and indiscriminate shelling of civilian areas accounted for a large share of casualties.

review.note: July 20 anchors Aleppo escalation but the numeric field is a rounded annual estimate. SOHR retrospective revisions differ from contemporaneous totals. Need dated primary SOHR/UN series and explicit annual-versus-cumulative scope; Houla/Daraya records overlap this aggregate.

07-20.title: Henan floods
07-20.description: Torrential rains struck Henan from July 17 to 23, 2021, with severe flooding in Zhengzhou on July 20. A subsequent State Council investigation recorded 398 people dead or missing across the province, 380 of them in Zhengzhou. Fourteen people died in the subway flooding. The 398 figure is a combined dead-and-missing toll.

review.note: 398 includes dead and missing across July 17-23, 95.5% (380) in Zhengzhou. Subway deaths were 14, not dozens. 302 is an earlier provincial figure wrongly assigned to Zhengzhou. The reported combined category does not establish 398 confirmed deaths. Withhold the numeric deaths-bearing row until missing-versus-dead accounting is resolved; the July 20 Zhengzhou flooding itself is established.

07-21.title: Beijing floods
07-21.description: Exceptional rain on July 21-22, 2012, caused severe flooding in Beijing. It was the city's heaviest rainfall in 61 years. Later assessments reported 79 deaths, at least 8,200 homes destroyed and approximately 11.6 billion yuan in losses.

07-22.title: Sharm el-Sheikh bombings
07-22.description: Bombs struck Sharm el-Sheikh shortly after 01:00 on July 23, 2005, local time, July 22 UTC. Targets included the Old Market and a hotel. Death reports differed: the official count was 64, while hospitals reported 88.

review.note: 01:15 Egyptian summer time July 23 equals 22:15 UTC July 22. IFRC's later report uses 64 deaths and 124 injured, while hospital-based accounts reported 88 and 200. Correct UTC date but retain fatality conflict explicitly.

07-22.title: Norway terror attacks (Oslo bombing and Utoya massacre)
07-22.description: On July 22, 2011, Anders Behring Breivik killed eight people in a bombing in Oslo and 69 in a shooting attack on a youth camp on Utoya, for 77 victims in total. He was convicted and sentenced to preventive detention initially set at 21 years, extendable if he remained dangerous.

07-22.title: Munich Olympia shopping mall shooting
07-22.description: A gunman killed nine people at and near Munich's Olympia shopping centre on July 22, 2016, before killing himself. The city officially commemorates the attack as racist and right-wing terrorism. The toll excludes the attacker.

07-23.title: Colombo Airport Attack
07-23.description: LTTE suicide commandos attacked Bandaranaike International Airport and the adjoining air force base near Colombo, killing at least 18 people and destroying or damaging 11-13 aircraft, including several SriLankan Airlines jets. The attack caused an estimated $350 million in losses to the national carrier alone.

review.note: Early reporting gave at least 18 including attackers; later accounts give seven servicemen and 14 attackers. The original does not define its scope and aircraft-loss figures vary. The documented 03:50 local start on 24 July is 23 July UTC (Sri Lanka then UTC+6). Proposed date/location only; resolve toll and damage claims before integration.

07-23.title: Kabul twin bombing of Hazara demonstration
07-23.description: Two suicide bombers attacked a peaceful demonstration at Kabul's Deh Mazang square on July 23, 2016. UNAMA documented 85 civilian deaths and 413 injuries. Islamic State's local affiliate claimed responsibility.
sources: UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan, 2016 annual civilian protection report

07-24.title: Air Algérie Flight 5017 Crash
07-24.description: Air Algerie Flight 5017, operated by Swiftair with an MD-83, crashed near Gossi, Mali, at about 01:47 UTC on July 24, 2014, roughly half an hour after leaving Ouagadougou. All 110 passengers and six crew died. Investigators linked loss of speed and an unrecovered stall to probable ice obstruction of engine pressure sensors and the crew's response.

review.note: Final report supersedes inconsistent BEA landing-page metadata: 110 passengers plus six crew, July 24 at 01:47, takeoff about 01:15. Thus about half an hour, not about an hour. Ice likely obstructed engine pressure sensors, not simply airframe icing. Remove unsupported airline ranking. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

sources.name: Mali investigation commission, final report hosted by BEA

07-24.title: Angara Airlines Flight 2311 crash
07-24.description: On July 24, 2025, an Angara Airlines Antonov An-24 operating Flight 2311 crashed near Tynda in Russia's Amur region while approaching its destination. All 42 passengers and six crew members died.

07-25.title: 2011 Thailand floods
07-25.description: Torrential monsoon rains from late July 2011 triggered the worst flooding in Thailand in more than half a century, affecting 65 of the country's 77 provinces and about 13.6 million people over more than five months. Official figures recorded 815 deaths and three missing. Floodwaters inundated Bangkok's outskirts and submerged large parts of the central plains, destroying millions of acres of crops and crippling the country's industrial estates, including hard-disk drive and automobile factories, with total economic damages estimated at around US$45 billion.
sources: Thai Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation

review.note: 815 dead, 13.6 million affected and 65 provinces corroborated in later World Bank account. July 25 exact onset and three missing not established. $46.5 billion is damage plus economic losses, not physical damage alone; earlier World Bank snapshots use different tolls.

07-26.title: Mumbai floods
07-26.description: Exceptional rain on July 26-27, 2005, caused severe flooding in Mumbai and other parts of Maharashtra. The Santacruz observatory measured 944 mm over 24 hours. Reported mortality totals differ in geographic and flood-related disease coverage.

review.note: 944 mm is the Santacruz station's 24-hour measurement, not citywide rainfall. 1,094 is commonly a Maharashtra-wide count, while some papers incorrectly or differently label it Mumbai-only; NIDM distinguishes municipal deaths. Establish regional/flood-versus-disease scope before accepting exact toll.

07-26.title: Ahmedabad serial bombings
07-26.description: A series of bombings in Ahmedabad on July 26, 2008 killed 56 people and injured more than 200. The targets included hospitals. In February 2022, a special court sentenced 38 defendants to death and 11 to life imprisonment in the bombing case.
sources: The Indian Express: Ahmedabad bombing sentences, February 18, 2022
Ministry of Home Affairs: tribunal order published August 6, 2024

07-26.title: Gansu flash flood at Weiyuan scenic area
07-26.description: A flash flood struck a scenic area in Weiyuan County, Dingxi City, on the afternoon of 26 July 2026, killing 25 people and injuring 23. China's national disaster commission said it would oversee an investigation into the disaster and urged Gansu Province to strengthen disaster prevention, mitigation and relief capacity.

07-27.title: Sknyliv air show disaster
