08-14.description: A Russian guided-bomb attack damaged an apartment building in Kramatorsk, killing one person and injuring others. Reports published August 14 described an overnight strike, with the reported injury count later rising to 22.

review.note: The attack is in Kramatorsk and one death is supported. Injury reports increased from 16/17 to 22. Overnight timing leaves August 13 versus 14 UTC unresolved. Omit the precise floors-destroyed count rather than retain an unchecked structural detail.

08-14.title: Series of shootings in Michigan kills six including gunman
08-14.description: Five people were killed in shootings in Missaukee County on August 14, and suspect Chad Hickman, 39, was later found dead. Police found victims at two homes and in woods near Whitlock Lake; another person was critically injured. The six-death total includes the suspect.

08-14.title: Toxic gas at Sitakunda shipbreaking yard kills ten workers
08-14.description: Workers at Ferdous Steel's Sitakunda shipbreaking yard were exposed to toxic gas inside a vessel on August 14. Authorities identified hydrogen sulfide. The reported death toll rose to ten after another worker died in hospital on August 19.

08-15.title: Peru earthquake
08-15.description: A magnitude 8.0 earthquake struck off central Peru on August 15, 2007, severely damaging Pisco and nearby communities and producing a tsunami. A USGS-funded research report cites an October 2007 Peruvian statistical count of 595 deaths, with missing people listed separately.

review.note: USGS-supported research report cites595 deaths plus318 missing as an October2 INEI figure; these are separate categories. Other summaries repeat519, so attribute595 explicitly rather than universal final count. Replace85percent destroyed with supported general damage; date23:40UTC unchanged. The differing 519/595 accounts have not been reconciled by reporting period and finalization; the attributed candidate prose does not by itself establish final mortality. Withhold pending that reconciliation.

08-15.title: Kerala floods
08-15.description: Monsoon flooding and landslides devastated Kerala in August 2018. A case study hosted by the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority reports over 483 deaths and about one million evacuees, with 35 dams opened. Other assessments use different reporting intervals and totals; these deaths did not all occur on August 15.

review.note: Over 100 dams is wrong: state-hosted case study gives 35, UNDP 37. Report intervals produce 433 versus 483 deaths. Preserve 483 only as the broader case-study tally and make multi-day scope clear. The precise August 15 calendar anchor remains unestablished within the multi-day flood period; retain the supported prose correction but withhold until the date/period representation is resolved.

08-15.title: Flash flood and landslide in Ponferrada area kill two women
08-15.description: A flash flood and debris flow struck Manzanedo de Valdueza and nearby settlements in the Ponferrada area on August 15, killing two women. Four other people, including two children, were injured. An elderly man initially missing was found unharmed.

08-15.title: Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon kill 11 including women and children
08-15.description: Lebanon's Health Ministry reported eleven deaths in Israeli strikes on Ansar and Deir Zahrani during the night leading into August 15 local time: seven in Ansar, including three children, and four in Deir Zahrani. Nineteen people were reported wounded.

review.note: The ministry's eleven deaths (seven Ansar, four Deir Zahrani) and nineteen wounded are supported. Accounts describe overnight/dawn strikes without enough precise timing for both sites to assign one UTC date. Strip ancillary flight, building-height and condemnation details, but retain the date blocker.

08-15.title: Israeli forces kill 14-year-old Palestinian in Khan Younis
08-15.description: Fourteen-year-old Suhail Masoud Shalouf was shot by Israeli forces on al-Tina Street south of Khan Younis on the evening of August 15, according to WAFA. The Palestinian Red Crescent recovered his body the following day.

08-15.title: Polish tourist bus overturns on Hungarian motorway killing 12
08-15.description: A bus carrying 57 Polish passengers and two drivers overturned on Hungary's M3 motorway near Mezokeresztes at about 01:00 local time on August 16, killing 12 people. Emergency services later reported 47 injured, including 10 seriously. Police detained the driver.

08-15.title: Russian drone strike on Marhanets kills three-month-old baby
08-15.description: Russian forces struck a multi-storey building in Marhanets, Dnipropetrovsk region, with drones during a nighttime attack, killing a three-month-old boy and injuring 11 people, including children, according to regional military administration chief Oleksandr Hanzha. Rescue and clearance operations continued at the site.

review.note: The three-month-old boy's death and eleven injured, including two children, are supported. The official account says nighttime; no strike time was located to distinguish August 14 and 15 UTC.

08-15.title: Shooting at Lexington, Kentucky park kills one and injures four
08-15.description: A shooting during the East End Day gathering at Charles Young Park in Lexington on August 15 killed sixteen-year-old Di'Zhon Robertson and wounded four people, including children. Police responded shortly before 7 p.m. local time.

08-16.title: Historic flooding in Indiana kills seven
08-16.description: Days of severe storms and record-setting rainfall produced historic flooding across Indiana, killing at least seven people by August 16, with the White River cresting at record levels and the National Guard assisting rescues. Dozens of people were rescued from vehicles and homes as rivers overflowed across the state.

review.note: Seven is a cumulative storm/flood-related toll reported August 16, not seven deaths necessarily occurring that day. NWS places the rainfall/flood episode earlier in the week. This overlaps the August 12 Midwest three-death record, which already includes Indiana victims. Resolve incident boundaries, direct/indirect deaths and duplicate victims before publication.

08-16.title: Landslide hits apartment in Geoje, South Korea, killing one
08-16.location: Okpo-dong, Geoje, South Gyeongsang, South Korea
08-16.description: A rain-triggered landslide struck a ground-floor apartment in Okpo-dong, Geoje, early on August 17 local time. Three people were rescued; one subsequently died. The other two survived.

08-16.title: Russian attack on Kryvyi Rih kills two
08-16.description: An overnight Russian missile and drone attack on Kryvyi Rih damaged industrial facilities. Regional authorities later reported two people killed and fourteen injured after another body was recovered on the morning of August 16.

review.note: Later regional reporting updates one dead/six injured to two dead/fourteen injured. The 04:25 time is a casualty update, not necessarily the strike time. August 15 versus 16 UTC remains unresolved for the overnight attack.

08-16.title: Ukrainian attacks across Russia reportedly kill six
08-16.location: Moscow region and other areas, Russia
08-16.description: Russian authorities reported at least six deaths after widespread overnight Ukrainian drone attacks reported August 16. Attacks affected the Moscow region and other areas, including industrial and energy facilities.

review.note: The six reported deaths and Russian claims of hundreds of drones are supported, but this is an overnight multi-region aggregate without UTC incident times. Do not infer occurrence date from the August 16 release or independently validate the claimed interception count/ranking. Resolve the fatal incidents before publishing a single-date total.

08-16.title: Wildfires on Salamina kill two
08-16.description: An elderly couple died during wildfires on Salamina on August 16. Fires broke out around midday in Peristeria and Selinia, prompting evacuations, including hundreds of people taken off the island by sea.

08-17.title: Pickup-truck collision on Gwalior-Bhind highway kills eight labourers
08-17.description: A pickup carrying migrant labourers collided with a dumper truck near Chhimka in Bhind district around 01:00 local time on August 18. Eight people were killed and numerous others injured.

08-17.title: Russian drone strike on Dniprovska mine near Pavlohrad kills one worker
08-17.location: Bohdanivske, Pavlohrad district, Dnipropetrovsk region, Ukraine
08-17.description: Russian drones struck the Dniprovska mine in the Bohdanivske community of Dnipropetrovsk region on August 17, killing one employee and injuring another, according to DTEK and local reporting.

08-17.title: School shooting in Zamboanga City leaves two dead, including attacker
08-17.description: A student shot another student and then himself at Ateneo de Zamboanga University's junior high school campus in Zamboanga City on the morning of August 18 local time. Police and the university confirmed two deaths, including the attacker.

08-17.title: Ukrainian missile strikes on Koloskovo in Belgorod region kill six
08-17.location: Koloskovo, Valuysky district, Belgorod region, Russia
08-17.description: Russian regional authorities reported that a Ukrainian missile attack on Koloskovo in Belgorod region killed six people and injured four, including a child. The announcement was made on August 17; the precise UTC date of the attack remains unestablished.

review.note: The August 17 morning announcement supports six reported deaths and four injuries but does not establish whether the strike was before or after midnight UTC. Border distance is 15 miles, about 24 km, not 15 km. Short proposed prose removes the unsupported distance and burning detail; date remains unresolved.

08-18.title: Gold mine collapse on Cameroon-CAR border kills over 100 miners
08-18.description: An artisanal gold mine collapsed at Zamboye near the Cameroon border on August 18. Local reporting attributed 107 recovered bodies to Garoua-Boulai's mayor; AP reported more than 100 deaths, while CAR authorities said the exact toll was still being established.

review.note: CAR authorities locate the mine in their territory; some initial Cameroonian reports mislocate it. The 107 figure is the Garoua-Boulai mayor's provisional recovery account, not a final CAR-confirmed count. CAR prosecutors said the exact total was still being determined. Retain that contradiction explicitly; final toll is unresolved.

08-18.title: Israeli airstrike on cafe near Gaza Port kills six
08-18.description: An Israeli strike hit a crowded seaside cafe near Gaza City's fishing port on August 18, killing six Palestinians, including a child, according to medical and eyewitness reports.

08-18.title: Russian missile strike on Pechenihy in Kharkiv region kills ten
08-18.description: A Russian missile strike hit the centre of Pechenihy in Kharkiv region on the morning of August 18, killing ten people, Ukrainian officials said. Shops, a post office and residential buildings were damaged, and numerous people were injured.

08-19.title: Canal Hotel (UN Baghdad headquarters) bombing
08-19.description: A suicide truck bombing struck the Canal Hotel, the UN headquarters in Baghdad, on August 19, 2003. It killed 22 people, including UN special representative Sergio Vieira de Mello and other UN staff.

08-19.title: Abidjan toxic waste dumping (Probo Koala)
08-19.description: Waste discharged from the Probo Koala was dumped by a local contractor at multiple sites around Abidjan on August 19, 2006. UNEP records more than 100,000 medical consultations afterward. Reported death counts and the extent of medically established causal links differ between sources.

review.note: UNEP describes528 cubic metres and12 sites, Amnesty at least18 sites and an official15-death report, while17 appears in later government-attributed summaries. More than100,000 consultations are not proof of100,000 poisoning hospitalizations. Exact mortality and causal attribution remain unsettled; preserve distinctions.

08-19.title: Les Issers police academy suicide bombing
08-19.description: A vehicle bombing outside the gendarmerie training school at Les Issers on August 19, 2008 struck people waiting for an entrance examination. Algeria's Interior Ministry reported 43 victims killed, comprising 42 civilians and one police officer, and 45 people injured.
sources: Amnesty International: Les Issers and Bouira bombings
AFP via La Depeche: Les Issers bombing, August 19, 2008
EFE via Listin Diario: preliminary report of 44 deaths

08-19.title: Baghdad Ministry Bombings
08-19.description: On August 19, 2009, coordinated truck bombings hit the Iraqi Foreign Ministry and Finance Ministry in Baghdad, along with other explosions, killing at least 95 people and wounding about 563 according to Iraqi Interior Ministry officials. The attacks, blamed on al-Qaeda-linked militants and Baathist elements, were the bloodiest day in Baghdad since February 2008 and the worst since US troops withdrew from Iraqi cities at the end of June 2009.

review.note: Reuters photograph corroborates ministry attack and August 19 date. The searches did not independently establish 95/563, the comparative superlatives or final perpetrator attribution; BBC access was blocked. Keep unverified until a casualty report is checked. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

08-19.title: Fire in commercial building in Qinhuangdao kills eight
08-19.description: A fire broke out in a ground-floor commercial property in Haigang district, Qinhuangdao, at about 03:40 local time on August 20. Eight people were killed and three injured. The fire was extinguished and its cause was under investigation.

08-19.title: Torrential rains in southwest China kill ten
08-19.description: Torrential rains across southwest China killed 10 people and forced thousands to evacuate, with flooding and landslides reported across the region. Officials warned that disaster risk remained high as further heavy rainfall was forecast, and emergency response teams were deployed to affected areas.

review.note: August 19 is publication date. Ten combines five in a Guangxi construction-site landslide on Monday August 17 and five in a Changning, Sichuan banquet-wall collapse at 17:30 CST August 18. This is not one August 19 incident. Preserve the aggregate in audit; split/reconcile actual incidents before publication. The Guangxi incident's precise UTC timing remains unestablished.

08-20.title: Charter plane crash in western Alaska kills all eight on board
08-20.description: A charter aircraft crashed near a remote radar facility in western Alaska on August 20, 2026, killing all eight people on board. The US Air Force confirmed there were no survivors, and rescue teams faced difficult access to the crash site.

08-21.title: Azizabad airstrike
08-21.description: A US-led operation struck Azizabad in Herat Province at approximately 02:00 local time on August 22, 2008 (August 21 UTC). UNAMA's annual report subsequently counted 92 civilian deaths, including 62 children. The civilian death toll remained disputed between investigations.

review.note: AIHRC places the attack at approximately 02:00 Afghanistan time on August 22, corresponding to August 21 UTC; propose the UTC correction without changing the original identity key. UNAMA's later annual report gives 92 civilian deaths including 62 children, not the initial 90/60, while the US investigation reported 33. The competing investigations have not been reconciled and 90 cannot be certified as a final total. Remove unverified compensation and aircraft detail, retain the contradiction in notes, and withhold the row pending a settled toll policy/evidence.

sources.name: Afghanistan Independent Human Rights Commission: report submitted to UN Human Rights Council
UNAMA: protection of civilians annual report 2008
Wikipedia: Azizabad airstrike, competing investigation totals

08-21.title: Daraya massacre
08-21.description: Between 20 and 25 August 2012, Syrian government forces and allied militiamen carried out a mass killing in the town of Darayya near Damascus after a siege and an offer of safe passage. SOHR documented about 320 killed and the opposition reported up to 400 bodies found in homes, streets, and a mosque; a later UN Commission of Inquiry found reasonable grounds that the murders constituted war crimes.

review.note: Sources place shelling from August 20 and mass killings mainly August 24-26; August 21 has no established identity role. Reported totals vary widely. Safe-passage claim and exact UN legal finding not established; source-specific estimate and date interval needed.

08-21.title: Ghouta chemical weapons attack
08-21.description: Sarin attacks struck opposition-held areas of Ghouta near Damascus in the early hours of August 21, 2013, local time. UN investigators confirmed chemical-weapons use. Human Rights Watch's analysis attributed the attacks to Syrian government forces. Death estimates vary and should not be presented as a confirmed count.

review.note: UN confirmed chemical-weapons use but was not mandated to assign responsibility. HRW attributes the attacks to government forces. Reported early-morning local attacks may begin August 20 UTC; exact onset must be extracted before changing the date. Fatality estimates vary substantially, so 1,400 is not a confirmed exact toll.

08-22.title: Typhoon Bilis
08-22.description: Typhoon Bilis made landfall in southern Taiwan on August 22, 2000 before crossing toward mainland China. NOAA reports winds of about 258 km/h and more than 70 deaths across Taiwan and mainland China.

review.note: NOAA supports 22 August landfall, winds over 200 km/h and over 70 deaths in Taiwan and mainland China; CWA supports the date. Remove unqualified all-time Taiwan intensity record, which depends on measurement and comparison. Exact 71 is not established by the reviewed over-70 source; withhold pending exact mortality evidence.

08-24.title: Russian passenger plane bombings
08-24.description: Two passenger aircraft departing Moscow were destroyed by suicide bombings over Tula and Rostov oblasts on August 24, 2004. Russia's report to ICAO counted all 90 occupants, including the attackers, as killed. Investigators identified explosive devices detonated in flight.

08-24.title: Greek forest fires
08-24.description: Widespread forest fires in Greece, most severely in the Peloponnese, burned from late August 2007 and killed 85 people across the country. Flames raced through villages, and many victims were trapped in their homes or while fleeing by car.

review.note: 85 is a summer/season total in secondary accounts, not established for fires beginningAugust24. European Commission study gives76 for2007, while secondary accounts distinguish67 inAugust. Need authoritative mortality reconciliation and defined episode start; July fires cannot be silently moved toAugust24.

08-24.title: San Fernando migrant massacre
08-24.description: Mexican marines discovered the bodies of 72 Central and South American migrants, 58 men and 14 women, bound, blindfolded, and shot dead inside a grain barn on a ranch near San Fernando, Tamaulipas, on August 24, 2010. The sole survivor, an Ecuadorean who escaped by feigning death, told investigators that members of the Los Zetas drug cartel killed the migrants after they refused to be forcibly recruited to work for the gang. The massacre was the largest single mass killing of the Mexican drug war at the time and drew international condemnation, with U.N. human rights chief Navi Pillay demanding an end to impunity.

review.note: August 24 is discovery, not necessarily killing date; CNDH dates the massacre August 22. Victims included an Indian national, so all Central/South American is overbroad. 'Sole survivor' and maximum-of-war claims need further checking. Precise UTC killing date remains unresolved.

08-24.title: Central Italy earthquake (Amatrice)
08-24.description: A magnitude 6.0 earthquake struck central Italy at 01:36 UTC on August 24, 2016. Italy's Civil Protection Department records 299 deaths: 237 in Amatrice, 11 in Accumoli and 51 in Arquata del Tronto.
sources: Italian Civil Protection Department, August 2018 update

08-24.title: Gang attack on Kenscoff in Haiti kills at least 47
08-24.description: Armed gangs attacked Kenscoff late on August 23 local time, killing residents, burning homes and attacking a church sheltering displaced people. AP reported at least 47 deaths by August 30. The final incident-specific toll remained uncertain.

08-24.title: Montana man kills eight relatives and himself at family dinner
08-24.description: A man killed eight relatives, including four children, at a family home outside Billings on Sunday evening, August 23 local time, before dying by suicide. Police responded shortly after 18:00, and the house caught fire. Nine people died, including the attacker.

08-25.title: Mumbai twin bomb blasts
08-25.description: Twin car bombs exploded at the Gateway of India and the Zaveri Bazaar jewellery market during the lunch hour, killing 52 people and injuring more than 200. Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba was suspected, and three people were later convicted for the attack.

review.note: Later court reporting disagrees: 54 in New Indian Express versus 52 in AFP/Dawn; even the reference summary conflicts internally. Date, targets and three convictions are corroborated, but the final incident-only toll needs a court or police source distinguishing other blasts in the prosecution.

08-25.title: Rohingya clearance operations, Myanmar
08-25.description: Myanmar's military launched clearance operations against Rohingya communities in Rakhine State on August 25, 2017. MSF's refugee surveys estimated that at least 6,700 Rohingya died violently between August 25 and September 24, including at least 730 children under five. The numeric toll represents that first-month estimate.

08-26.title: Kabul airport bombing
08-26.description: An ISIS-K suicide bomber attacked crowds at Kabul airport's Abbey Gate on August 26, 2021, during evacuation operations. Thirteen US service members and around 170 Afghan civilians were killed. The subsequent US military investigation described one bomber, correcting early reports of a complex attack.

08-26.title: Ice-rock avalanche triggers Nepal-Tibet flood killing at least 1,446
08-26.location: Bhote Koshi valley, Rasuwagadhi, Nepal / Tibet border
08-26.description: An ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border triggered a destructive flood through the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors on August 26. Reporting by September 17 put recovered deaths at 1,403 in Nepal and 43 in China, a combined 1,446. Another 6,669 people were reported missing across both countries, separately from the death toll. Scientific analysis indicated warming likely contributed to slope instability.

08-27.title: Hurricane Laura
08-27.description: Hurricane Laura made landfall near Cameron, Louisiana on 27 August 2020 as a Category 4 storm with winds of 240 km/h, the strongest hurricane to hit the state since 1856. The storm killed 81 people in total across its path, including at least 41 in the United States (30 in Louisiana), 31 in Haiti and 9 in the Dominican Republic, and caused roughly $19 billion in damage. Storm surge and wind destroyed entire communities along the Gulf Coast of Louisiana and Texas.

review.note: Landfall identity and category supported; 81 is a combined direct/indirect total, not Louisiana fatalities. Louisiana government cites 31 rather than original 30; sources vary on Dominican Republic and Louisiana breakdowns. Need final NHC mortality table and check 'strongest since 1856' against 1856/2020 intensity equivalence.

08-28.title: South Asia floods
08-28.description: Monsoon flooding affected Bangladesh, India and Nepal in August 2017. On September 2, UNICEF reported at least 1,288 deaths since mid-August and estimated more than 45 million people affected. Affected population is not the same as displaced population.

review.note: UNICEF's September 2 release supports at least 1,288 reported deaths since mid-August and over 45 million affected, not 40 million displaced. August 28 is an unsupported single-day anchor within an ongoing monsoon disaster. The toll is a dated preliminary count, not a reconciled season total; do not replace the date with the publication date and call it verified.

08-28.title: Church minibus collision in central Zimbabwe kills 27
08-28.description: A minibus carrying church members collided head-on with a truck that was overtaking in central Zimbabwe on August 28, 2026, killing at least 27 people. Police reported the crash on Saturday, August 29, in the latest deadly road accident to hit the country.

08-28.title: Israeli strikes kill five in Gaza and three in West Bank
08-28.location: Gaza Strip and West Bank, Palestine
08-28.description: Israeli airstrikes on August 28, 2026 killed five people in Gaza and three in the West Bank city of Jenin, according to Palestinian health officials. The strikes came amid continuing Israeli military operations despite the ceasefire framework, as tensions persisted across the occupied territories.

08-28.title: Russian drone strike on ammunition warehouse near Kyiv kills 38
08-28.location: Myla, Bucha district, Kyiv region, Ukraine
08-28.description: A Russian drone strike hit an ammunition storage site in Myla on the evening of August 28, triggering explosions and fires in nearby buildings. President Zelenskyy reported 38 deaths and 20 injuries on August 30, with four people still missing. Authorities opened an inquiry into the storage arrangements.

08-29.title: Imam Ali Mosque bombing in Najaf
08-29.description: A bombing outside the Imam Ali shrine in Najaf on August 29, 2003, killed Ayatollah Mohammed Baqir al-Hakim and many other worshippers. Iraq Body Count records a range of 83-126 deaths; contemporary reporting gave differing totals.

review.note: 95 includes al-Hakim, not 95 plus him. PBS updated contemporary count to 95 with 142 wounded; IBC retains 83-126 deaths. Exact final count and over-200 injury claim remain unsettled. Proposed prose preserves the range instead of pretending a final total is established.

08-29.title: Hurricane Katrina
08-29.location: US Gulf Coast, including Louisiana and Mississippi
08-29.description: Hurricane Katrina struck the northern US Gulf Coast on August 29, 2005, causing catastrophic storm surge and flooding. New Orleans suffered extensive inundation after flood-protection failures. The National Weather Service's updated assessment attributes 1,392 deaths and $125 billion in damage, in 2005 dollars, to the hurricane.

08-30.title: Typhoon Lionrock floods in North Korea
08-30.description: Heavy rain associated with Typhoon Lionrock caused severe flooding in northeastern North Korea in late August 2016. A September 14 UN update reported 138 confirmed deaths and 400 people missing. Those missing were not confirmed dead in that report.

review.note: The September 11 UN report lists 133 confirmed dead and 395 missing; September 14 gives 138 and 400. Neither supports more than 500 confirmed deaths in North Korea or 550 internationally. Missing people cannot simply be added to confirmed deaths. OCHA references August 29 while ACAPS describes August 30; Japan landfall does not establish North Korea's flood onset or its UTC date. Core date and final toll remain unresolved.

sources.name: United Nations in DPR Korea, September 11 update
United Nations in DPR Korea, September 14 update

08-31.title: Typhoon Rusa
08-31.description: Typhoon Rusa, the strongest typhoon to strike South Korea in more than four decades, made landfall near Goheung on August 31, 2002. It killed 238 people across South Korea, Japan and North Korea and caused about $4.2 billion in damage.

review.note: JTWC confirms 31 August Goheung landfall. Korean retrospective reports 246 dead or missing in South Korea; that is not interchangeable with 238 confirmed deaths across three countries. Need country-specific dead/missing reconciliation and intensity-superlative definition.

08-31.title: Rizhskaya metro station bombing
08-31.description: A female suicide bomber detonated an explosive device near the Rizhskaya metro station in Moscow, killing 10 people and wounding more than 50. The attack, linked to Chechen separatist militants, came one week after the bombing of two Russian passenger planes.

review.note: Contemporary reports give ten total deaths; later accounts differ on whether that includes the bomber and accomplice. Russian reference explicitly includes both, while AP wording suggests a larger victim-only count. Date and location established; do not silently equate totals with innocent victims.

08-31.title: Al-Aaimmah bridge stampede
08-31.description: A stampede on the Al-Aaimmah bridge in Baghdad during a Shia pilgrimage killed at least 965 people, mostly women and children crushed or drowned in the Tigris River after rumours of a suicide bomber sparked panic. The stampede followed mortar fire near the Kadhimiya shrine that had already killed pilgrims.

review.note: 965 appears in retrospective summaries, while contemporary RTE gives 956 and forecasts 1,000. Need final official count and confirmation that earlier mortar victims are excluded. This was a crowd crush triggered by a reported bomber rumor, not an established suicide bombing; terrorism categorization needs taxonomy review.

08-31.title: Israeli strikes kill at least five across the Gaza Strip
08-31.description: Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip on August 31, 2026, killed at least five people, according to Palestinian health officials. The strikes hit several parts of the enclave amid the continuing Israel-Hamas war.

08-31.title: Suspected PDF fighters kill 12 civilians in Mahlaing Township, Myanmar
08-31.description: Twelve civilians were killed in an attack on Hta Man Gyi village in Mahlaing Township, Mandalay Region, on August 31, 2026, which Myanmar's military government blamed on members of the resistance-aligned People's Defence Force. State media said the attackers entered the village and opened fire on residents.

review.note: Approximately 04:00 MMT August 31 is August 30 UTC. ACLED describes an unidentified armed group and victims including administrators/security-team or militia leaders assumed unarmed; military media blame PDF. Do not silently endorse either perpetrator identity or civilian status. IOM URL is a country feed, not a stable individual source record; Myawady open failed although search retrieved its text. Corroboration and victim status remain insufficient for publication.

09-01.title: Beslan school siege
09-01.description: Militants seized School Number One in Beslan on September 1, 2004, holding more than 1,100 people hostage. Explosions and an armed assault ended the siege on September 3. The civilian death toll was 334, including 186 children; attackers also died.
sources: European Court of Human Rights case-law note

09-01.title: Hurricane Dorian
09-01.location: Abaco Islands and Grand Bahama, Bahamas
09-01.description: Hurricane Dorian, a Category 5 storm with sustained winds of 185 mph, devastated the northern Bahamas when it made landfall on 1 September 2019, stalling over the Abaco Islands and Grand Bahama for more than a day. The storm killed 84 people across all affected areas, including 74 in the Bahamas, where hundreds of people were initially reported missing and whole settlements were flattened by the storm surge. It was the strongest hurricane on record to hit the Bahamas and caused tens of thousands of people to be displaced or left homeless.

review.note: September 1 landfall, category 5 and 185 mph established. Need reconcile 84 all-area deaths and 74 Bahamas with NHC confirmed/reported and missing categories and later Bahamas revisions; no full verification of numeric death/displacement scope. The NHC report could not be opened successfully (access denied), so its final mortality table was not checked.

09-01.title: Nigeria floods
09-01.description: Flooding across Nigeria in 2022 killed 662 people, injured 3,174 and displaced about 2.43 million, according to NEMA's director general in January 2023. These are nationwide seasonal totals, not deaths on a single September day.

review.note: NEMA's January 2023 retrospective supersedes 603: 662 deaths, 3,174 injuries and 2,430,445 displaced. September 1 is not established as onset of the season-long floods; a precise event date remains unresolved. Remove unsupported destroyed-home total and overly simple dam-release causation.

09-01.title: Russian missile and drone attacks on Kyiv kill at least 12
09-01.description: Russian missile and drone attacks on Kyiv and surrounding areas on September 1, 2026, killed at least 12 people, including an Indian national, and wounded dozens more, according to Ukrainian officials. Residential buildings and other civilian infrastructure were damaged in what President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as a continuing series of Russian strikes on the capital.

review.note: Twelve deaths including an Indian national are supported, but the attack ran more than 12 hours overnight August 31-September 1 and into Tuesday. Fatal incident times were not established sufficiently to assign all twelve to September 1 UTC. The publication date cannot resolve the mixed interval.

09-01.title: US airstrike on wedding party in Hormozgan province kills five
09-01.description: A US strike hit a home hosting a wedding celebration in Kuhestak on the evening of September 1, according to Iranian authorities and AP's subsequent on-scene reporting. Five people died, including a woman who died in hospital September 3, and more than 60 were injured. Vice President JD Vance said September 3 that the US was investigating.

09-01.title: US strike reportedly kills four IRGC members in Kermanshah
09-01.description: Iran's provincial IRGC reported four Aerospace Force members killed in a US strike in Kermanshah, according to September 2 reporting. The precise UTC date remains unestablished; the casualty claim came from Iranian authorities, not CENTCOM.

review.note: CENTCOM confirms operations, not five Kermanshah deaths. Anadolu September 2 attributes FOUR Aerospace Force deaths to the provincial IRGC, separately three Basij on Lavan Island. No corroborated five-person Kermanshah total found. The exact Kermanshah strike time/date within the September 1-2 attacks is not established. Do not merge wedding casualties or Lavan deaths.

09-02.title: Bus crash in South Sinai, Egypt, kills at least 22
09-02.description: A bus crashed in South Sinai, Egypt, on September 2, 2026, killing at least 22 people, including ten Jordanian nationals, and injuring 28 others. The bus was travelling between the Red Sea towns of Dahab and Nuweiba when the accident occurred.

09-02.title: Fuel siphoning deaths in Rivers State, Nigeria, reach 43
09-02.description: Dozens of people reportedly died during an alleged petroleum-siphoning attempt at Okari Jetty, Okrika, around midnight at the start of September 3 local time. Reports describe toxic-fume exposure and some drownings, but differ between at least 37 deaths and 43 dead or feared dead.

review.note: Channels gives approximately 00:00 WAT September 3, which is September 2 UTC. Anadolu reports 43 dead but Vanguard calls 43 feared dead and later AP reports at least 37. Reports also differ on loading vessel versus tapped pipeline; some victims reportedly drowned after inhalation. No reconciled confirmed 43-person toll retrieved.

09-02.title: Minivan collision on Sege highway in Ghana kills 13
09-02.description: A collision involving two passenger minivans on the Sege section of the Accra-Aflao highway killed 13 people on September 2. Others were injured, according to Ghanaian news reports quoting emergency personnel.

09-02.title: Minneapolis apartment shooting leaves three dead, including attacker
09-02.description: A gunman killed two people at an apartment building in Minneapolis's Loring Park neighborhood on September 2 before police shot and killed him. Three civilians and three officers were injured; two of the officers suffered gunshot wounds.

09-04.title: Kunduz Fuel Tanker Airstrike
09-04.description: On September 4, 2009, NATO aircraft, at the request of German forces, bombed two fuel tankers hijacked by Taliban insurgents near Kunduz City. Villagers had gathered around the stranded tankers to siphon fuel. Death toll estimates range from 56 to 179, with a German parliamentary investigation concluding up to 142 people died, including more than 100 civilians. The strike sparked a major political crisis in Germany and led to compensation payments to victims' families.

review.note: Bundestag says the exact number remains unknown and cites reports up to 142; it does not establish over 100 civilians as the parliamentary conclusion. Numeric 100 is unsupported precision. Also verify local overnight strike against UTC before retaining September 4. Do not replace it with a different estimate as a confirmed count.

09-04.title: Apalachee High School Shooting
09-04.description: A 14-year-old student opened fire at Apalachee High School near Winder, Georgia, on September 4, 2024. Two students and two teachers were killed, and nine other people were injured. The suspect was taken into custody without incident and charged with four counts of felony murder.

09-04.title: Explosion at military base in Viacha, Bolivia, kills nine
09-04.description: Explosions struck the Bolivar military regiment in Viacha on the afternoon of September 4. Authorities confirmed nine deaths by September 8, with five people still missing, and later reported 84 injured. The cause remained under investigation.

09-04.title: Fire at wedding party in Kinshasa kills at least 12
09-04.location: Lingwala, Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo
09-04.description: A fire broke out during a wedding reception at the Panacee hall in Lingwala, Kinshasa, on the evening of September 4. The government's subsequent official account reported 12 deaths, lower than initial local estimates of 22. Investigators were still determining the cause.

09-04.title: Mudslide in Mingkeng village, Jiangxi, kills 13
09-04.location: Mingkeng village, Suichuan County, Jiangxi, China
09-04.description: A mudslide struck Mingkeng village in Gaoping, Suichuan County, around 04:00 local time on September 5 after prolonged rain associated with Typhoon Saudel. Thirteen people died in this mudslide. The separate countywide total of 16 included deaths in two other towns.

09-04.title: Pakistani security forces kill 48 separatists in Balochistan raids
09-04.description: Pakistan's military announced September 4 that its forces had killed 48 alleged militants during several raids in Balochistan over the preceding 72 hours. This is an attributed operational aggregate, not a September 4 single-day death toll.

review.note: The military's 48 is a multi-raid total over 72 hours ending September 4, not 48 deaths on that date. Geo identifies six in Mastung September 4, with other operations on earlier dates. Incident-specific dates/UTC and allocation are needed before publication as daily events; reporting does not independently establish military claims about all victims.

09-05.title: Pakistan monsoon floods — 2012
09-05.location: Sindh, Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, Pakistan
09-05.description: Heavy monsoon rains from a low-pressure system that lingered over Pakistan from 3 to 12 September 2012 caused severe flooding across southern Punjab, upper Sindh, and parts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan. The National Disaster Management Authority reported 455 deaths and some five million people affected, with record rainfall in several cities and widespread destruction of homes and crops.

review.note: 455 is an October reporting tally; September 5 as onset and exact weather-system interval remain unverified. ADRC groups the flood season from August 23. Need season-wide versus September-only scope before certifying.

09-05.title: Luding earthquake (Sichuan)
09-05.description: An earthquake struck Luding County in Sichuan, China, on September 5, 2022, triggering landslides and damaging buildings and roads. The Hong Kong Red Cross reported 93 deaths, more than 400 injured and 25 missing as of September 11; later landslide research reports 424 injuries.

09-05.title: Bus crash on Fogo island, Cape Verde, kills at least 25
09-05.description: A passenger bus left a mountain road between Cha das Caldeiras and Campanas de Cima on Fogo island late on September 5, killing 25 people and injuring 14. Many victims were children and adolescents.

09-05.title: Fuel tanker explosion on Hamedan-Sanandaj highway, Iran, kills 11
09-05.description: A fuel tanker suffered an apparent brake failure, hit other vehicles and exploded on the Hamedan-Sanandaj highway in western Iran on September 5, 2026, killing 11 people and injuring seven others. The initial reported toll of 10 was later revised upward.

09-06.title: Avalanche on Mount Mizhirgi, Russia, kills 17 climbers
09-06.description: An avalanche hit a group of 33 climbers on Mount Mizhirgi in the Bezengi Gorge on September 6. Search teams recovered the final missing person on September 13, bringing the death toll to 17. Sixteen survived, including six who were hospitalized.

09-06.title: Cargo plane crash at Miami airport kills five
09-06.description: A Boeing 767-300 cargo plane operated by 21 Air for Amazon Air overshot the runway and struck vehicles while landing at Miami International Airport on September 6, 2026, killing five people and injuring five others.

09-06.title: Fireworks explosion at religious celebration in Temascalcingo, Mexico, kills 10
09-06.description: Fireworks exploded beside the Nuestra Senora de la Luz church in Santa Maria Canchesda, Temascalcingo, during a religious celebration on the night of September 5 local time. Ten people were killed and 64 injured. The cause was under investigation.

09-06.title: Hostel building collapse in New Delhi kills seven
09-06.description: A five-storey building housing a private hostel collapsed in Satya Niketan on the afternoon of September 6. The death toll reached seven by September 7, and twelve people were rescued and taken to hospital.

09-07.title: Yunnan earthquakes
09-07.description: On 7 September 2012, a doublet of earthquakes (magnitudes 5.6 and 5.3) struck Yiliang County in Zhaotong, Yunnan, China. The quakes killed 81 people and injured 821, damaged more than 20,000 houses, and forced the evacuation of at least 100,000 residents from the mountainous, landslide-prone area.

review.note: ADRC reports Chinese magnitudes 5.7/5.6, not 5.6/5.3; magnitude agency/scale is unspecified. Date/daytime UTC aligns. Final 81/821 and housing/evacuation totals require primary final report rather than mixed preliminary values.

09-07.title: Kashmir Floods
09-07.description: Monsoon flooding in September 2014 devastated Jammu and Kashmir and parts of Pakistan, including Punjab. Srinagar was extensively inundated. Fatality reports covered different regions and reporting dates, so a Kashmir-only total must not be inferred from combined India-Pakistan figures.

review.note: Flood deaths predate September 7. 500 combines incompatible regional/time scopes; NDMA gives 367 in Pakistan including Punjab, not solely Kashmir. Resolve intended geographic extent and onset before replacing date/toll.

09-07.title: Super Typhoon Yagi
09-07.description: Super Typhoon Yagi, the most powerful storm of the 2024 season, made landfall in northern Vietnam on September 7, 2024, after causing destruction in the Philippines and southern China, and spawned flooding and landslides across Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, and Myanmar. The storm and its aftermath killed at least 844 people across the region, more than 320 of them in Vietnam, with hundreds more missing in Myanmar.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

review.note: 844 appears in Global Water Monitor but a secondary compilation ranges to 1,009; national accounting and Myanmar missing/dead reconciliation remain incomplete. September 7 is Vietnam landfall, not onset of multinational impacts. Most powerful storm of the 2024 season is not supported by HKO, which gives a narrower South China Sea ranking. Withhold pending geographic/time-scope alignment.

09-07.title: Israeli strikes on Kfar Rumman kill 13, including children and a medic
09-07.description: Israeli strikes on a residential building and a vehicle in Kfar Rumman were reported on September 7. Lebanon's Health Ministry later reported 13 deaths: twelve in the building, including six children, and one medic in the vehicle strike. Two other medics were wounded. The precise UTC date remains unestablished.

review.note: Al-Monitor September 14 is republication: Reuters dateline/photo September 7; MarketScreener explicitly shows September 7 publication and September 14 modification. NOT a new September 14 attack. Updated ministry toll 13 comprises 12 in building, including 6 children/3 women, plus ONE medic killed and 2 medics wounded; original two-medic-death wording is superseded. Earlier AP 12 and WAFA 11 are preliminary. Reuters contains contradictory timing cues: state media 'after midnight' versus witnesses preparing for school; exact UTC date September 6/7 remains unresolved. Two Reuters URLs share one wire report.

09-07.title: Saudi airstrike on prison in Al-Jawf, Yemen, kills 17
09-07.description: A Saudi airstrike hit a prison in Al-Jawf Governorate, Yemen, on September 7, 2026, during an offensive against Houthi forces, killing seven people, including a child, and trapping dozens under the rubble. The toll rose to 17 the following day as bodies were recovered.

review.note: AP September 9 reports 23 recovered deaths, superseding 17; these are updates to the September 7 prison incident. Houthi authorities blame Saudi-led airstrikes; the Yemeni rights centre blames the Houthis. Do not state Saudi responsibility as undisputed. Exact strike time/UTC boundary was not established. Two AP documents share publisher and Houthi-source provenance.

sources.name: Yemeni Center for Rehabilitation of Victims of Violations and Torture

09-08.title: Malegaon bombings
09-08.description: Four explosions struck Malegaon on September 8, 2006, around Friday prayers. The Bombay High Court's later account records 31 deaths and 312 injuries. In April 2026, the court discharged the last four accused, leaving no accused facing trial in this case at that time.

09-08.title: Zamboanga City siege
09-08.description: Fighting between government forces and an MNLF faction began in Zamboanga City early on September 9, 2013, local time, or September 8 UTC. The city government's commemoration records 38 civilian and security-force deaths, excluding rebel fatalities, during the siege.

review.note: 04:30 September 9 local is September 8 UTC. City government confirms 38 non-rebel deaths (20 soldiers, five police, 13 civilians), not the overall 200 figure. Rebel toll, total displacement and endpoint differ across accounts; these remain unverified.

09-08.title: Chiapas earthquake, Mexico
09-08.description: A magnitude 8.2 earthquake struck offshore Chiapas, Mexico, at 04:49 UTC on September 8, 2017, late September 7 locally. The disaster killed at least 98 people and caused extensive damage in southern Mexico.

09-08.title: Marrakesh–Safi earthquake
09-08.description: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck Morocco's High Atlas region at 22:11 UTC on September 8, 2023, 23:11 locally. Villages in Al Haouz and surrounding areas were devastated. IFRC retrospective reporting records at least 2,960 deaths and more than 5,600 injuries.

09-08.title: AFP sources report more than 500 deaths in renewed Yemen fighting
09-08.description: AFP reported on September 8 that military and medical sources counted at least 278 Houthi fighters,216 government troops and 29 civilians killed since renewed fighting began the previous week. Their components total 523; this is a cumulative attributed figure, not a single-day toll.

review.note: Components 278+216+29 equal 523, not 500. AFP says MORE THAN 500 and attributes figures to unnamed military/medical sources, not a universally confirmed total. Multi-day offensive since the previous week; September 8 is report date, not date of 523 deaths. Reconcile possible overlap with Al-Jawf prison and other Yemen strikes before integration. Arabic liveblog repeats AFP rather than independently verifies counts.

09-08.title: Drone strike near courthouse in Umm Ruwaba, Sudan, kills 13
09-08.description: A drone strike near the Um Rawaba courthouse on the afternoon of September 8 killed at least 12 people, according to local reports; the Sudan Doctors Network reported 13. Sources blamed the RSF. The precise toll remains unreconciled.

review.note: Tuesday afternoon September 8 supports same UTC date. Sudan Doctors Network reporting gives 13 dead/22 injured; Radio Tamazuj's authorities/eyewitnesses give 12 dead/20 injured outside courthouse. No reconciled final count retrieved. RSF attribution is a claim by monitoring groups/army-aligned authorities, not independently proven here.

09-08.title: Famine in Jebel Marra, Sudan, kills at least 20
09-08.description: On September 8, the SLM-AW-aligned civil administration reported famine conditions in Jebel Marra and nearby areas, estimating that up to 20 people were dying daily from hunger and disease. This was a reported mortality estimate, not a verified September 8 event toll.

review.note: Source says UP TO 20 dying EACH DAY from hunger/disease, an estimated mortality rate attributed to SLM-AW-aligned civil administration, not at least 20 identified deaths on September 8. Famine language is a local authority claim, not an IPC determination established here. No incident-level toll/date or second independent source record retrieved.

09-08.title: Helicopter crash in Sarawak, Malaysia, kills five
09-08.description: A MBB Bo 105 helicopter operated for the Flying Doctors of Malaysia crashed near Long Lellang in Sarawak, Malaysian Borneo, on September 8, 2026, killing all five people on board.

09-08.title: Landslide at forest-road work site in Shizuoka kills one worker
09-08.description: A landslide at a forest-road construction site in Kawanehoncho trapped a male worker on the morning of September 8. He was transported from the site the next day and confirmed dead.

09-08.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv and Kyiv region kill seven
09-08.description: Russian strikes reported overnight and during September 8 killed five people in Kyiv and two in the surrounding region, according to Ukrainian authorities. The attacks damaged warehouses and other civilian buildings. Fatal incident times remain insufficiently resolved for a single UTC date.

review.note: City government confirms five killed in September 8 attacks; UATV separately reports two in Kyiv region. Injury counts differ 23/29/35 and need not be retained. Strikes spanned Monday night and Tuesday; exact fatal-incident UTC dates unestablished. Sept 10 two-death Kyiv record may be an earlier bulletin from this attack; do not add without resolving identity.

09-09.title: Assassination of Ahmad Shah Massoud
09-09.description: Two al-Qaeda operatives posing as journalists detonated a bomb hidden in a camera while interviewing Ahmad Shah Massoud, the military leader of the Afghan Northern Alliance, killing him and one other person. The assassination came two days before the September 11 attacks and removed the alliance's most effective commander ahead of the US invasion.

review.note: UNAMA supports the 9 September assassination by attackers posing as journalists. The second non-attacker death and camera-versus-battery concealment require stronger direct evidence; 'most effective commander' is an assessment, not an established factual rank.

09-09.title: Explosion at Ritom hydroelectric plant in Switzerland kills two workers
09-09.description: Two workers died after a fire and explosion at the old Ritom hydroelectric plant in Piotta, Ticino, shortly after 09:30 local time on September 9. Cantonal police described a serious workplace accident.

09-09.title: Explosion at weapons depot in Sarmada, Syria, kills 14
09-09.description: An explosion at a temporary depot for weapons and war remnants near Sarmada, Idlib, on September 9 killed 14 people and injured 11, according to the local health department's updated account.

09-09.title: Israeli strike kills family of four in northern Gaza
09-09.description: An Israeli airstrike hit the Ahmed family's home near Kamal Adwan Hospital in northern Gaza at about 01:45 local time on 10 September 2026, or late 9 September UTC. Two parents and their two daughters were killed, according to Palestinian medical and human-rights reporting.

09-09.title: Russian drone strike on shopping centre in Sumy kills two
09-09.description: A Russian drone hit the parking area of the Manufactura shopping centre in Sumy on the evening of 9 September 2026, killing two people. An initial report of three deaths was corrected. Subsequent reporting put the number injured at 23.

09-10.title: Mekong Delta floods
09-10.description: The worst flooding in the Mekong Delta in decades inundated more than 825,000 homes and affected over 5 million people. 482 people died, most of them children.

review.note: ADRC supports major prolonged flooding and 825,000 inundated homes, but not a discrete 10 September event or final 482 toll. Mekong Commission's later table gives a different national total (453). Geographic and reporting-period reconciliation is required.

09-10.title: Cargo ship fire at Qingdao port kills 25
09-10.description: A fire broke out aboard a foreign-flagged cargo ship at a port in Qingdao, Shandong province, eastern China, on September 10, 2026. The death toll rose to 25 during the day as rescue and recovery operations continued aboard the vessel; authorities did not immediately announce a cause.

09-10.title: Church roof collapse in Vellore, India, kills three
09-10.location: Manju Krishnapuram, Thiruvalam, Vellore district, Tamil Nadu, India
09-10.description: The roof of the under-construction CSI Zion Hill Church at Manjukrishnapuram near Thiruvalam in Vellore district collapsed during concreting at about 16:30 local time on 10 September 2026. Three workers were killed and 14 others were injured.

09-10.title: Grenade attack on house in Dehiwala, Sri Lanka, kills two children
09-10.description: A grenade attack on a house in Dehiwala killed two brothers aged 11 and 17 and injured their father at about 03:20 local time on 11 September 2026, or late 10 September UTC. Police said the attackers appeared to have targeted the wrong house in suspected gang retaliation.

09-10.title: Hurricane Lowell linked to at least two deaths in Hawaii
09-10.description: Two deaths were linked to Hurricane Lowell in Hawaii: a man killed by a falling tree on Oahu and a man found dead on Kauai after being reported missing. The reports concern different incident and recovery dates, not two established deaths on 10 September.

review.note: Two deaths were linked to the storm, but September 10 is a report/update date. Hawaii News Now places the fatal Waimanalo tree incident at about 20:35 HST on Monday September 7, which is September 8 UTC. The other man's body was recovered on Kauai on September 9 after he went missing the previous day; recovery time does not establish death time. A single September 10 UTC casualty allocation is unsupported. Storm-surge attribution for the Kauai death was preliminary.

09-10.title: Russian attacks on Mykolaiv kill four
09-10.description: Russian attacks on Mykolaiv during 9 September and the following night killed four people and injured 19, according to Ukrainian police. The figure covers a reporting interval rather than a single established UTC day.

review.note: Four deaths and 19 injuries are supported for attacks during September 9 and the night into September 10, not four established deaths on September 10 UTC. Ukrinform identifies two women and two men among the dead. The reporting interval crosses dates and individual fatal incident times were not established. The first two documents draw on the same police casualty account.

09-10.title: Russian large-scale attack on Kyiv kills two
09-10.description: A large-scale Russian attack on Kyiv on September 10, 2026, killed two people and injured at least ten, according to Ukrainian authorities.

review.note: Matching two-dead/ten-injured Ukrinform bulletin is dated September 8, not 10; AFP corroborates early September 8 two-death count. September 10 reporting describes a gas-station strike with injuries and a separate regional death, not the claimed city toll. Likely a misdated preliminary duplicate of September 8 aggregate, but cannot assert identical victims without further evidence; do not publish or add twice.

09-10.title: Tour bus crash in eastern Switzerland kills five
09-10.description: A Dutch tour bus crashed between Zernez and Susch in the Swiss canton of Graubunden at about 16:45 local time on 10 September 2026. Police reported five deaths and 40 injuries among the 44 adult passengers and driver.

09-10.title: US strike on suspected drug boat in the Caribbean kills three
09-10.description: U.S. Southern Command said its forces killed three people in a strike on a boat in the Caribbean on 9 September 2026. The military alleged that the vessel was involved in drug trafficking; the retrieved reports did not independently establish that allegation.

review.note: SOUTHCOM dates the operation to September 9; September 10 is the reporting date. Both publishers relay the same military announcement, not independent confirmation of the occupants' identities or trafficking allegations. The operation's exact time and the command's date time zone were not established, so the proposed September 9 date is not verified as UTC and the row remains withheld.

09-10.title: Ukrainian drone strike kills woman in Borisoglebsk, Russia
09-10.description: Regional authorities said an attack by Ukrainian drones overnight on 9-10 September killed a woman and injured two people in Borisoglebsk, Voronezh Oblast.

review.note: Regional authorities reported a woman killed and two people injured in Borisoglebsk. The attack occurred overnight September 9-10 local time; the morning September 10 announcement is not an incident timestamp. Both sources rely on the regional governor. The UTC date remains unresolved, and attribution to Ukraine is the authorities' account.

09-11.title: September 11 Attacks
09-11.location: New York City, Arlington, Virginia, and Pennsylvania, United States
09-11.description: Al-Qaeda hijackers flew commercial airliners into the World Trade Center towers and the Pentagon. A fourth plane crashed in Pennsylvania after passengers fought back. 2,977 people were killed.

09-11.title: Ali Enterprises factory fire
09-11.description: A fire at the Ali Enterprises garment factory in Baldia, Karachi, on September 11, 2012, killed more than 255 workers and injured 57 according to the ILO's compensation-program reporting. The numeric toll here is a lower-bound representation of that report, not a final exact victim count.

09-11.title: Mecca crane collapse
09-11.description: A crawler crane collapsed onto Mecca's Grand Mosque during a severe storm on the late afternoon of September 11, 2015, killing 111 people and injuring 394. Manufacturer Liebherr said the crane was caught by strong winds and should have been placed in its prescribed storm configuration.
sources: Florida Building Commission, engineering review draft

09-11.title: Derna dam collapses and floods
09-11.description: Two dams above Derna failed early on September 11, 2023 after Storm Daniel's heavy rainfall, flooding the city. OCHA's November 28 reporting recorded 4,352 deaths in the wider Libyan flood disaster, with thousands separately missing. Amnesty documented neglected dam maintenance and failures in disaster preparedness.

09-12.title: Drone attacks on cars in Kramatorsk
09-12.description: Three people were killed in separate drone attacks on cars in Kramatorsk, according to local authorities. The city council reported three incidents within about 90 minutes.

09-13.title: Jakarta Stock Exchange bombing
09-13.description: A car bomb exploded in the underground car park of the Jakarta Stock Exchange on 13 September 2000, killing 15 people. Four men were subsequently convicted in connection with the attack, including two soldiers sentenced to life imprisonment in August 2001.

09-13.title: N1 minibus collision in Western Cape
09-13.location: Between Leeu Gamka and Prince Albert, Western Cape, South Africa
09-13.description: A collision involving two minibuses and an SUV killed at least 21 people, according to Western Cape officials. Three of the reported victims died after being taken to hospital.

09-14.title: Typhoon Mangkhut
09-14.description: Typhoon Mangkhut, the strongest storm of the year, made landfall in northern Luzon, Philippines, on September 15, 2018, with sustained winds of 205 km/h. The typhoon triggered landslides in mining and farming areas, destroyed over 400,000 homes, and killed at least 134 people in the Philippines, with additional deaths reported in Hong Kong and southern China. Storm surges and flooding affected millions across the region.

review.note: Landfall was early September 15 local time, September 14 UTC; UTC date correction supported. 134 is a multinational total in secondary summaries, not Philippine deaths; Hong Kong deaths and 400,000 destroyed homes are not substantiated. Keep unresolved until a consistent final geographic toll and damage definition are established.

09-15.title: Bangladesh floods
09-15.description: Severe flooding affected western and southwestern Bangladesh in September 2000, forcing large numbers of residents from their homes. The IFRC described major inundation in border districts on 22 September. Contemporary casualty and displacement figures were provisional.

review.note: The description incorrectly says two million drowned: sources describe homelessness or affected population. IFRC dates the major western-border inundation to 22 September; 15 September and 150 deaths are not established. Published counts differ by event scope, so no replacement date or toll is asserted.

09-16.title: Washington Navy Yard shooting
09-16.description: On the morning of September 16, 2013, contractor Aaron Alexis opened fire inside the Washington Navy Yard, killing 12 people and wounding others. Police killed him during their response, bringing the total deaths including the attacker to 13.

09-16.title: Drone strike on passenger bus in Nikopol district
09-16.description: A drone strike on a passenger bus killed five people, according to regional authorities, who attributed the attack to Russian forces.

09-16.title: Fatal flooding near Newcomb on the Navajo Nation
09-16.location: Newcomb and Two Grey Hills area, New Mexico, United States
09-16.description: Two adults and a child died in flooding on the Navajo Nation. Police said their bodies were found near the Newcomb and Two Grey Hills area following overnight flooding.

09-16.title: News helicopter crash in Chatsworth
09-16.location: Chatsworth, Los Angeles, California, United States
09-16.description: A television news helicopter crashed while covering a nearby traffic collision. Two people aboard the aircraft and one person on the ground were killed.

09-16.title: SUV and Metro bus collision in Chatsworth
09-16.location: Chatsworth, Los Angeles, California, United States
09-16.description: Two people died and six others were injured when an SUV collided with a Metro bus, according to the Los Angeles Fire Department.

09-17.title: Chinese melamine milk scandal
09-17.description: In 2008, melamine deliberately added to diluted milk contaminated infant formula and other milk products in China. A WHO-authored review reported six deaths, 294,000 affected children and 51,900 cumulative hospitalizations as of December 1, 2008. The exact beginning of the contamination and resulting illness was unknown; the problem became public in September.

review.note: The WHO-authored review supports six reported deaths, 294,000 cases and 51,900 cumulative hospitalizations as of December 1, not 50,000 people simultaneously hospitalized at the peak. It says the illness/contamination onset is unknown, with complaints in December 2007 and a first death in May 2008. September 17 marks Singapore's first detection outside China, not the start of the Chinese scandal. No replacement exact onset date is established. Remove unsupported withdrawal tonnage and arrest detail; the supported shorter description does not cure the unresolved date.

sources.name: WHO authors in Environmental Health Perspectives: The Melamine Incident
Food Policy: China's milk scandal and its institutional roots

09-17.title: Benisheik massacre
09-17.description: Suspected Boko Haram militants attacked Benisheik and nearby travellers in Borno State on Tuesday night, September 17, 2013. UPI's September 20 report, citing Nigerian officials and Daily Trust, put the reported death toll at at least 161 after additional bodies were found.

review.note: Contemporaneous UPI and the Eagle Online place the attack on Tuesday September 17; the latter specifies 6-7 p.m., the same UTC date. The tertiary overview instead dates it September 18 and gives 159, while UPI's later body-recovery report estimates at least 161. The date correction is supported, but final victim total and scope are not reconciled. Withhold the partially corrected record.

09-17.title: Bamako Attack
09-17.description: On September 17, 2024, jihadist attackers from Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) stormed a military police school and the military airport in Bamako, Mali, in a coordinated assault. The attack killed at least 77 people, including civilians, and wounded more than 250, making it one of the deadliest attacks in Mali in years and prompting heightened security measures in the capital.

review.note: Date, JNIM and targets supported. AFP simultaneously reported 77 from a security source and an authenticated official document naming 81 victims and suggesting around 100. The 77 figure cannot be presented as a settled final count; civilian inclusion and exact injured total also need reconciliation.

09-17.title: Fatal debris from drone interception near Taif
09-17.description: Saudi civil defence said debris from an intercepted drone killed a Yemeni resident and injured two other people. Saudi authorities attributed the drone launch to Yemen's Houthis.

09-18.title: 2001 Anthrax Attacks
09-18.description: Anthrax-contaminated letters, including mail postmarked 18 September 2001, caused 22 infections and five deaths in the United States. CDC estimated that 32,000 people began preventive antibiotics. The FBI closed its investigation in 2010 after concluding Bruce Ivins was responsible. A National Research Council review found the scientific evidence linking the letter material to a particular laboratory flask less conclusive than the Justice Department had stated.

09-18.title: Hurricane Jeanne flooding in Haiti
09-18.description: Torrential rains from Tropical Storm Jeanne triggered catastrophic flash flooding and mudslides in Haiti, most severely in the coastal city of Gonaives, which was left largely submerged. The Haitian government's final tally recorded 3,006 deaths, including 2,826 in Gonaives, with about 200,000 people affected.

review.note: NOAA confirms catastrophic Haiti flooding and over 3,000 deaths, but exact 3,006/2,826 and the asserted final-government provenance were not established from accessible primary text. NHC report fetch was blocked; archive search found it but not its casualty discussion. September 18 is an onset label for flooding extending into September 19.

09-18.title: Sikkim earthquake
09-18.description: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck on September 18, 2011 near the Nepal-Sikkim border in northeastern India, with the epicentre in the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area. At least 111 people were killed, including 97 in India (mostly in Sikkim), 7 in China's Tibet region, 6 in Nepal and 1 in Bhutan, and hundreds were injured. The quake, felt across northern India, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Tibet, triggered landslides and rockfalls that cut off remote areas and damaged roughly 43,000 houses in Sikkim.

review.note: USGS establishes magnitude 6.9 and September 18 India-Nepal border event. Cross-country 111 breakdown and 43,000 Sikkim houses need an original final assessment. Do not infer all of them from a secondary summary.

09-18.title: Bombing and gun attack on police headquarters in Kohat
09-18.description: A bombing and gun attack on a police compound killed at least 31 people, according to the victim toll reported by authorities on September 19. The attack began the previous afternoon.

09-19.title: Puebla earthquake, Mexico
09-19.location: Puebla, Morelos and Mexico City, Mexico
09-19.description: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck central Mexico on September 19, 2017, damaging Puebla, Morelos and Mexico City. Mexico's CENAPRED records 369 deaths. The quake occurred on the anniversary of the 1985 Mexico City earthquake.

09-19.title: Fatal strike in Jabalia
09-19.description: A strike in Jabalia killed one person, according to Palestinian medical sources. This entry records only the Jabalia death, not the larger daily Gaza toll.

09-19.title: Fatal strike in Shuja'iyya
09-19.description: A strike in Shuja'iyya killed one person, according to Palestinian medical sources. This entry excludes other deaths reported elsewhere in Gaza that day.

09-20.title: Islamabad Marriott Hotel bombing
09-20.description: A suicide truck bombing struck the Marriott Hotel in Islamabad on the evening of September 20, 2008, causing a major fire and killing dozens. A group calling itself Fedayeen Islam later claimed responsibility, but that claim was not authenticated in the contemporaneous Reuters report.

review.note: September 20 evening is established, but the exact victim total is not: the US State Department's annual report says 53, the original says 54, and a 2012 US court opinion cites 56 from BBC reporting. These are not demonstrated to be solely attacker-inclusion differences. The statement that no group claimed responsibility is false: Reuters reported a Fedayeen Islam claim on September 22 while explicitly saying it was unauthenticated. Remove the unsupported explosive weight, nationality breakdown and ranking; preserve the unverified nature of that claim. Toll remains a publication blocker.

sources.name: US State Department: Pakistan human rights report 2008
Reuters via RFE/RL: unauthenticated responsibility claim
US District Court: DiFederico v Marriott memorandum opinion

09-20.title: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico
09-20.description: Hurricane Maria made landfall in Puerto Rico on September 20, 2017, as a Category 4 hurricane with sustained winds of 155 mph. A George Washington University study estimated 2,975 excess deaths from September 2017 through February 2018 after accounting for population displacement. This is a modeled estimate, not a count of individually certified storm deaths.
sources: US National Weather Service, San Juan

09-20.title: MV Nyerere ferry capsizing
09-20.description: The overloaded ferry MV Nyerere capsized while approaching Ukara Island on Lake Victoria on September 20, 2018. Later government figures put the death toll at 228, with 41 people rescued. It had been travelling from Ukerewe Island.

review.note: Ferry was approaching Ukara, not just departing Ukerewe. 41 survivors, not hundreds; 228 is the later government tally summarized by secondary source, while September 24 AFP still reported 224. The later 228 toll was not corroborated beyond a secondary summary in this batch; the opened contemporary AFP source still had 224. Route/survivor corrections do not establish a final death tally.

09-20.title: Fatal shooting near Neve Tzuf
09-20.location: Near Neve Tzuf, occupied West Bank
09-20.description: A Palestinian gunman shot dead an Israeli man near Neve Tzuf, according to Israeli authorities. The suspect was subsequently detained.

09-20.title: Palestinian motorist killed near Ganim
09-20.location: Near Ganim, Jenin area, occupied West Bank
09-20.description: Israeli troops shot dead a Palestinian motorist. The Israeli military alleged an attempted vehicle attack; Reuters said it could not independently verify the circumstances.

09-20.title: Reported airstrike on displacement camp in Kunar
09-20.description: Afghan provincial officials said an airstrike killed three people at a camp for families displaced by an earthquake. They attributed the strike to Pakistan; Pakistan's military had not commented in the cited initial report.

09-21.title: Westgate shopping mall attack
09-21.description: Gunmen attacked Nairobi's Westgate shopping mall around midday on September 21, 2013. Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility. The Congressional Research Service records at least 67 victims killed and almost 200 wounded in the four-day siege; this toll excludes attackers.

09-21.title: Tabas Coal Mine Explosion
09-21.description: A methane explosion at the Madanjoo coal mine near Tabas, Iran, on the evening of September 21, 2024 killed 52 miners, according to later reporting. Early rescue reports gave lower recovered-body counts while other workers remained trapped.

09-22.title: Peshawar church bombing
09-22.description: Two suicide bombers attacked worshippers at All Saints Church in Peshawar on September 22, 2013. Reported death totals differed: the bishop of Peshawar reported 127 by September 30, above figures circulating in official and international reporting. A reconciled final count is not established by these sources.

review.note: Bishop's September 30 account gives 127 dead and 170 injured; Dawn reports competing 83/123 totals. These are competing sources, not a demonstrated official upward revision. Exact final toll remains unresolved.

sources.name: Titus Presler, account from bishop of Peshawar
Dawn, competing official and community tolls

09-24.title: Balochistan earthquake
09-24.description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck Balochistan, Pakistan, at 11:29 UTC on September 24, 2013, causing extensive destruction around Awaran. Published fatality figures differ, and totals must distinguish the mainshock, subsequent earthquakes and geographic scope.

review.note: USGS confirms magnitude 7.7 and September 24 at 11:29 UTC. The 825/840 total has not been reconciled with lower official district counts or the September 28 aftershock. NDMA PDF opened, but casualty search failed; do not certify its unread table.

09-26.title: MV Le Joola capsizing
09-26.description: The overloaded Senegalese ferry Le Joola capsized off The Gambia late on 26 September 2002 while traveling from Ziguinchor to Dakar. The official toll was 1,863 dead or presumed dead, and 64 people survived.

09-26.title: Typhoon Ketsana (Ondoy)
09-26.description: Tropical storm Ketsana (Ondoy) struck the Philippines on September 26, 2009, bringing the heaviest rainfall to Metro Manila in more than four decades — about a month's rain in under 12 hours — and causing catastrophic flash flooding. The consolidated regional death toll reached roughly 900, including 671 in the Philippines, 179 in Vietnam, and dozens more in Cambodia and Laos. Hundreds of thousands were displaced across Southeast Asia.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

review.note: JICA cites 464 Philippine deaths; GMA's 277 is explicitly an October 1 preliminary count. Neither supports 671 Philippine deaths or the 921 regional field. Need comparable final country reports; do not add preliminary and final or Ondoy/Pepeng totals.

09-26.title: Iguala Mass Kidnapping of 43 Students
09-26.description: Forty-three Ayotzinapa students disappeared after attacks in Iguala on the night of September 26-27, 2014, local time; six other people were killed. Independent investigators challenged the official claim that all 43 bodies were burned at a single rubbish dump. By March 2024, remains of three students had been identified, while the full fate of the group remained unresolved.

review.note: 43 is disappeared students, not a confirmed death count; six other people were killed during the attacks. Three students' remains had been identified by March 2024, contradicting 'never found.' Independent evidence rejects the original dump-burning reconstruction. Night September 26-27 local likely falls September 27 UTC, but precise start not confirmed.

09-27.title: Mount Ontake Eruption
09-27.description: Mount Ontake erupted at 02:52 UTC on September 27, 2014, while hikers were on the mountain. The disaster left 58 confirmed dead and five missing; the missing are not included in the confirmed-death count.

09-27.title: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War
09-27.description: On 27 September 2020, Azerbaijan launched a large-scale military offensive against the Armenian-backed Nagorno-Karabakh (Artsakh) region, starting a 44-day war that ended with a Russian-brokered ceasefire on 10 November 2020. Official figures from both sides listed about 2,900 Azerbaijani and 3,800 Armenian soldiers killed, along with roughly 185 civilians, for a combined death toll of more than 6,900, with tens of thousands displaced. Azerbaijan regained control of territory around and within the region under the ceasefire terms.

review.note: September 27 start and 44-day war supported. Official counts have continued changing; latest retrieved Armenian report gives 3,833 including 3,755 military and 78 civilians. 6,900 needs matching as-of dates and inclusion policy for missing/foreign fighters, not a mixture of rounded figures. Mortality study estimates are not official named deaths.

09-28.title: Start of the Second Intifada
09-28.description: The Second Intifada began after Israeli opposition leader Ariel Sharon visited the Temple Mount compound. By end of 2000, roughly 300 people had been killed.

review.note: Sharon's visit and the late-September onset are supported, but 300 by year-end is not established by the cited December report, which ends 2 December and separates populations. Need a defined inclusive date range and victim scope; the count is not a 28 September toll.

09-28.title: Sulawesi earthquake and tsunami
09-28.description: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck the Indonesian island of Sulawesi, triggering a tsunami up to six meters high that hit Palu Bay, along with widespread soil liquefaction that swallowed entire neighborhoods. The disaster destroyed tens of thousands of buildings in Palu, Donggala, and Sigi and displaced over 200,000 people. Indonesia's disaster agency (BNPB) confirmed 4,340 deaths, more than 10,000 injured, and hundreds missing.

review.note: Date, magnitude and disaster identity supported. Need reconcile 4,340 with recovered bodies, missing and people presumed buried; calling all confirmed deaths while also listing missing risks category mixing. BNPB page returned 403 on open. Tsunami-height maximum and displacement total also require final source.

09-29.title: Samoa Earthquake and Tsunami
