09-29.description: A magnitude 8.1 earthquake near the Samoan Islands on September 29, 2009, generated destructive tsunami waves. NOAA records 192 deaths: 149 in Samoa, 34 in American Samoa and nine in Tonga. Runup exceeded 22 meters in Tonga.

09-30.title: West Sumatra (Padang) Earthquake
09-30.description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck off the coast of West Sumatra on September 30, 2009, about 45 km northwest of Padang. The Indonesian government confirmed 1,115 deaths, with more than 1,200 seriously injured and about 450,000 people displaced. Widespread collapse of poorly reinforced buildings in Padang and Padang Pariaman district caused most casualties. USGS called it the deadliest earthquake of 2009.

review.note: Date, Padang/Pariaman area and magnitude corroborated by assessment material; retrieved assessment gives over 1,117, not 1,115. Exact final toll, displacement and strongest mortality ranking need reconciliation with BNPB/USGS, rather than selecting a convenient near-match.

09-30.title: Kaaj education centre bombing (Kabul)
09-30.description: A suicide bombing at the Kaaj education centre in Kabul's Dasht-e Barchi district on September 30, 2022 killed 54 people and wounded 114, according to later UN reporting. Most victims were young Hazara women and girls. A later UN report attributes a claim of responsibility to ISIL-K, although an earlier Dutch government report described the attack as unclaimed.

10-01.title: Srinagar Legislative Assembly Attack
10-01.description: A vehicle bombing and armed attack struck the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly complex in Srinagar on October 1, 2001. India's Home Ministry subsequently attributed the attack to Jaish-e-Mohammed and recorded 38 deaths. Published casualty breakdowns disagree on whether attackers are included.

review.note: Further research establishes October 1 and the attack identity in an MHA gazette notification, which gives 38 deaths. However, SATP's 2001 assessment includes four attackers within 38, while its 2000-2017 table lists 38 victims plus three attackers (41 total); its timeline also contains 36. These are material scope conflicts, not merely unsupported injury/occupancy prose. Remove the original 60-injured and no-legislators claims, but do not certify a victim-only total.

sources.name: South Asia Terrorism Portal: attack table

10-01.title: Bali bombings
10-01.description: Three suicide bombers attacked restaurants in Kuta and Jimbaran, Bali, on October 1, 2005. Twenty victims were killed and more than 100 people injured. Including the three bombers, 23 people died.

10-01.title: Nigeria floods — 2012
10-01.description: From July to October 2012, the worst flooding in Nigeria in four decades submerged large areas of the country, peaking in October. The National Emergency Management Agency reported 363 deaths and over 2.1 million people displaced, with 30 of Nigeria's 36 states affected; Kogi and Benue were the hardest hit, and more than 150,000 hectares of farmland were destroyed.

review.note: 363 and more than 2.1 million displaced supported for July-October; October 1 is not a established unique event date. State count, hardest-hit ranking and 150,000 hectares require assessment-level corroboration. Record overlaps a multi-month season.

10-02.title: Beltway sniper attacks
10-02.location: Washington metropolitan area, Maryland and Virginia, United States
10-02.description: John Allen Muhammad and Lee Boyd Malvo carried out shootings across the Washington metropolitan area in October 2002. Beginning on 2 October, the regional series killed ten people and critically injured three before the suspects were captured on 24 October.

10-02.title: Kunduz hospital airstrike
10-02.description: A US AC-130 attacked MSF's Kunduz trauma hospital early on October 3, 2015, local time, or October 2 UTC. MSF confirmed at least 42 deaths: 14 staff, 24 patients and four caretakers. The US military described the strike as mistaken and administratively disciplined 16 personnel; none faced court-martial.

10-02.title: Las Vegas Route 91 Harvest festival shooting
10-02.description: A gunman fired from the Mandalay Bay hotel into the Route 91 Harvest festival crowd on the Las Vegas Strip late on October 1, 2017, October 2 UTC. The official toll is 60 victims, including two who died from their injuries in 2019 and 2020, and excludes the attacker.
sources: Federal Bureau of Investigation, incident chronology
Las Vegas Review-Journal, official revised toll

10-03.title: Typhoon Parma (Pepeng)
10-03.description: Typhoon Parma (Pepeng) made landfall in northern Luzon on October 3, 2009, and lingered over the island for a week, making landfall three times and causing torrential rains. Massive landslides in Benguet province and the Cordillera Administrative Region killed 465 people in the Philippines, with total regional deaths near 500, including in Vietnam and China. Landslide-buried villages in La Trinidad and Baguio City accounted for the heaviest losses.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

review.note: Search located an NDCC-attributed 465 Philippine tally but not a directly inspected final official report. Regional 500, non-Philippine deaths and the claim that landslides alone caused all 465 require corroboration. Secondary lead is not sufficient to verify this record. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

10-04.title: Hurricane Matthew in Haiti
10-04.description: Hurricane Matthew struck southwestern Haiti on October 4, 2016, as a Category 4 hurricane. The post-disaster assessment records 546 deaths in Haiti and 128 people missing. The numeric toll counts confirmed Haitian deaths, not missing people or deaths in other countries.
sources: International Labour Organization, Haiti post-disaster needs assessment
United Nations Haiti humanitarian response plan

10-05.title: Hurricane Stan
10-05.description: Hurricane Stan triggered torrential rain and catastrophic mudslides across Guatemala, El Salvador and southern Mexico, burying entire villages including Panabaj near Lake Atitlan, where about 1,400 residents were declared missing and presumed dead. More than 1,600 people were killed across the region, most of them in Guatemala.

review.note: NOAA authors distinguish 80 direct Stan deaths from 1,000-2,000 deaths in the broader regional weather system. October 5 is near dissipation, not landfall; the Panabaj estimate and exact 1,660 aggregate are not established. Needs explicit regional episode scope and onset.

10-07.title: US-Led Invasion of Afghanistan
10-07.description: The US-led air campaign in Afghanistan began on 7 October 2001. The Project on Defense Alternatives estimated that 1,000-1,300 civilians were killed directly by bombing between that date and 1 January 2002. The recorded figure is the lower end of that estimate for the campaign period, not a count for 7 October alone.

10-07.title: Herat earthquakes
10-07.description: A sequence of strong earthquakes struck Herat province in western Afghanistan between October 7 and 15, 2023. WHO reported 1,482 deaths and 2,100 injuries from the sequence, with widespread destruction of homes and damage to health facilities.

10-07.title: Israel-Hamas war: Gaza deaths reported in 2023
10-07.description: The war began after the Hamas-led attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, followed by Israeli military operations in Gaza. By December 31, Gaza's Health Ministry reported 21,822 Palestinians killed and 56,451 injured in Gaza. This entry counts that dated Gaza total only, not deaths in Israel, later fatalities, or a final toll of the war.

10-08.title: Kashmir earthquake
10-08.description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck near Muzaffarabad in Pakistani-administered Kashmir, collapsing tens of thousands of poorly built homes and schools and killing an estimated 75,000 people in Pakistan and more than 1,300 in India, with regional estimates reaching 87,000. About 3.5 million people were left homeless.

review.note: Original 75,000 does not match its own Pakistan-plus-India narrative. OCHA uses over 73,000 in Pakistan; other sources give 87,350 and higher regional totals. Magnitude/date established; final geographic and mortality-estimate basis must be chosen explicitly.

10-08.title: Yemen wedding party airstrike
10-08.description: A wedding gathering near Mokha, Yemen, was struck on September 28, 2015. Residents attributed it to the Saudi-led coalition, which denied involvement. Contemporary reporting put deaths at 131, while a UN panel later cited at least 135. This was distinct from the October 2015 Sanaban wedding attack and the October 2016 Sanaa funeral strike.

review.note: Conflation: Mokha wedding was September 28; Sanaban wedding was October 7; acknowledged October 8 strike concerns Sanaa funeral in 2016. Mokha reports 131 versus UN panel at least135; coalition denied responsibility. Supported local calendar correction supplied, but precise UTC time and final toll unresolved.

10-08.title: Sanaa funeral hall airstrike
10-08.description: Saudi-led coalition airstrikes hit a funeral ceremony in Sanaa on October 8, 2016. The coalition initially denied responsibility before acknowledging the attack. Reported casualty counts differed and were preliminary.

review.note: October 8 funeral attack and coalition responsibility are supported; HRW documents the initial denial and subsequent acknowledgement. The 155 figure was explicitly preliminary in same-day reporting. UN initially reported over 140, while HRW later cited the health ministry's at least 110/610, with identification incomplete. No reconciled final 155/525 tally is established. Preserve this contradiction, not a definitive replacement death count.

10-08.title: Kunduz mosque bombing
10-08.description: A suicide bomber attacked the Sayed Abad Shia mosque in Kunduz on October 8, 2021. A later UNAMA report recorded at least 80 people killed and at least 150 wounded. Early reports used conflicting casualty figures, including a combined dead-and-injured total above 100.

10-08.title: Israel-Hezbollah conflict in Lebanon, 2023-2024
10-08.description: Cross-border hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah began on October 8, 2023 and escalated sharply in September 2024. A ceasefire took effect on November 27. On November 29, the UN reported Lebanese authorities' nonfinal toll of around 4,000 dead and over 16,000 injured since the conflict began.

10-10.title: Ankara peace rally bombing
10-10.description: Two suicide bombers attacked a peace-rally gathering outside Ankara's central railway station on October 10, 2015. The toll rose to 103 in November 2015; later commemorative accounts differ on whether 103 or 104 victims are counted. Islamic State was identified as responsible.

review.note: 102 superseded by103 in November2015; 2025 accounts still differ103/104. The record's109 is not reconciled with these sources. Morning October10 date sound; final fatality definition and later deaths unresolved.

10-12.title: USS Cole bombing
10-12.description: Al-Qaeda suicide bombers rammed an explosive-laden boat into the USS Cole as it refuelled. Seventeen American sailors were killed and 39 wounded.
sources: US Naval History and Heritage Command

10-12.title: Bali bombings
10-12.description: Three bombs exploded in Kuta and Denpasar on Bali, including a large car bomb outside the Sari Club nightclub, in an attack linked to Jemaah Islamiyah. The bombings killed 202 people, mostly foreign tourists, and injured more than 200.

10-12.title: Typhoon Hagibis
10-12.description: Typhoon Hagibis, one of the most powerful typhoons to strike Japan in decades, made landfall on the Izu Peninsula near Tokyo on 12 October 2019, bringing record rainfall that caused more than 70 rivers to overflow and widespread landslides. Around 100 people were killed, more than 350 were injured and thousands of homes were flooded, with several prefectures including Nagano, Fukushima and Miyagi among the worst affected. The storm disrupted transport, power and the 2019 Rugby World Cup, and the government described the scale of damage as unprecedented.

review.note: Government white paper gives 91 dead, three missing, 42 seriously and 334 lightly injured as of April 10, 2020. About 100 may reflect later indirect deaths; source for that basis absent. Need consistent final interval and source for 70 rivers/world-cup/superlative claims. Only one source was established in this batch, below the two-source publication minimum.

10-14.title: Mogadishu truck bombing
10-14.description: A truck bombing devastated Mogadishu's Zoobe intersection on October 14, 2017. The Zobe Rescue Committee later reported 587 deaths, but a UN monitoring report cites 582 and also notes a separate 587 count. The final toll and scope of the day's separate explosions need reconciliation.

review.note: Hiiraan's March 5 report attributes 587 to the Zobe Rescue Committee of volunteers and officials, not a parliamentary committee. Its final report was released March 4, increasing December's 512. The UN monitoring report gives as many as 582 in its main text and notes ACLED's 587, an unresolved discrepancy. Also distinguish the principal truck blast from the second explosion before assigning a combined toll. Original Hiiraan URL failed to open; an indexed rendering supplied the article text.

sources.name: Hiiraan Online report, accessible archived rendering
UN Somalia Monitoring Group report S/2018/1002

10-17.title: End of the Raqqa campaign declared
10-17.description: The SDF and US-led coalition operation to capture Raqqa from Islamic State was declared complete on October 17, 2017. A later Amnesty International and Airwars investigation reported more than 1,600 civilians killed by coalition air and artillery strikes during the June-October campaign. That figure is not an all-perpetrator battle total.

review.note: The operation was declared complete October 17 after beginning June 6. Amnesty/Airwars' later investigation reports more than 1,600 civilian deaths from coalition air and artillery strikes, not a 1,300-1,600 airstrike-only range. That source-specific count does not establish the original 1,800 all-perpetrator battle total or reconcile the several local-monitor totals. Keep core toll unresolved; do not create a synthetic midpoint across differently scoped estimates.

10-20.title: Daping coal mine gas explosion
10-20.description: A gas explosion at the Daping coal mine near Xinmi in Henan Province on October 20, 2004, killed 148 miners.

10-20.title: Typhoon Tokage
10-20.description: Typhoon Tokage crossed Japan on October 20, 2004, bringing destructive rain, floods and landslides. Official records list 95 deaths and three missing. It was the tenth typhoon to make landfall in Japan that year.
sources: Japan Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism

10-21.title: Haiti cholera outbreak confirmed
10-21.description: Haiti's National Public Health Laboratory confirmed a cholera outbreak on October 21, 2010. The epidemic spread nationwide. PAHO reported more than 820,000 cases and 9,792 deaths in the outbreak that began in October 2010 and continued into 2019; these are cumulative reported figures, not deaths on the confirmation date.

10-23.title: Moscow theater siege (Nord-Ost)
10-23.description: Chechen militants seized the Dubrovka theater in Moscow on October 23, taking more than 900 hostages. Russian security forces pumped an incapacitating gas into the building on October 26; at least 130 hostages died, most of them from the gas.

review.note: Dates, more than 900 hostages and gas-related deaths are supported. ECHR case material and HRW record 129 while later summaries give 130 or higher; final official 130 and the claimed lower-bound wording need reconciliation, not averaging.

10-23.title: Niigata Chuetsu earthquake
10-23.description: The October 23, 2004, Niigata Chuetsu earthquake and subsequent activity caused 68 deaths and 4,805 injuries. JMA gives magnitude 6.8 on its scale. Some 3,175 homes were destroyed and peak evacuation exceeded 100,000 people.

10-23.title: Van earthquake
10-23.description: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck eastern Turkey near the city of Van on October 23, 2011, collapsing poorly constructed masonry and adobe buildings, particularly in the town of Ercis. It killed 604 people, injured about 4,152, and left roughly 60,000 people homeless, with 11,232 buildings damaged. A magnitude 5.7 aftershock on November 9 killed about 40 additional people, bringing the earthquake sequence's combined toll to approximately 644.
sources: AFAD (Disaster and Emergency Management Presidency of Turkey)

review.note: AFAD gives 644 deaths and 1,966 injured across October 23 and November 9. Existing 4,152 injuries and precise 604/40 split need reconciliation. Keep single-earthquake versus sequence scope explicit; cannot certify the full record from combined totals. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

10-23.title: Siege of Marawi ends
10-23.description: Fighting between Philippine forces and Islamic State-aligned militants in Marawi began on May 23, 2017. The government declared the city liberated on October 17 and announced the end of combat operations on October 23. Published casualty breakdowns differ in their inclusion of civilians who died of illness.

review.note: October 23 is the declared end of combat operations; the separate liberation announcement was October 17. The original 1,233 sums 978 militants, 168 government personnel and 87 civilians; tertiary reporting says 40 of those civilians died of illness. The Army-hosted clipping repeats some later numbers but an authoritative reconciled total and direct/indirect scope were not established; the presidential briefing failed to open. Remove the inaccurate only-Muslim-majority-city claim and other ancillary rankings/costs. The exact total remains unresolved.

sources.name: Philippine Presidential Communications Office, October 27 briefing

10-24.title: Quetta police training college attack
10-24.description: Attackers stormed the police training college near Quetta late on October 24, 2016. Lashkar-e-Jhangvi claimed collaboration with Islamic State in the attack. Published victim counts range above the initially reported 61.

review.note: The Tribune supports the October 24 attack and early 61/165 count. Later Dawn gives 64 including two non-cadet personnel. Australia's listing gives at least 62 and notes LeJ claimed collaboration with Islamic State. The original exact total is not reconciled. Remove the false deadliest-since-2014 ranking: the Lahore Easter bombing in 2016 was deadlier.

10-25.title: Baghdad Justice Ministry Bombings
10-25.description: On October 25, 2009, two suicide car bombs exploded in quick succession near the Iraqi Ministry of Justice and the Baghdad Provincial Council building, killing at least 155 people and wounding more than 500. Victims included about two dozen children riding a bus near the Justice Ministry daycare. The Islamic State of Iraq, an al-Qaeda-linked group, claimed responsibility. It was Iraq's deadliest attack in more than two years.

10-25.title: Mentawai Islands earthquake and tsunami
10-25.description: A magnitude 7.7-7.8 earthquake struck beneath the Indian Ocean off the Mentawai Islands, west of Sumatra, Indonesia, on October 25, 2010, generating tsunami waves up to 3 meters that devastated low-lying coastal villages. The Indonesian disaster management agency and IFRC recorded 452 people dead and 76 missing, with nearly 15,000 displaced. The disaster struck the same week as the Mount Merapi eruption, and both events combined killed over 700 people, with many of the tsunami victims never recovered from the sea.

review.note: Research documents 3-9 m runup, contradicting a 3 m maximum. IFRC final operational report contains 500 deaths, not 452/76; table snapshots are not necessarily final official mortality. Need reconciled official toll and tsunami-height definition before full replacement.

10-25.title: Lewiston mass shooting
10-25.description: An Army reservist killed 18 people and injured 13 at a bowling alley and a bar in Lewiston, Maine, on October 25, 2023. He was found dead after a two-day search; investigators said he died by suicide. A state commission later found that local law enforcement and the Army Reserve missed opportunities to intervene before the attacks.

10-26.title: Mount Merapi eruption
10-26.description: Mount Merapi in central Java began a series of violent eruptions on October 26, 2010, with major eruptions continuing through November 5, including a powerful blast that killed its spiritual guardian Mbah Maridjan and overwhelmed emergency shelters. The final toll recorded 273 deaths, 176 from pyroclastic flows on the spot and 97 from related causes after hospitalization, with 577 people injured and up to 300,000 displaced across Central Java and Yogyakarta. It was the volcano's most powerful eruption in over a century, its eruptive activity peaking in early November.

review.note: 273 should not be described as final: later reporting gives 347, while other summaries give 353. Mbah Maridjan died during the initial October 26 eruption, not the November 5 peak implied by the sentence. IFRC table uses earlier dated snapshots. Exact final official scope remains unresolved.

10-26.title: Hindu Kush earthquake
10-26.description: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck Afghanistan's Hindu Kush on October 26, 2015. Reports recorded 280 deaths in Pakistan and 115 in Afghanistan, with widespread damage across both countries. A consistent all-country total remains to be established.

review.note: USGS confirms magnitude7.5 at09:09UTC October26; primary reports support280 Pakistan and115 Afghanistan. Four India deaths and exact399 total not independently established. Do not silently certify whole regional sum.

10-27.title: Pittsburgh synagogue shooting
10-27.description: An antisemitic gunman attacked worshippers at Pittsburgh's Tree of Life synagogue on October 27, 2018, killing 11 people from three congregations during Shabbat services. Six others, including four police officers, were wounded. It was the deadliest antisemitic attack in United States history.

10-28.title: Balochistan earthquake
10-28.description: A magnitude-6.4 earthquake struck Balochistan on October 28, 2008 UTC, in the early morning of October 29 locally, severely damaging villages in the Ziarat area. IFRC reporting recorded 166 deaths and hundreds of injuries; other published death totals differ.

review.note: The first destructive magnitude-6.4 shock was October 28 at 23:09 UTC, October 29 locally; another large shock occurred October 29 UTC. Propose October 28 for the first shock. IFRC's initial appeal update and later Pakistan plan report 166 deaths, whereas the original calls 215 final and inconsistently says official reports had reached 236. Those alternative totals are not reconciled. IFRC's roughly 122,000 refers to people affected, not all homeless. Remove that conflation and the unsupported failed-appeal story. The ASC event page was indexed but could not be opened; the exact UTC time is also given in the secondary earthquake record.

sources.name: IFRC: Pakistan earthquake appeal update MDRPK00201
Amateur Seismic Centre: October 28, 2008 Balochistan earthquake
Wikipedia: 2008 Ziarat earthquakes, UTC event times

10-28.title: Peshawar Meena Bazaar Bombing
10-28.description: On October 28, 2009, a car bomb exploded in the Meena Bazaar, a women's market in Peshawar, killing approximately 110-120 people — about 70 of them women and children — and injuring more than 200. The blast, among the deadliest attacks in Peshawar's history, destroyed several buildings and trapped many victims in rubble. Pakistani Taliban-linked militants were suspected. The bombing came amid a surge of militant attacks across Pakistan's northwest.

review.note: Dawn's October 30 report gives 117; later retrospective says 137. The existing 112 and demographic split require reconciliation, not certification.

10-28.title: Lion Air Flight 610 crash
10-28.description: Lion Air Flight 610, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 travelling from Jakarta to Pangkal Pinang, crashed into the Java Sea about 13 minutes after takeoff, killing all 189 aboard. It was early October 29, 2018 locally, still October 28 UTC. Investigators documented technical problems on preceding flights.

10-29.title: Delhi serial bombings
10-29.description: Three bombs struck the Paharganj and Sarojini Nagar markets and a bus in the Govindpuri/Kalkaji area of Delhi on October 29, 2005, shortly before Diwali. Later reporting differs on the final death and injury totals.

review.note: PTI court coverage supports 67 deaths/over 225 injured, but other court reporting gives 62 and over 100; TOI gives 67/105. Original half-hour timing also conflicts with 17:30 to18:05 reporting. Core toll conflict is unresolved; remove unsupported tight timing.

10-29.title: Mogadishu twin vehicle bombings
10-29.description: Two vehicle bombs exploded near Somalia's Education Ministry in Mogadishu on October 29, 2022. On November 1 the health minister reported 121 deaths, 333 injuries and ten people missing. Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility. An official told VOA that the second device was carried by a motorcycle pulling a trailer.

10-29.title: Seoul Halloween crowd crush (Itaewon)
10-29.description: A crowd crush in a narrow, sloping alley in Seoul's Itaewon district during Halloween celebrations on October 29, 2022 killed 159 people and injured 196. Police subsequently referred 23 officials to prosecutors over alleged failures in prevention and emergency response.

10-29.title: Valencia Flash Floods (DANA)
10-29.description: Extreme rainfall on October 29, 2024 caused flash floods in eastern Spain, especially Valencia province. By the first anniversary, 229 deaths were attributed to the disaster in Valencia and 237 across Spain. The numeric toll in this entry is Valencia's, not the nationwide total.

10-31.title: Our Lady of Salvation church siege
10-31.description: Gunmen from the Islamic State of Iraq stormed Our Lady of Salvation, a Syriac Catholic church in Baghdad, during Sunday Mass on October 31, 2010, taking more than 100 worshippers hostage before Iraqi security forces stormed the building. The siege killed 58 people, including 44 worshippers, two priests, seven security personnel, and five attackers, and wounded more than 70. It was the deadliest attack on Iraq's Christian community since the 2003 invasion and prompted an exodus of Iraqi Christians, with many families fleeing the country.

review.note: Siege date/location corroborated; accounts give incompatible casualty breakdowns. Existing 58 includes five attackers, whereas other reports present 58 victims. Need original final victim list/official statement; do not merge incompatible categories. Exodus causality is not established.

10-31.title: Metrojet Flight 9268 bombing
10-31.description: Metrojet Flight 9268 broke up over Egypt's Sinai Peninsula on October 31, 2015, killing all 224 people aboard the Sharm el-Sheikh-Saint Petersburg flight. Islamic State claimed responsibility. Russian authorities concluded a bomb destroyed the aircraft, and Egypt's president later acknowledged terrorism caused the crash.

10-31.title: Tezgam train fire
10-31.description: The Karachi-to-Rawalpindi Tezgam Express caught fire near Rahim Yar Khan at about 06:30 local time on October 31, 2019. Radio Pakistan reported 74 deaths that day. Later inquiry reporting identified a possible electrical short circuit followed by cylinder explosions.

11-02.title: Kabul University attack
11-02.description: On 2 November 2020, three gunmen from Islamic State Khorasan Province stormed Kabul University during an Iranian book fair, killing 32 people and wounding more than 50 in a siege that lasted several hours. The attackers, killed by security forces, brought the total death count including themselves to 35. The attack targeted students and academics and was one of the deadliest attacks on a university in Afghanistan's recent history.

review.note: Date and IS attack supported. Sources differ between 22 initially, 35 students/professors in later reporting, and secondary 32 victims plus three attackers. Do not infer 32 by subtracting attackers from a source saying 35 students/professors. Iranian book-fair context and over-50 injured require corroboration.

11-03.title: Hurricane Eta
11-03.description: Hurricane Eta made landfall near Puerto Cabezas, Nicaragua on 3 November 2020 as a Category 4 hurricane, then stalled over Central America for two days, triggering catastrophic flash floods and landslides across the region. At least 189 people died, including 74 in Honduras, 60 in Guatemala and 19 in Panama, with more than 100 missing. Eta was followed within two weeks by Hurricane Iota, which compounded the destruction in Honduras and Nicaragua.

review.note: Hurricane/date identity established; retrieved summaries disagree internally between at least 175 and 189. Need final NHC table and national figures to reconcile missing, presumed dead and Eta-versus-Iota totals; 74 Honduras/60 Guatemala/19 Panama breakdown not established.

11-03.title: Jajarkot earthquake
11-03.description: An earthquake struck western Nepal at 23:47 local time, 18:02 UTC, on November 3, 2023. Nepal's health ministry review records 154 deaths across Jajarkot and Rukum West, with extensive damage to homes. Research describes the earthquake as moment magnitude 5.7, corresponding to a reported local magnitude of 6.4.
sources: Nepal Ministry of Health and Population

11-05.title: Fort Hood Shooting
11-05.description: On November 5, 2009, Army psychiatrist Major Nidal Hasan opened fire at the Soldier Readiness Processing Center at Fort Hood, Texas, killing 13 people — 12 soldiers and one civilian — and wounding more than 30. Hasan, a US Army officer, was shot by responding police and survived. It was the deadliest mass shooting on a US military base; Hasan was convicted in 2013 of 13 counts of premeditated murder.

11-05.title: Sutherland Springs church shooting
11-05.description: A gunman attacked First Baptist Church in Sutherland Springs, Texas, on November 5, 2017. Authorities count 26 victims, including the unborn child of a pregnant woman who was killed, and 22 injured. The victim toll excludes the attacker.
sources: US Department of Justice, event date

11-06.title: Baghlan bombing
11-06.description: A bombing targeted a parliamentary delegation visiting a sugar factory in Baghlan on November 6, 2007. Many children and several lawmakers died. UN reporting found that police and bodyguard gunfire after the explosion added to the casualties; the exact number killed by each cause was not established.

review.note: UNAMA's contemporaneous record and later Secretary-General report distinguish bombing deaths from subsequent police/bodyguard gunfire and use roughly70, not79. Exact split and final total remain uncertain; do not assign all deaths to bomber. UN investigation statements also differed before later reporting.

11-07.title: Second Battle of Fallujah
11-07.description: US-led forces launched an offensive against insurgents in Fallujah in November 2004. Civilian and combatant death estimates vary, and available civilian counts cover different areas and periods. Iraq Body Count records 581-670 civilian deaths in nine neighborhoods.
sources: International Committee of the Red Cross

review.note: Numeric 1,000 is not a defensible overall count when the prose itself gives larger combatant losses before civilians. IBC's 581-670 covers nine neighborhoods, not a complete battle census; the reported 800 was an anonymous unofficial Red Cross estimate, not a verified ICRC institutional total. Need consistent full-battle population and interval.

11-07.title: Pétion-Ville school collapse (Collège La Promesse Évangélique)
11-07.description: The College La Promesse Evangelique school in Petion-Ville collapsed during classes on November 7, 2008. An Inter Press Service report a year later put the death toll at 97, with more than 100 people injured. Earlier reports gave lower totals while rescue and recovery work continued.
sources: IFRC: Haiti school collapse information bulletin 1
AFP via La Nacion: November 10 toll update
Inter Press Service via Global Issues: one-year retrospective

11-07.title: Typhoon Haiyan
11-07.description: Typhoon Haiyan, known locally as Yolanda, first made landfall near Guiuan in the Philippines at 20:40 UTC on November 7, 2013, or November 8 locally. Its winds and storm surges devastated central Philippine communities. Later reports put the Philippine death toll at approximately 6,300.

11-08.title: Camp Fire wildfire
11-08.description: The Camp Fire began in Butte County, California, on November 8, 2018 and devastated Paradise and nearby communities. It killed 85 people, burned 153,336 acres and destroyed 18,804 structures.

11-09.title: Amman hotel bombings
11-09.description: Three suicide bombers attacked the lobbies of the Grand Hyatt, Radisson SAS and Days Inn hotels in Amman, Jordan, killing 60 people and injuring more than 100, including victims at a wedding reception in the Radisson. Al-Qaeda in Iraq claimed responsibility for the attacks.

11-09.title: Shizong coal mine gas outburst
11-09.description: A coal and gas outburst occurred at Sizhuang coal mine in Shizong County, Yunnan, at 6:19 a.m. local time on November 10, 2011 (November 9 UTC). The official investigation recorded 43 deaths and identified illegal production and serious safety failures.

11-09.title: Mai Kadra massacre
11-09.description: On 9-10 November 2020, in the first days of the Tigray War, hundreds of Amhara civilians were killed in house-to-house raids in the town of Mai Kadra near the Sudanese border. Estimates of the death toll ranged from hundreds to more than 1,100, with a Reuters investigation confirming at least 767 deaths; Amnesty International reported that hundreds were killed, likely by local Tigrayan security forces, police and militias aligned with the TPLF. The massacre was the first documented mass atrocity of the Tigray conflict.

review.note: Secondary summaries cite Reuters' 767 but direct Reuters investigation was not retrieved. Must distinguish November 9 killings of Amhara civilians from subsequent retaliatory killings of Tigrayans. Original attribution to Amnesty and 1,100 upper estimate require source-specific scope; not independently verified.

11-11.title: Typhoon Vamco (Ulysses)
11-11.description: Typhoon Vamco, known locally as Ulysses, made landfall in Quezon province on 11 November 2020 as the third typhoon to strike the Philippines in two weeks. The storm caused severe flooding in Metro Manila and Cagayan Valley, killing 102 people with 10 more missing, according to the Philippine disaster agency. More than a million people were displaced, and the flooding in Cagayan was described as the worst in decades.
sources: NDRRMC (Philippines National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council)

review.note: November 11 Philippine landfall supported. Secondary accounts conflict between 102 dead/10 missing, 98/19 and 101/10 at different dates. Need NDRRMC final report and distinguish affected from displaced; one million displaced is not established.

11-12.title: Beirut suicide bombings
11-12.description: Two suicide bombings struck the crowded Bourj el-Barajneh area in Beirut's southern suburbs on November 12, 2015. At least 43 people were reported killed and more than 240 wounded. Islamic State claimed responsibility.

11-12.title: Iran-Iraq earthquake
11-12.description: A magnitude 7.3 earthquake struck near the Iran-Iraq border on November 12, 2017. It killed approximately 630 people and caused severe damage, particularly around Sarpol-e Zahab in Iran. The numeric toll is approximate.

11-13.title: Paris Attacks
11-13.description: Coordinated shootings and suicide bombings struck Paris and Saint-Denis on November 13, 2015, including the Bataclan, restaurants and Stade de France. They killed 130 people in the immediate attacks and injured more than 400. France's later official toll is 132, including two survivors who subsequently died by suicide.

11-14.title: Gaza conflict — Operation Pillar of Defense
11-14.description: Israel's Operation Pillar of Defense began on November 14, 2012, with an airstrike that killed Hamas military leader Ahmed Jabari amid escalating hostilities. A UN Human Rights Council report recorded 174 Palestinian deaths during the crisis, including 107 civilians, and six Israeli deaths. A ceasefire took effect on November 21. The 180 figure combines both sides over the operation.

11-14.title: Piatra Neamț hospital fire
11-14.description: A fire broke out in the COVID-19 intensive-care unit of Piatra Neamt Emergency Hospital in Romania on November 14, 2020. Ten patients died, and officials initially reported seven people critically injured, including a doctor. Firefighters reported extinguishing the blaze in about 25 minutes.

11-15.title: Podi Coal Mine Explosion
11-15.description: A gas explosion at the Podi coal mine in Jiaocheng County, Shanxi, on November 15, 2001 killed 33 people. A subsequent investigation found that ventilation failures allowed gas to accumulate and that the mine had resumed production without the required authorization.

11-15.title: Istanbul bombings
11-15.description: Truck bombings targeted two Istanbul synagogues on November 15, 2003, and the British consulate and HSBC offices on November 20. The attacks were linked to al-Qaeda. Reported death totals vary, including whether the four bombers are counted.

review.note: Two attack dates are established, but later totals differ: BBC summary 58; detailed reference 59 including four bombers; original 57 not reconciled. Remove the unqualified all-time Turkish superlative. Count covers both November 15 and 20, not only the indexed date.

11-15.title: Cyclone Sidr
11-15.description: Cyclone Sidr struck Bangladesh on November 15, 2007, causing destructive winds and coastal flooding. Officially reported death counts changed between assessments. Early fears that the toll might reach 15,000 were estimates, not confirmed fatalities.

review.note: 3,447 is a November20 provisional official count, later repeated by GFDRR; ADRC records3,363 onDecember29 and World Bank later3,406.15,000 was a feared early estimate, not a confirmed alternative tally. Date secure; final reported deaths/missing reconciliation remains needed.

11-18.title: Zasyadko mine explosion
11-18.description: A methane explosion at the Zasyadko coal mine in Donetsk on November 18, 2007, killed 101 miners, including one who died later in hospital. There were 457 miners underground when the explosion occurred. Later explosions in December are not included in this toll.

11-19.title: Pike River Mine disaster
11-19.description: A methane explosion at the Pike River coal mine on the South Island of New Zealand on November 19, 2010 trapped 29 miners, all of whom were declared dead after a series of further explosions prevented rescue attempts and a subsequent fire forced the mine to be sealed. The victims' bodies were never recovered. A royal commission of inquiry found the explosion was preventable and identified systemic failures in mine management, gas monitoring, and safety culture, prompting a major overhaul of New Zealand's mining safety legislation.

11-20.title: Xinxing Coal Mine Explosion
11-20.description: A gas explosion struck the Xinxing Coal Mine in Hegang, Heilongjiang, at about 2:30 a.m. local time on November 21, 2009 (November 20 UTC), while 528 miners were underground. The subsequent government investigation recorded 108 deaths and 133 injuries and identified serious safety and regulatory failures.

11-23.title: Sadr City bombings
11-23.description: Car bombs and mortar attacks struck Baghdad's Sadr City on the afternoon of November 23, 2006. Iraq Body Count records 215 deaths in the attacks.

11-23.title: Maguindanao Massacre
11-23.description: On November 23, 2009, armed men linked to the Ampatuan clan massacred 58 people in Maguindanao, Philippines, in an attack associated with the filing of Esmael Mangudadatu's gubernatorial candidacy. The victims included 32 journalists and media workers. CPJ describes it as the deadliest single attack on the press.

11-24.title: Tazreen Fashion factory fire
11-24.description: A fire at Tazreen Fashions near Dhaka, Bangladesh, on November 24, 2012, killed 112 workers according to the ILO. Many other workers were injured. The disaster prompted a tripartite fire-safety action plan for Bangladesh's garment sector.

11-24.title: Bir al-Abed mosque attack, Egypt
11-24.location: Al-Rawda near Bir al-Abed, North Sinai, Egypt
11-24.description: Armed attackers struck al-Rawda mosque near Bir al-Abed in North Sinai during Friday prayers on November 24, 2017. Later reports put the death toll at 311. The mosque is associated with a Sufi community.
sources: Tahrir Institute for Middle East Policy

11-25.title: Qala-i-Jangi Fortress Uprising
11-25.description: Taliban and al-Qaeda prisoners revolted at the Qala-i-Jangi fortress near Mazar-i-Sharif, triggering a six-day battle in which up to 400 prisoners, about 73 Northern Alliance fighters, and CIA officer Johnny Spann — the first American killed in combat in the war — died. Only 86 of the more than 400 prisoners survived, including American Taliban fighter John Walker Lindh.

review.note: 400 was an upper-end prisoner estimate, not a verified total including Northern Alliance and US deaths. Accounts differ on duration and fighter losses; 86 survivors is reported. A single precise aggregate cannot be inferred from these incompatible estimates.

11-26.title: Mumbai attacks (26/11)
11-26.description: Ten Lashkar-e-Taiba attackers carried out coordinated attacks in Mumbai from November 26 to 29, 2008. The attacks killed 166 victims and injured 304 people. Nine attackers were killed during the operation, while Ajmal Kasab was captured alive.
sources: Bureau of Police Research and Development: Mumbai attack review
FBI: role and lessons learned in the Mumbai investigation

11-27.title: Chenjiashan coal mine gas explosion
11-27.description: A gas explosion at Chenjiashan coal mine near Tongchuan, Shaanxi, killed 166 miners. It occurred at about 07:10 on November 28, 2004, local time, November 27 UTC. Fire and toxic gases hampered rescue and recovery.

11-27.title: Dongfeng coal mine explosion
11-27.description: A coal-dust explosion at Dongfeng coal mine in Qitaihe, Heilongjiang, on November 27, 2005, killed 171 people and injured 48, according to the official investigation. The death toll included workers underground and at the surface.

11-27.title: Nevsky Express Bombing
11-27.description: On the night of November 27, 2009, a bomb equivalent to roughly 7 kg of TNT derailed the Nevsky Express train traveling from Moscow to St. Petersburg near Bologoye, killing 28 people and injuring about 90. Russian authorities declared the derailment a terrorist attack, blaming militants from the North Caucasus. It was the second bombing on the line, following an explosion in August 2007 that injured dozens.

review.note: Date, route, explosive cause and approximately 7 kg TNT corroborated. Reports give preliminary 25 then 26 and more than 100 wounded; final 28 and about 90 injuries not established by these sources. Do not substitute preliminary toll.

11-28.title: Kano Central Mosque Attack
11-28.description: Bombers and gunmen attacked Kano's Central Mosque during Friday prayers on November 28, 2014. Contemporary emergency reports estimated about 120 deaths, although early hospital counts were lower. Boko Haram was widely suspected of responsibility.

review.note: Friday November 28 prayer-time attack supported; 120 was an emergency-source estimate while hospitals reported over 80. Attribute the approximate toll and do not assert a definitive claim of responsibility. The competing hospital and emergency-source figures are not a reconciled final toll; the approximate wording alone does not resolve the numeric field.

11-28.title: Koshebe massacre
11-28.description: On 28 November 2020, gunmen believed to be Boko Haram fighters attacked farmers harvesting rice fields near the village of Koshebe in Borno State, northeastern Nigeria. The United Nations reported that as many as 110 civilians and peasant farmers were killed, six were wounded and about 15 women were kidnapped. The attack, which followed a dispute with farmers who had disarmed a Boko Haram gunman the previous day, was among the deadliest attacks on civilians in Nigeria during 2020.

review.note: UN's initial 110 figure was amended to tens. The primary statement confirms November 28 attack and abductions, not precise totals. Six injured, 15 women abducted and the alleged precipitating dispute remain unestablished; no defensible exact replacement toll.

11-30.title: Philippines typhoon series and Quezon floods
11-30.description: Several tropical cyclones caused severe flooding and landslides in the Philippines in November and early December 2004. A December WHO report recorded 1,060 deaths and 559 missing. Winnie caused much of the destruction, including in Quezon Province.

review.note: WHO release reproduced by ScienceDaily gives 1,060 dead and 559 missing, not 566, as a December snapshot. NASA establishes several storms over November-December and Winnie on November 29. November 30 is not a substantiated onset for the series, and Quezon alone does not describe its total scope.

11-30.title: Super Typhoon Durian and Mayon mudflows
11-30.description: Typhoon Durian, known locally as Reming, struck the Philippines on November 30, 2006. Rain triggered destructive mudflows around Mayon Volcano. The Philippine disaster agency's report records 734 deaths and separately lists 762 people missing; the recorded death toll does not add the missing.

12-01.title: Ben Yehuda Street Bombings
12-01.description: Two suicide bombers struck the Ben Yehuda pedestrian area in Jerusalem on 1 December 2001, followed by a car bomb. Eleven people were killed and more than 130 injured. Hamas claimed responsibility.

12-01.title: Chennai floods
12-01.description: Repeated northeast-monsoon rains flooded Chennai and other parts of Tamil Nadu in November-December 2015. Official and research accounts give differing death totals for the city, state and wider region. The final severe flooding followed early-December rain, but losses accumulated over a longer period.

review.note: 500 is broader South India estimate,422 appears in NIDM,470 is statewide monsoon count. December1 does not represent the whole November-December episode. Resolve period and geography before assigning a count/date. NGO CAG differs from Comptroller and Auditor General.

sources.name: NITI Aayog, Tamil Nadu flood review
Citizen consumer and civic Action Group, assessment

12-02.title: Haifa Bus 16 Bombing
12-02.description: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked bus 16 in Haifa on 2 December 2001, killing 15 other people and wounding about 40. The attack followed the previous night's bombings in Jerusalem.

12-02.title: San Bernardino shooting
12-02.description: Two attackers opened fire at a San Bernardino County employee gathering at the Inland Regional Center on December 2, 2015, killing 14 people and injuring 22 according to the county's retrospective. The FBI classified it as terrorism. Both attackers were killed in a later confrontation with police.

12-03.title: Typhoon Bopha (Pablo)
12-03.description: Typhoon Bopha, the strongest storm ever recorded to strike the Philippines at that time of year, made landfall on Mindanao late on 3 December / early 4 December 2012 as a Category 5-equivalent super typhoon. The NDRRMC's final toll was 1,901 dead, with widespread flash floods and landslides in Davao Oriental and Compostela Valley, where mudslides buried villages, including in New Bataan.

review.note: NASA gives 04:45 December 4 local, i.e. December 3 UTC, and strongest recorded in Mindanao, not strongest nationwide for the season. 1,901 combines commonly reported 1,067 dead and 834 missing rather than 1,901 confirmed dead. ADRC full-page open failed (502); obtain final NDRRMC table before replacing toll.

12-04.title: Lame Horse Nightclub Fire
12-04.description: A fire at the Lame Horse nightclub in Perm began early on December 5, 2009 local time, or December 4 UTC, after indoor pyrotechnics ignited ceiling material. Court reporting records 156 deaths.

12-09.title: Whakaari/White Island eruption
12-09.location: Whakaari/White Island, Bay of Plenty, New Zealand
12-09.description: Whakaari/White Island erupted in New Zealand's Bay of Plenty on December 9, 2019, while visitors and guides were on the island. Twenty-two people died and 25 were injured, most critically. Two victims' bodies were not recovered.

12-10.title: Mayfield tornado outbreak
12-10.description: A historic tornado outbreak spawned an EF4 tornado that leveled the town of Mayfield, Kentucky, and caused damage across six states from Arkansas to Ohio during the night of December 10-11. At least 89 people were killed, most of them in Kentucky, where it was the deadliest tornado event in the state's history, with deaths also reported in Tennessee and elsewhere.

review.note: NWS assessment supports 89 direct tornado deaths and 71 tornadoes across eight states, not six. 89 is entire-outbreak toll, not one Mayfield tornado. Need UTC beginning of chosen whole-outbreak scope; Mayfield's late December 10 local impact is December 11 UTC.

12-11.title: Algiers bombings
12-11.description: Two car bombs struck Algiers on December 11, 2007, near the Constitutional Court and UN offices. The United Nations confirms that 17 of its staff were killed. Published overall death counts differ.

review.note: UN confirms17 staff andDecember11; anniversary message says20minutes between bombs, not10.37 is later official total, while secondary41 and early hospital67 differ. Exact overall toll cannot be established from UN staff-only memorial; remove unsupported exact interval.

12-13.title: Indian Parliament Attack
12-13.description: Five gunmen attacked India's Parliament complex in New Delhi on 13 December 2001. Eight security personnel and a gardener were killed, and all five attackers were shot dead. Indian authorities attributed the attack to Pakistan-based militant groups.

12-14.title: Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting
12-14.description: On December 14, 2012, a gunman killed his mother at home and then killed 20 children and six adult staff members at Sandy Hook Elementary School in Newtown, Connecticut. There were 27 murdered victims across the two sites. The attacker also died by suicide and is not included in that victim count.

12-15.title: Outbreak of the South Sudanese Civil War
12-15.description: Fighting began between military factions in Juba on December 15, 2013, and spread into South Sudan's civil war. By December 26, UNMISS estimated about 1,000 deaths in Juba, a preliminary count rather than the eventual nationwide war toll.

review.note: December 15 onset is established. 1,000 was a preliminary estimate, with Amnesty specifying UNMISS's Juba estimate by December 26. Original wording risks treating this as exact national deaths or onset-day deaths. Precise onset UTC time not established.

12-16.title: Typhoon Washi (Sendong) flash floods
12-16.location: Cagayan de Oro and Iligan, Philippines
12-16.description: Tropical Storm Washi (locally named Sendong) made landfall on Mindanao on the night of December 16-17, 2011, dumping up to 20 cm of rain in 24 hours and triggering flash floods that swept away thousands of sleeping residents in the riverside cities of Cagayan de Oro and Iligan. The Philippines' NDRRMC final count recorded 1,268 fatalities, 181 missing and 6,071 injured, with nearly 700,000 people affected and more than 11,000 homes destroyed. It was the deadliest tropical cyclone to hit Mindanao in recorded history.

review.note: Final-report transcription supports 1,268/181/6,071. Washi was a tropical storm, not a typhoon; midnight-local flood deaths fall on December 16 UTC. All-time Mindanao superlative, full affected count and final official source version need reconciliation.

12-16.title: Army Public School Attack, Peshawar
12-16.description: Pakistani Taliban gunmen attacked the Army Public School in Peshawar on December 16, 2014, killing students and staff. The initial reported toll of 141 rose in subsequent accounts; a reconciled final count and breakdown are needed before treating one figure as definitive.

review.note: 141 was initial; later reports give 148 and 150, with differing child counts. Seven attackers reported initially, not nine; other retrospective accounts give six. Exact final victim/perpetrator totals require reconciliation. Morning time is December 16 UTC.

12-16.title: Super Typhoon Rai
12-16.description: Typhoon Rai, known in the Philippines as Odette, struck the country on December 16, 2021, causing destructive winds, flooding and displacement. Philippine disaster reporting recorded 405 reported deaths. Initial situation reports included fatalities still undergoing validation.

12-18.title: Jishishan earthquake
12-18.description: An earthquake struck Jishishan County in Gansu, China, at 23:59 local time, 15:59 UTC, on December 18, 2023. Chinese authorities measured surface-wave magnitude 6.2. The earthquake killed 151 people across Gansu and Qinghai and injured nearly 1,000.

12-21.title: Prague university shooting
12-21.description: A student attacked Charles University's Faculty of Arts in Prague on December 21, 2023, killing 14 people and injuring 25 before dying by suicide. Police linked him to his father's killing earlier that day and to the murders of a man and infant six days earlier. Those three earlier victims are not included in this university-attack toll.

12-23.title: Damascus twin suicide bombings
12-23.description: Two car bombs struck security-service compounds in Damascus on December 23, 2011. Syrian authorities reported 44 deaths and 166 injuries. The government blamed Islamist militants; opposition representatives denied involvement and alleged government responsibility. The casualty composition and perpetrators were disputed.

12-24.title: Sudan famine confirmed in North Darfur camps
12-24.description: On December 24, 2024, FAO, WFP and UNICEF reported the IPC Famine Review Committee's finding of famine in at least five assessed areas, including three North Darfur displacement camps and resident and displaced populations in the Western Nuba Mountains. The assessment covered October-November 2024 and projected further spread.

review.note: The five-area finding was announced December 24, 2024 and assessed October-November conditions, with projections through May 2025. February 19 is not established as a new confirmation. Western Nuba coverage refers to residents and displaced people, not necessarily two named physical sites. A photographer's caption repeats 522,000 child malnutrition deaths attributed to the Sudan Doctors Union, but no underlying estimate, methods or authoritative corroboration was found. IPC people-in-Catastrophe figures are not deaths. The Sudan government also disputed the IPC process; its disagreement does not negate the independent famine classification. Retain in audit, not public canonical data.

12-25.title: Luoyang Dongdu commercial building fire
12-25.description: A fire caused by welding work spread through the Dongdu commercial building in Luoyang on 25 December 2000, killing 309 people. Smoke reached a crowded dance hall; investigators said the welders left without raising the alarm.
sources: French Ministry of Ecological Transition, ARIA

12-26.title: Bam earthquake
12-26.description: A magnitude 6.6 earthquake struck Bam and surrounding communities in southeastern Iran on December 26, 2003. It destroyed much of the city and killed tens of thousands. Published fatality totals differ; the World Bank's reconstruction report used approximately 26,000.

review.note: Magnitude 6.6 and December 26 UTC are supported. Fatality accounts conflict: World Bank about 26,000, Iranica 31,824-43,000, and the reference summary cites later 34,000 versus an earlier revised 26,271. Do not silently treat one precise figure as settled. The 1990 Iranian quake also makes 'deadliest in decades' unsafe.

12-26.title: Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami
12-26.description: The December 26, 2004, earthquake off northern Sumatra generated a devastating Indian Ocean tsunami. NOAA and UNESCO's 2024 summary records 227,899 people killed or missing and presumed dead in 15 countries, with about 1.7 million displaced.

12-27.title: Grozny government headquarters bombing
12-27.description: Suicide attackers drove explosive-laden vehicles into the Chechen government headquarters in Grozny on 27 December 2002. The reported victim toll was 83, excluding the attackers.

12-27.title: Assassination of Benazir Bhutto
12-27.description: Former Pakistani prime minister Benazir Bhutto was assassinated as she left a campaign event in Rawalpindi on December 27, 2007. The UN commission of inquiry records 24 other people killed and 91 injured in the attack, giving 25 victims including Bhutto.
sources: UN Commission of Inquiry via Refworld

12-27.title: Gaza War (Operation Cast Lead) begins
12-27.description: Israel began Operation Cast Lead with airstrikes in Gaza on December 27, 2008 and launched a ground invasion on January 3, 2009. The offensive continued until January 18. B'Tselem's later accounting recorded 1,391 Palestinian deaths and 13 Israeli deaths across the conflict; official Israeli and earlier published Palestinian totals differed.

review.note: The December 27 start and January 3 ground invasion are supported by the IDF chronology; the toll covers the whole offensive through January 18, not only the opening day. The original 1,400 numerically combines an older B'Tselem count of 1,387 Palestinians with 13 Israelis. B'Tselem subsequently revised its Palestinian count to 1,391 (1,404 combined), while other B'Tselem pages contain older 1,385/1,390 figures; Israel's official total of 1,166 Palestinians also differs in inclusion and classification. Preserve those contradictions: this batch does not certify one exact total or reconcile civilian/child definitions. Remove outdated subtotals, the unverified 40-at-headquarters detail and the compressed UN legal conclusion. Toll and geographic scope remain unresolved for integration.

sources.name: B'Tselem: September 2009 casualty release, with update notice
B'Tselem: Gaza Strip background and updated conflict totals
Israel Defense Forces: Operation Cast Lead chronology

12-27.title: Indonesia AirAsia Flight QZ8501 Crash
12-27.description: Indonesia AirAsia Flight QZ8501 crashed into the Java Sea on December 27, 2014 UTC, or the morning of December 28 locally, while flying from Surabaya to Singapore. All 162 aboard died. Investigators found that a recurring equipment fault and the crew's response led to loss of control and a stall.

12-28.title: Mogadishu truck bombing
12-28.description: On 28 December 2019, a truck bomb detonated at the Ex-Control Afgoye checkpoint on the outskirts of Mogadishu, followed by another blast at a bus station in the city, killing at least 85 people and injuring more than 140. The attack hit taxis, buses and minibuses collecting passengers at the checkpoint during rush hour, and al-Shabaab claimed responsibility. It was among the deadliest attacks in Mogadishu in years and targeted a route frequented by civilians travelling between the capital and surrounding towns.

review.note: 85 appears in later secondary totals. A second bus-station blast is not established and may conflate a different bombing. Need final reputable toll and responsibility statement.

12-29.title: Jeju Air Flight 2216 Crash
12-29.description: Jeju Air Flight 2216 from Bangkok made a gear-up landing at Muan International Airport on December 29, 2024, overran the runway and struck a concrete structure. Of 181 occupants, 179 died and two survived with serious injuries. The preliminary investigation documented bird-strike evidence but did not establish the complete cause.

12-30.title: Rizal Day bombings
12-30.description: Coordinated bombings struck five locations across Metro Manila on a national holiday, killing 22 people. The deadliest blast hit a crowded LRT train.

12-30.title: Aden airport attack
12-30.description: On 30 December 2020, explosions and gunfire hit Aden International Airport just as a plane carrying members of Yemen's newly formed unity government, including the prime minister and the Saudi ambassador, was landing from Riyadh. The attack killed 28 people and wounded 107, though none of the cabinet passengers were hurt. A UN investigation later found the Houthi movement responsible for the attack, which came as the Saudi-brokered power-sharing government returned to the interim capital.

review.note: Attack followed landing, rather than necessarily occurring during landing. UN missile analysis must not be reduced to unqualified attribution without checking confidence language. Early Reuters toll was 22; 28/107 later secondary tally and Saudi ambassador aboard require final evidence.

12-31.title: Israel–Hamas War: 2024 Death Toll in Gaza
12-31.description: During 2024, the Israel–Hamas war in the Gaza Strip continued with intense Israeli military operations and armed resistance, with the Gaza Ministry of Health reporting more than 45,600 Palestinians killed since October 2023 — roughly 25,000 of them during 2024 — while most of the territory's 2.1 million residents were repeatedly displaced and UN agencies warned of famine conditions and disease outbreaks. The conflict also involved continued rocket fire into Israel and expanding regional confrontation with Hezbollah and Iran.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

review.note: December 31 OCHA publication uses Gaza MoH data through December 30: 45,541 cumulative since October 7, 2023, not 45,600 deaths during 2024. Simple difference from the 21,822 end-2023 snapshot is 23,719 but changes to cumulative reporting are not necessarily deaths occurring within the year. Need actual occurrence-year accounting or explicitly repurpose to a cumulative snapshot, avoiding double counting record 113. Annual toll remains unresolved.

12-31.title: Russia–Ukraine War: 2024 Casualties
12-31.description: The Russia–Ukraine war entered its third year in 2024, with Russian offensives in eastern Ukraine, a Ukrainian incursion into Russia's Kursk region, and relentless artillery and drone strikes on cities including Kharkiv, Kyiv, and Odesa. Independent media documented more than 78,000 named Russian soldiers killed by December 2024 and estimated total military deaths on both sides at more than 100,000 during the year — making 2024 the war's deadliest — while the UN recorded about 1,300 civilian deaths in Ukraine in 2024 and more than 12,000 civilians killed since the February 2022 invasion.

review.note: UN initially documented 2,064 civilian deaths in 2024, later revised to 2,088, not about 1,300. Named Russian deaths are cumulative verified identifications, not all-side annual deaths. The exact 100,000 annual combined military total and deadliest-year assertion are not established; dynamic Mediazona data cannot be backdated to December 2024. December 31 is a reporting-period endpoint, not a one-day battle date.
